description:
PROBLEM
BuildDDxBinary and BuildDDxFizeauTestSeamBinary create process-lifetime binary directories shared through sync.Once. After ddx-b2702b9f moves both directories beneath configured execution scratch, cleanup must eventually reclaim abandoned directories without deleting one still owned by a long-running test process. The cleanup allowlist currently recognizes ddx-fixture-bin-* but not ddx-fizeau-testseam-bin-*; adding the missing prefix without ownership evidence would make directory age alone sufficient to delete a live process-owned binary directory.

ROOT CAUSE WITH FILE:LINE
cli/internal/testutils/fixture_repo.go:87-95 stores both built binary paths in process-wide sync.Once state, and cli/internal/testutils/fixture_repo.go:119-167 creates and publishes the two binary directories without a durable owner marker.
cli/internal/agent/execution_cleanup.go:26-46 includes ddx-fixture-bin-* in defaultExecutionCleanupScratchPrefixes but omits ddx-fizeau-testseam-bin-*.
cli/internal/agent/execution_cleanup.go:667-681 synthesizes ownership when cleanup.json is absent, while cli/internal/agent/execution_cleanup.go:728-755 removes an allowlisted directory after the age threshold when no liveness evidence preserves it.
cli/internal/agent/execution_cleanup.go:189-221 preserves a directory with live PID or lease evidence only when compatible metadata exists.
ddx-05e3d16b and ddx-1eb1ba93 establish the host-global trust and metadata-marked reclamation rules, but neither makes the fixture-binary producer emit process-lifetime ownership evidence.

PROPOSED FIX
Add a small lower-level scratch-owner marker contract that can be imported by both internal/testutils and internal/agent without an import cycle. The marker must record the resource kind, owner PID, creation time, and a process-start identity when the platform exposes one; marker writes must be atomic.
Have BuildDDxBinary and BuildDDxFizeauTestSeamBinary write the marker immediately after creating their directory and before caching or returning the binary path. If marker creation fails, remove the new directory and fail the build helper instead of publishing an unowned path.
Teach execution cleanup to recognize both ddx-fixture-bin-* and ddx-fizeau-testseam-bin-* through the owner-marker contract. Preserve an old directory while its recorded owner process identity is live. Reclaim it only after the owner is dead or conclusively mismatched and the existing minimum-age requirement is satisfied.
When process identity cannot be validated safely, preserve the directory and emit a structured uncertain-owner observation. Missing or malformed markers must follow the ownership rules from ddx-05e3d16b and ddx-1eb1ba93; a prefix alone is never host-global ownership proof.

IN-SCOPE FILES
- cli/internal/testutils/fixture_repo.go and fixture_repo_test.go
- cli/internal/agent/execution_cleanup.go and execution_cleanup_test.go
- a small shared internal scratch-owner marker package and its tests

NON-SCOPE
Do not change Fizeau routing, test-seam behavior, harness selection, model selection, or provider policy.
Do not replace the process-wide sync.Once binary cache with t.TempDir.
Do not redesign general host-global scratch trust; ddx-05e3d16b and ddx-1eb1ba93 own that policy.
Do not reclaim a metadata-less or uncertain-owner host-global directory merely because its name matches a DDx prefix.
Do not change execution scratch placement; ddx-b2702b9f owns that migration.

PARENT
ddx-f914dddd

DEPS
ddx-b2702b9f must land first so both producers use the configured scratch root.
ddx-1eb1ba93 must land first so metadata-marked stale reclamation and host-global ownership rules are established; it already depends on ddx-05e3d16b.

description:
PROBLEM
The two embedded-dispatch runner tests isolate provider configuration by changing HOME to a raw ddx-home-* directory. On Niflheim, an abandoned ddx-home-3567057526 contained a 468 MB private Go module cache with read-only module directories. A later internal/agent gate discovered that prefix, recursively walked it, and produced more than 2.7 GB of Go test operation logs before continuing. Repeated gates can duplicate the module cache, leak inodes, and make cleanup expensive.

ROOT CAUSE WITH FILE:LINE
cli/internal/agent/runner_test.go:29-34 and cli/internal/agent/runner_test.go:56-61 call os.MkdirTemp with an empty root, change HOME, and discard os.RemoveAll errors. Changing HOME also changes the default GOPATH and GOMODCACHE for any Go subprocess or embedded tool that does not receive explicit values. Downloaded module directories are commonly mode 0555, so the ignored cleanup error can leave the entire test HOME under the process-global temp root. These are the only ddx-home-* producers in cli/internal/agent.

PROPOSED FIX
Replace the raw os.MkdirTemp fixtures with a shared test helper backed by t.TempDir so cleanup failures are test failures. Before changing HOME, preserve an explicit stable Go module-cache/GOPATH policy for child work so the isolated provider-config HOME cannot become a second module cache. Add a tripwire that runs both embedded-dispatch paths and proves no HOME/go/pkg/mod tree and no new process-global ddx-home-* directory is created.

IN-SCOPE FILES
- cli/internal/agent/runner_test.go
- nearest internal/agent test helper if shared setup is warranted

NON-SCOPE
Do not change production runner routing, make live provider calls, delete existing host scratch, or change production cleanup ownership/budgets. ddx-f914dddd and ddx-de1ff4b4 own those cleanup changes.

PARENT
ddx-6a2ce3bd.

DEPS
None; this test-producer repair can land independently of the production scratch-root helper children.

description:
PROBLEM
Forwarded federation writes need an autonomous idempotency proof. Retrying the same hub-issued command with the same request id must replay the original result and must not launch duplicate workers, append duplicate bead events, or write the same document twice.

ROOT CAUSE
- docs/helix/03-test/test-plans/TP-002-server-web-ui.md:338 defines TC-017.5 idempotency for federated worker commands.
- docs/helix/03-test/test-plans/TP-002-server-web-ui.md:379 defines TC-020.6 idempotency for mutating managed-node commands.
- docs/helix/06-iterate/server-operator-workbench-plan-2026-06-08.md:98-102 requires forwarded commands to carry request id, target node/project, and expected version metadata.
- Existing GraphQL idempotency tests such as cli/internal/server/graphql/resolver_mutation_runs_test.go:101-154 and resolver_operator_prompt_test.go:218-231 cover local idempotency surfaces, but the federation owner-write path needs its own forwarded-command coverage.

PROPOSED FIX
- Add focused Go tests or live multi-process tests for forwarded federation write idempotency.
- Use the same request id/idempotency key for two identical hub-issued worker, bead, or document write commands.
- Assert the second response returns the original result/deduplicated state and does not duplicate spoke-local state.
- Cover at least two command classes: worker start and one persistent data mutation (`beadCreate` or `documentWrite`).
- Keep the test deterministic with loopback servers and synthetic request ids; do not rely on wall-clock sleeps beyond short polling for process readiness.

NON-SCOPE
- Do not build a new global idempotency framework unless existing request-id plumbing cannot support the tests.
- Do not add real network/tailnet tests.
- Do not change unrelated local run/operator-prompt idempotency behavior.

PARENT + DEPS
Parent: ddx-a038a090. Depends on live owner-targeted write coverage so the idempotency assertions attach to a proven forwarding path.

PROBLEM
Parent bead ddx-c6317784 is too broad for one execution pass. This child owns part 2 of 5 of that parent scope.

ROOT CAUSE
# PROBLEM
The bead backend interface today (`cli/internal/bead/backend.go`) is JSONL-shaped: `RawBackend` requires whole-corpus `ReadAll`/`WriteAll`, and `Backend` declares only 22 of `*Store`'s 69 public methods. Per TD-027 (the canonical Bead Storage System and Lifecycle spec), the bead architecture needs:

- A typed `Operation` pattern with `Apply(b *Bead) error` (CAS via error returns)
- 11 LSP-clean storage sub-interfaces composing `Backend`
- Pluggable `IDGenerator` and parallel `LifecycleSubscriber`
- `context.Context` first-parameter discipline on every interface method
- Sentinel errors (`ErrNotFound`, `ErrConflict`, `ErrInvalidID`, `ErrAlreadyClaimed`, `ErrNotClaimedByOwner`, `ErrUnsupported`)
- The optional `OperationApplier` interface on `RawBackend` so JSONL backends can preserve heartbeat sidecar optimization
- A canonical Bead data model (field enumeration + invariants + JSONL wire format + schema-versioning policy)

This bead lays the foundation that all per-concern beads (L/C/E/X/Q/D/A/MIG) depend on. It declares the event reader/writer interfaces but deliberately does not migrate `AppendEvent`, `Events`, or `EventsByKind`; the E bead owns event-method ctx threading and `*Store` event interface satisfaction.

- `cli/internal/bead/backend.go:10-67` — `RawBackend` (4 whole-corpus methods) + `Backend` (22 high-level methods, incomplete).
- `cli/internal/bead/store.go` — `*Store` exposes 69 public methods, none take `ctx context.Context`.
- `cli/internal/bead/axon_backend.go:340-381` — `WriteAll` ships entire corpus per mutation (catastrophic for Postgres).
- Operation pattern, IDGenerator, sentinel errors, context discipline — all absent.
- Bead data model (the canonical schema of fields + invariants) — only implicit in the Go struct.

# PROPOSED FIX
Implement TD-027 §5–§13 foundation pieces that are required before the per-concern beads can execute.

## New files

1. `cli/internal/bead/operation.go` — `Operation` interface with `Apply(b *Bead) error`. `MutateFunc` adapter for ad-hoc mutations. Empty named-op section (per-concern beads add their op types).
2. `cli/internal/bead/id.go` — `ValidateID`, format constants (`DefaultIDPrefix`, `MaxIDLength`, `MinIDLength`), `IDGenerator` interface, `RandomHexIDGenerator`, `SequentialIDGenerator`, `NewIDGenerator()` default.
3. `cli/internal/bead/errors.go` — sentinel e
...[truncated]

- Sentinel errors declared as distinct `error` values. Test: `TestSentinelErrors_AreErrorValues`.
- Context typed accessors implemented. Tests: `TestWithIdentity_RoundTrip`, `TestIdentityFromContext_AbsentReturnsFalse`, `TestWithTrace_RoundTrip`.

description:
PROBLEM
Execute-bead providers can launch a focused test and the full package suite concurrently. On 2026-07-13, the ddx-12a41acc provider stated that it would run the exact focused regex first and only then the full internal/agent suite, but emitted both tool calls in the same turn. That duplicated Go compilation, started the expensive suite before the focused proof was known green, and increased the chance of CPU and provider-process fan-out.

ROOT CAUSE WITH FILE:LINE
cli/internal/agent/execute_bead.go:2104-2112 and cli/internal/agent/execute_bead.go:2139-2147 require git/index mutations to be sequential but do not impose the same ordering on validation commands. cli/internal/agent/execute_bead.go:2085-2094 governs reruns of long commands but does not forbid overlapping focused tests, full suites, linters, or lefthook. Rich harnesses may issue multiple shell tool calls concurrently in one model turn, so narrative intent to run focused-then-full is not an execution constraint.

PROPOSED FIX
Add a shared execute-bead instruction requiring validation gates to run sequentially: wait for focused tests to complete successfully before launching broader package/workspace tests, then wait before lint or pre-commit. Explicitly forbid overlapping go test, cargo test, npm test, make test, and lefthook invocations in the same attempt. Preserve legitimate parallelism inside a single build/test command.

NON-SCOPE
Do not globally disable model tool parallelism, serialize read-only inspection, reduce language toolchain internal parallelism, skip any required gate, or weaken test timeouts. Resource enforcement and host-wide concurrency caps remain owned by ddx-c4cbf253 and ddx-93f6041e.

Parent: ddx-5958e8a. Depends on ddx-aa6cc320 so its internal/agent verification cannot launch real provider fixtures.

description:
PROBLEM
A Complete requirement can pass coverage cardinality by pointing at a whole test file in the Verification mapping instead of pinned proof. The analyzer must exclude those file-only rows before the cardinality join so requirements covered only by broad file paths are reported as uncovered.

ROOT CAUSE WITH FILE:LINE
The spechonesty analyzer package does not exist in this checkout: cli/tools/lint/spechonesty/analyzer.go:1 is absent, and cli/tools/lint/ currently contains only evidencelint, routinglint, and runtimelint. The sibling cardinality pass is expected to count mapping rows as coverage, but there is no integration point that filters rows through a citation-granularity predicate before joining requirements to Verification evidence. The governing contract is docs/helix/06-iterate/phase2-doc-truth-plan-2026-07-13.md:67, which requires coverage by a Verification mapping row rather than an unspecific pointer.

PROPOSED FIX
Wire the citation-granularity predicate into the coverage-cardinality pass before the requirement-to-evidence join. A mapping row whose evidence field resolves to a test-file path without an exact mapped Test* symbol, check, or artifact target must not count as coverage; an otherwise-Complete requirement covered only by that row must receive the sibling uncovered diagnostic. Rows naming concrete targets must still count and must not produce an uncovered diagnostic. Follow cli/tools/lint/evidencelint/analyzer.go and cli/tools/lint/evidencelint/analyzer_test.go conventions, including golang.org/x/tools/go/analysis and analysistest-style fixtures where applicable. The analyzer is read-only.

NON-SCOPE
Do not implement the zero-evidence empty-row-set diagnostic. Do not design the uncovered or duplicate cardinality diagnostic family beyond applying the pre-join file-only exclusion to the sibling cardinality pass. Do not handle waivers. Do not parse requirement inventories or mapping tables beyond consuming the mapping-parser child model. Do not implement status parsing. Do not auto-restamp documents, infer proof from prose, fetch network state, or mark aspirational metrics complete. Do not implement duplicate-id or stale-observation detection. Prose quality and AC numbering style are out of scope. Do not resolve whether named Test* symbols, static checks, or artifacts actually exist on disk; this child only relies on whether the row names a target at all. Do not enforce the executable verification command allowlist.

DEPS: parent ddx-29449fa5 and its parent ddx-471d66b6; the spechonesty scaffold/status-parser child; the Verification mapping-parser child that provides the inventory + rows model; the sibling coverage-cardinality child; the child bead that adds the citation-granularity predicate. GOVERNING ARTIFACT: docs/helix/06-iterate/phase2-doc-truth-plan-2026-07-13.md WB-1 steps 3-4.

description:
PROBLEM
An execute-bead agent that correctly writes status: open in no_changes_rationale.txt while leaving an uncommitted implementation patch is still sent through a synthesized iteration commit and the full staged pre-commit gate. Live attempt 20260713T105612-7589dd4a spent more than a minute in the race hook after a 745.706-second diagnostic failure, even though the agent explicitly requested retry and no land. This turns the fallback contract into another expensive mixed-result attempt and can discard useful dirty work after classification.

ROOT CAUSE WITH FILE:LINE
cli/internal/agent/execute_bead.go:1314-1377 checks IsDirty and calls SynthesizeCommit before reading the bundle rationale. Only afterward, cli/internal/agent/execute_bead.go:1415-1448 reads no_changes_rationale.txt and classifies a synthesized implementation commit plus rationale as mixed_commit_and_no_changes_rationale. Because RealGitOps.SynthesizeCommit invokes git commit, cli/internal/agent/gitops_real.go:148-218 also runs repository hooks before DDx learns that the attempt was explicitly retryable.

PROPOSED FIX
Read and parse the bundle no_changes_rationale.txt before the synthesis branch. When a valid status: open, status: proposed, status: blocked, or verification_command rationale is present and the agent made no explicit commit, do not call SynthesizeCommit. Preserve any dirty implementation diff as a durable rescue patch in the execution bundle, attach its path to the result, then classify the rationale normally. Retain synthesized commits for dirty successful exits without a rationale, and retain fail-closed mixed-result rejection when the agent itself made an implementation commit and also wrote a rationale.

NON-SCOPE
Do not weaken mixed_commit_and_no_changes_rationale rejection, skip required gates for successful implementation commits, change no-changes retry/close policy, or automatically land the preserved dirty patch.

PARENT
None; root execute-bead fallback-contract regression observed during the Niflheim queue drain.

DEPS
None.

description:
PROBLEM
procExecutionCleanupAttemptProcessScanner.inspect (cli/internal/agent/execution_cleanup_process_linux.go:57-74) drops a process entirely -- it is never even offered to classification -- whenever os.Readlink("/proc/<pid>/cwd") fails or returns empty (execution_cleanup_process_linux.go:63,70-72), or when the resolved cwd no longer maps to any known root. Such a process is invisible to the leftover-worktree scan even though it may still hold open files inside a leased worktree (design: docs/helix/02-design/technical-designs/TD-040-leftover-worktree-process-reaping.md, "Change 2").

ROOT CAUSE
Worktree attribution today has exactly one signal: cwd (executionCleanupAttemptProcessFromWorkerStatus, execution_cleanup_process.go:415-437, fed from procExecutionCleanupAttemptProcessScanner.inspect at execution_cleanup_process_linux.go:63). If proc.Worktree ends up empty, inspect returns `(executionCleanupAttemptProcess{}, false)` at execution_cleanup_process_linux.go:70-72 and the process is dropped from the scan entirely -- it never reaches classifyExecutionCleanupAttemptProcessGroup, so it can never be reaped no matter how long it has been orphaned.

PROPOSED FIX
In procExecutionCleanupAttemptProcessScanner.inspect, when cwd-based attribution yields an empty Worktree, add a fallback: enumerate /proc/<pid>/fd/*, resolve each entry's symlink target (best-effort, skipping unreadable descriptors), and apply the same root-truncation rule used for cwd attribution (reuse or extract the truncate-to-root helper introduced or existing in execution_cleanup_process.go) against each resolved target. The first fd target that truncates to a root under the configured tempRoot becomes Worktree. This is strictly additive: cwd-based attribution keeps priority, and a process with no cwd signal and no matching fd signal remains unclassified (excluded from the scan, never killed), preserving today's conservative default.

NON-SCOPE
- No change to the classification/kill-safety logic in classifyExecutionCleanupAttemptProcessGroup -- this bead only widens the detection signal feeding it.
- No non-Linux implementation -- mirrors the existing execution_cleanup_process_other.go no-op split.
- No change to the cwd-based root-normalization fix (separate child bead, ddx-79dab565).

description:
PROBLEM
On 2026-07-07 the multi-project workers stopped making steady claim progress because /tmp had zero free inodes. Cayce emitted repeated picker.claim_race events with `bead: create claim liveness tmp: open /tmp/ddx-claim-heartbeats/...: no space left on device`, while resource.preflight continued to report status=ok because it checked /Users/erik/Projects/.ddx-exec-wt and project evidence roots, not the claim-liveness root. Manual cleanup restored /tmp from 0 free inodes to ~347k free inodes and Cayce immediately claimed cayce-a9775904.

ROOT CAUSE WITH FILE:LINE
cli/internal/bead/claim_liveness.go:31-35 hardcodes claim heartbeat sidecars under `filepath.Join(os.TempDir(), "ddx-claim-heartbeats", ...)`.
cli/internal/bead/claim_liveness.go:56-64 creates atomic temp files in that directory and returns `bead: create claim liveness tmp` when /tmp has no inodes.
cli/internal/agent/execution_resources.go:250-267 enforces byte/inode thresholds only for roots passed into execution resource preflight, and current worker preflight evidence showed those roots excluded /tmp/ddx-claim-heartbeats.

PROPOSED FIX
Add the claim-liveness temp root to pre-claim resource preflight so inode exhaustion is detected before claim attempts loop as claim races. Prefer moving claim liveness under the configured DDx execution temp root or a project-scoped runtime root instead of raw os.TempDir(), but preserve stale-claim detection across workers on the same machine. Add cleanup for stale tmp files under ddx-claim-heartbeats and include reclaimed inode counts in resource.preflight events.

NON-SCOPE
Do not change bead claim semantics or heartbeat TTL. Do not remove durable worker/evidence history. Do not weaken cross-worker stale-claim protection.

ROOT CAUSE WITH FILE:LINE
The spechonesty analyzer path is absent in this checkout at cli/tools/lint/spechonesty/analyzer.go:1, and the analyzer run has no runtime-artifact existence check over parsed Verification rows. The governing contract is docs/helix/06-iterate/phase2-doc-truth-plan-2026-07-13.md:67, requiring every Complete/Implemented mapping row to name an exact evidence target, and docs/helix/06-iterate/phase2-doc-truth-plan-2026-07-13.md:68, requiring rejection of mappings to nonexistent artifacts. PROPOSED FIX
When spechonesty runtime-artifact validation emits a missing-artifact diagnostic, populate the diagnostic with the requirement id from the parsed Verification mapping row and the source document path containing that row. Reuse the mapping-parser row model for source metadata and do not infer missing context from prose. Keep the analyzer read-only.

NON-SCOPE
Do not add new categories of diagnostics beyond missing inspectable runtime artifact mappings. Do not reimplement target classification or path resolution — consume the resolver child. Do not handle waivers — that is the waiver child. Do not parse requirement inventories or mapping tables — that is the mapping-parser child. Do not auto-restamp documents, infer proof from prose, fetch network state, or mark aspirational metrics complete. Status parsing lives in the scaffold child. Duplicate-id and stale-observation detection are a sibling child. Prose quality and AC numbering style are out of scope. Do not enforce requirement coverage cardinality or duplicate mapping counts — the coverage-cardinality child owns that. description:

Execution code lacks a transport-neutral coordination domain contract for claim requests and outcomes, so connected and offline workers cannot share claim contention semantics.

ROOT CAUSE WITH FILE:LINE
cli/cmd/try.go:256-259 and cli/cmd/execute_loop_shared.go:280-282 construct NewLocalLandCoordinator directly, bypassing any domain contract. cli/internal/agent/workerprobe/probe.go:129-224 tracks connection state and buffers events in memory, but does not define typed claim requests, claim outcomes, idempotency keys, or contention behavior.

PROPOSED FIX
Add or extend a coordination domain package under cli/internal/agent with typed claim request/outcome APIs and a local implementation backed by the existing bead-store claim path. Add TestCoordinationContract_LocalClaimContention to exercise two local coordinators against a real temporary bead store and git repository, proving one claim wins and the contending claim receives the contract-defined already-claimed/contended outcome without call-recording mocks.

NON-SCOPE
Do not add server routes, wire Cobra commands, centralize bead picking, or change process ownership. Do not implement the HTTP coordination client in this bead. Do not implement the durable offline journal or cross-process offline lock here except for interfaces needed by the contract. Do not cover tracker transitions or landing outcomes beyond the minimal types needed to keep the claim contract cohesive.

description:
PROBLEM
Complete/Implemented documents can claim verification with a Verification mapping row whose evidence target is an inspectable runtime artifact path that does not exist. That lets a Complete stamp rely on unverifiable artifact names instead of current-revision evidence.

ROOT CAUSE WITH FILE:LINE
The requested spechonesty analyzer path is absent in this checkout at cli/tools/lint/spechonesty/analyzer.go:1, and the parent analyzer work has not yet added runtime-artifact existence checks for parsed Verification rows. The governing contract is docs/helix/06-iterate/phase2-doc-truth-plan-2026-07-13.md:67, which requires every Complete/Implemented mapping row to name an exact evidence target, and docs/helix/06-iterate/phase2-doc-truth-plan-2026-07-13.md:68, which requires rejecting mappings to nonexistent artifacts. Current-revision executable verification is reinforced at docs/helix/06-iterate/phase2-doc-truth-plan-2026-07-13.md:176.

PROPOSED FIX
After the spechonesty scaffold/status-parser child and Verification mapping-parser child exist, add artifact-target validation for mapping rows whose evidence target type is an inspectable runtime artifact. A mapped runtime artifact target must resolve to an existing repository path or generated fixture artifact that the analyzer can inspect without network access. Emit a missing-artifact diagnostic for each nonexistent artifact target, naming the path from the mapping row. Keep the analyzer read-only.

NON-SCOPE
Do not handle waivers — that is the waiver child. Do not parse requirement inventories or mapping tables — that is the mapping-parser child. Do not auto-restamp documents, infer proof from prose, fetch network state, or mark aspirational metrics complete. Status parsing lives in the scaffold child. Duplicate-id and stale-observation detection are a sibling child. Prose quality and AC numbering style are out of scope. Do not enforce requirement coverage cardinality or duplicate mapping counts — the coverage-cardinality child owns that. Do not resolve Go Test* symbols or static check names — the evidence-target child owns those checks. Do not enforce command allowlisting — the verification-command allowlist child owns that.

DEPS: parent ddx-29449fa5; parent/root dependency ddx-471d66b6; the spechonesty scaffold/status-parser child; the Verification mapping-parser child that provides the inventory + rows model. GOVERNING ARTIFACT: docs/helix/06-iterate/phase2-doc-truth-plan-2026-07-13.md WB-1 steps 3-4.

1. `TestSupervisor_OperatorAttentionTerminalDoesNotRespawn` still proves an unresolved operator_attention worker is not immediately respawned.
2. Add `TestSupervisor_ResolvedOperatorAttentionAllowsRespawnAfterDesiredUpdate` proving that a desired state update newer than the blocking terminal and a clean project root allow a new worker to start.
3. Add `TestSupervisor_HistoricalOperatorAttentionDoesNotBlockFreshDesiredStateAcrossRestart` proving old `.ddx/workers/*/status.json` records do not permanently suppress desired workers after a server restart.

description:
PROBLEM
  Server-managed workers can remain absent even when `.ddx/workers/desired.json` has `desired_count=1`. On 2026-07-07, `/home/erik/Projects/ddx` had desired_count=1 and `/home/erik/Projects/niflheim` had desired_count=1, but `ddx work status --all-projects --json` showed only axon and helix workers. Both ddx and niflheim had older `status=operator_attention` worker records, while the current desired state still asked the supervisor to run one worker.

ROOT CAUSE
  `cli/internal/server/workers_supervisor.go:364-374` records every restart-blocking terminal worker into `blockedTerminals`. `cli/internal/server/workers_supervisor.go:417-419` then makes `canStartMore` return false whenever `blockedTerminals` is non-empty. There is no expiry, no check that the underlying dirty/root condition has been resolved, and no operator command/state transition that clears the block. Because `snapshotWorkers` reads historical terminal records from `.ddx/workers`, the block can survive server restarts and suppress a fresh desired worker indefinitely.

PROPOSED FIX
  - `cli/internal/server/workers_supervisor.go:364-419`: distinguish active unresolved operator-attention stops from stale historical records. A clean project root with a current desired state must be able to start again after the operator resolves the condition.
  - `cli/internal/server/workers_supervisor.go:497-516`: keep true restart-blocking semantics for genuinely unresolved dirty-root/operator-attention records, but add a deterministic release path keyed to resolved project state or an explicit desired-state update timestamp newer than the blocking worker.
  - `cli/internal/server/workers_supervisor_test.go`: add regression coverage for a historical operator_attention terminal followed by a newer desired state and clean project root.

NON-SCOPE
  - Do not weaken the dirty-root guard inside `ddx work`; a currently dirty implementation root must still stop.
  - Do not edit or delete existing `.ddx/workers/*/status.json` records as the fix. Worker history must remain durable.
  - Do not change routing/model/provider selection.

PARENT / DEPS
  Root operational bug. No deps.

description:
PROBLEM
A DDx run record that has reached dispatching or running must be finalized from typed immediate errors and public final execution events. Without terminal updates, final outcome, completion time, cost/token data, and repository evidence still have to be inferred from execution directories, bundles, or provider-specific artifacts.

ROOT CAUSE WITH FILE:LINE
cli/internal/agent/service_run.go:230-233 calls FizeauService.Execute and then consumes public execution events, while cli/internal/server/state_runs.go:295-317 and cli/internal/server/state_runs.go:465-490 still synthesize run-layer state from sessions and bundles when no stored record exists. The Phase 3 WB-2 plan at docs/helix/06-iterate/phase3-server-rebuild-plan-2026-07-13.md:104-149 requires the DDx-owned record to reach terminal state using typed immediate/final result fields plus repository evaluation evidence, not provider-session canonical state.

PROPOSED FIX
On typed immediate error and on public final execution event plus repository evaluation, atomically update the existing .ddx/runs/<run-id>/record.json to a terminal lifecycle phase. Persist typed outcome fields, completed timestamp, cost/token fields when available, and evidence links to repository evaluation artifacts. Keep legacy read-side session synthesis unchanged except where tests need to observe the newly stored record.

NON-SCOPE
Do not query provider sessions for canonical state, build the UI migration, implement legacy migration, choose a Fizeau route, implement the first running transition behavior, or implement kill-interruption atomicity tests beyond the normal writer contract used by this terminal update.

GOVERNING ARTIFACT
docs/helix/06-iterate/phase3-server-rebuild-plan-2026-07-13.md:104-149, WB-2 run substrate.

PARENT
Original bead ddx-61c41896. Queue parent field ddx-5bf0f8d0.

DEPS
Phase 1 typed Fizeau result contract and Phase 0 safe execution exit. Requires the run-record schema/writer and pre-dispatch publish children to be available before final wiring.

description:
PROBLEM
A document can claim Complete/Implemented while citing a test file that does not contain the test it implies, leaving normative requirements unmapped, mapping one requirement twice, or pointing at an artifact that does not exist. FEAT-009/FEAT-002/FEAT-012 are Complete with absent or incomplete verification coverage; TD-027 cites phantom tests (TestOperationCatalog_AxonStoreSwitchCoverage and TestWatcherHub_UsesProvidedFactory do not exist) alongside two real ones — two real tests must not make absent coverage pass.

ROOT CAUSE WITH FILE:LINE
The spechonesty analyzer at cli/tools/lint/spechonesty/analyzer.go has no Complete-status verification-coverage logic; it consumes the requirement inventory and mapping rows produced by the mapping-parser child but never checks them. The contract is docs/helix/06-iterate/phase2-doc-truth-plan-2026-07-13.md WB-1 steps 3-4.

PROPOSED FIX
For every Complete/Implemented document, require that every requirement/anchor in the inventory is covered by exactly one Verification mapping row. For each row, resolve its evidence target: a `Test*` symbol must exist, a named static check must exist, and an inspectable runtime artifact path must exist; the row's command must be on the executable verification allowlist. Produce a failure for each uncovered requirement, missing evidence target (nonexistent `Test*` symbol, check, or artifact), duplicate mapping of a requirement, or non-allowlisted command. A test-file path without the specific test or check it proves is not coverage. Reject any zero-evidence Complete/Implemented document. Analyzer remains read-only.

NON-SCOPE
Do not handle waivers — that is the waiver child. Do not parse requirement inventories or mapping tables — that is the mapping-parser child. Do not auto-restamp documents, infer proof from prose, fetch network state, or mark aspirational metrics complete. Status parsing lives in the scaffold child. Duplicate-id and stale-observation detection are a sibling child. Prose quality and AC numbering style are out of scope.

DEPS: the spechonesty scaffold/status-parser child and the Verification mapping-parser child (provides the inventory + rows model).

description:
# PROBLEM
The pre-claim dirty-root gate and the land advancer's staged-changes check both compute the exact dirty-path list, then park unconditionally. Observed: ddx worker idled 8h (02:20-14:31Z 2026-07-06) over one DDx-owned file; pqueue exited on every relaunch for 10h over stash-safe attempt files. Both were resolvable by the classification now codified in 'ddx doctor --unjam' (ddx-f8582f42).

# PROPOSED FIX
Before parking, both gates invoke the unjam classification: if every dirty path resolves to class (a) DDx-owned or (b) preserve-ref-backed, remediate in place and proceed (claim / land) in the same loop iteration; only class (c) unknown paths park with operator_attention listing the unremediated paths. Grep entry points: the preflight that prints 'project root has uncommitted tracked changes' and the land advancer that prints 'landing worktree has staged changes' (cli/internal/agent/).

# NON-SCOPE
The suite itself (ddx-f8582f42); supervisor watchdog (sibling).

description:
PROBLEM
The required cd cli && go test ./internal/agent/... -timeout 600s gate has again exhausted its entire package-wide timeout. During attempt 20260713T062233-4a0585c0 it timed out three times after distinct cleanup-fixture fixes; the latest run reached TestExecuteBead_RoutingEvidenceRecorded only at the end and that test had run for about one second when the package alarm fired at 600.034s. Focused tests are green and no live provider fan-out remains, so the gate has insufficient cumulative runtime headroom and prevents otherwise valid bead work from landing.

ROOT CAUSE WITH FILE:LINE
cli/internal/agent/agent_test.go:21-29 runs all 1,341 root-package tests beneath one TestMain and therefore one 600-second package budget. The heavy Git, execution-worktree, cleanup, and concurrency fixtures accumulate serial wall time. The prior fix in closed bead ddx-1a0d4d26 saved only about twelve seconds by shortening lsof and one sleep; subsequent suite growth and shared-root cleanup regressions consumed that margin. .github/workflows/ci.yml:248-270 records test JSON and a timing summary, but the job is non-gating and cli/tools/test-timing/main.go:19-72 reports only individual tests, not package total or required headroom, so this regression was not detected before the default gate became un-runnable.

PROPOSED FIX
- Capture a cold-cache go test -json baseline for internal/agent and use cli/tools/test-timing to identify the cumulative hot path, including subprocess, Git fixture, polling, and cleanup costs.
- Reduce the top contributors with deterministic synchronization, smaller private fixtures, and safe t.Parallel use where tests have no process-global environment, cwd, Git config, or shared-cache state. Split genuinely integration-only coverage into an explicit subpackage or integration lane only when its default-gate coverage is preserved elsewhere.
- Extend cli/tools/test-timing and the CI timing path to report package elapsed time and flag loss of the required 20 percent headroom, so suite growth is observable before the hard timeout.
- Preserve all existing assertions and the five-worker concurrency coverage. Do not skip tests, weaken race/cleanup checks, raise the 600-second timeout, or serialize around a live external provider.

NON-SCOPE
Do not change production worker routing, provider selection, or queue ordering. Provider fixture isolation is owned by ddx-aa6cc320; shared scratch-root isolation is owned by ddx-e6abf4a6; bounded production reclamation is owned by ddx-de1ff4b4.

PARENT
None; root performance regression.

DEPS
ddx-e6abf4a6 must land first so performance measurements use private test scratch roots instead of host-wide cleanup work.

Observed process I/O reached approximately 2.9 GB rchar and 1.26 GB write_bytes. Use this attempt as the before baseline and include Go testlog/cache amplification among the top contributors.

description:
PROBLEM
A stale terminal worker record can suppress all desired worker restarts indefinitely.

ROOT CAUSE WITH FILE:LINE
cli/internal/server/workers_supervisor.go:411-418 returns false whenever blockedTerminals is non-empty. cli/internal/server/workers_supervisor.go:441-453 clears blocked terminals only when desired.UpdatedAt is newer than the terminal time. cli/internal/server/workers_supervisor.go:374-386 records operator_attention/dirty_root terminals into blockedTerminals but cli/internal/server/workers_supervisor.go:387-388 does not add those terminals to restartEvents, so restart backoff does not throttle expired blocks.

PROPOSED FIX
Add DefaultTerminalBlockTTL = 10m in the supervisor, expire blocks older than the TTL, clear blocks when desired.UpdatedAt is newer, and make active blocks consume one desired slot instead of suppressing all starts. When an expired block permits a restart, append a restartEvents entry with reason/evidence sufficient for existing restart backoff to throttle repeat expired-block restarts.

NON-SCOPE
Do not add a new worker-slot store. Do not change worker launch argv or liveness predicates in this bead.
notes: Reviewed design clarification: terminal suppression reasons must be canonicalized before storage/comparison. Map dirty_root/dirty-root/dirty root to dirty_root, operator_attention to operator_attention, and EMFILE/too many open files/resource_exhausted to resource_exhausted; expired resource_exhausted blocks feed the same restart throttle as expired operator_attention/dirty_root blocks.

description:
PROBLEM
After attempt 20260713T062233-4a0585c0 failed, the managed worker launched post-attempt bead-lifecycle triage as Codex PID 1130622. During that live provider call, ddx work status --json reported active_work.count=1 but bead_ids=[] and no provider_children, even though the prompt was explicitly classifying ddx-aa6cc320. A slow or leaked classifier is therefore indistinguishable from an idle worker and can block the single queue worker indefinitely after the implementation lease is already released.

ROOT CAUSE WITH FILE:LINE
cli/internal/agent/execute_bead_loop.go:3623-3625 clears the attempt liveness record immediately when the implementation attempt returns. The later parking path at cli/internal/agent/execute_bead_loop.go:4103-4117 releases the claim and invokes runPostAttemptTriage without publishing a candidate-scoped phase. runPostAttemptTriage at cli/internal/agent/execute_bead_loop.go:640-653 calls the hook directly with the long-lived loop context and no operation deadline or descendant cleanup. cli/internal/agent/triage_hook.go:109-123 dispatches the model provider, so any provider child created there is outside the attempt watchdog and absent from status.

PROPOSED FIX
- Publish transient candidate-scoped post_attempt_triage liveness before dispatch, heartbeat it with provider-child metadata, and keep it explicitly lease-free.
- Add a configurable bounded post-attempt triage deadline with a conservative default; on expiry append a structured post_attempt_triage_timeout event, preserve the original report, and continue the watch loop.
- Establish a provider-process baseline and terminate/reap only descendants introduced by the triage hook on success, malformed output, error, timeout, and cancellation.
- Clear transient triage state on every return while preserving the existing fail-open report semantics and event ordering.

NON-SCOPE
Do not change bead-lifecycle classification vocabulary, retry/cooldown policy, implementation-attempt watchdog budgets, or preclaim decomposition lifecycle owned by ddx-092f0d34. Do not kill providers that predate the triage hook or belong to another worker.

PARENT
None; root reliability regression.

DEPS
ddx-2afca9c9 must land first so the required internal/agent gate has reliable runtime headroom.

description:
PROBLEM
DDx workers continue attempting claims and dispatches while /tmp is already near inode exhaustion, so one failing attempt can cascade into many ENOSPC failures. On 2026-07-08, DDx and Cayce workers repeatedly failed shell startup with `ENOSPC: no space left on device, mkdir /tmp/claude-501/...`; manual stale cleanup restored progress immediately. Cleanup exists, but it is not escalated aggressively when inode use crosses a critical threshold.

ROOT CAUSE WITH FILE:LINE
cli/internal/agent/execute_bead_loop.go:1664 runs cleanup at worker startup and cli/internal/agent/execute_bead_loop.go:2044 runs cleanup pre-claim, but the cleanup pass is generic and does not escalate based on inode high-water state.
cli/internal/agent/execution_cleanup.go:821-825 uses a fixed default scratch min age, so even obvious DDx-owned scratch may survive until the age threshold despite active resource pressure.
cli/internal/agent/execution_resources.go:250-267 checks roots after cleanup but does not trigger an aggressive DDx-owned scratch cleanup mode when inode use is critically high.

PROPOSED FIX
Add an inode high-water cleanup mode before claim and before dispatch: if a checked temp root has inode usage above a critical threshold or free inodes below the hard minimum, run an aggressive-but-safe cleanup pass for DDx-owned scratch prefixes (ddx-home-*, ddx-provider-shim-*, ddx-fixture-bin-*, stale claim-liveness tmp files) with a shorter pressure-only age threshold. If cleanup cannot restore hard minimum capacity, stop the worker with a clear resource_exhausted/operator_attention event rather than repeatedly claiming beads that cannot run.

IN-SCOPE FILES
- cli/internal/agent/execute_bead_loop.go
- cli/internal/agent/execution_resources.go
- cli/internal/agent/execution_cleanup.go
- cli/internal/agent/execute_bead_loop_cleanup_test.go or resource preflight tests

NON-SCOPE
Do not delete non-DDx-owned /tmp content. Do not weaken ordinary cleanup safety when no resource pressure exists. Do not hide resource_exhausted; if cleanup fails, the worker must stop or surface operator attention clearly. Do not change provider routing.
title: work: run aggressive DDx scratch cleanup at inode high-water

description:
Hand-curated sub-agent prompts have been outperforming ddx work / ddx try in this session. Two competing hypotheses for why:
H1: ddx execution machinery (the 9 fail-prone layers) is unreliable — failure is in the workers/server code.
H2: Bead authoring quality is insufficient — beads punt investigation; hand-curation papers over the gap.

Both are plausible. Determining the relative contribution requires a 3-path study, NOT the original 2-path proposal.

THREE PATHS

Path A: ddx try / ddx work with the bead's auto-prompt verbatim (current production path).
Path B: Sub-agent dispatched with the bead's auto-prompt verbatim (NOT hand-curated). Same prompt as A; different executor. Isolates ddx machinery from prompt quality.
Path C: Sub-agent dispatched with operator hand-curated prompt (file:line cites, named tests, explicit non-scope, etc.). Establishes the ceiling.

INTERPRETATION
- A vs B differ → ddx machinery is the failure (file follow-ups against the 9 layers).
- B vs C differ → bead authoring quality is the failure (already covered by bead-quality-audit + retrofit).
- A == B << C → both are real, with bead quality being the dominant gap.

METHOD
Pick 5 representative CLOSED beads as fixtures: one trivial fix, one refactor child, one test addition, one multi-file feature, one documentation update. For each fixture, run all 3 paths on a branch from the bead's base-rev (parent of the original work commit). Throwaway commits — the original work is already in main. We're measuring path properties, not producing mergeable code.

MEASUREMENTS
Per path per bead:
- Time-to-first-claim (A) / time-to-first-output (B,C)
- Time-to-merge-eligible-commit (whether or not we merge)
- Attempts (A) / iterations (B,C)
- Status outcomes: success / no_changes / preserved / blocked / errored
- Cost: tokens, USD
- Manual interventions
- Failure mode classified per the 9-layer machinery list

OUTPUT
.ddx/executions/<run-id>/ddx-vs-subagent-comparison-2026-05-03.md with:
- Per-bead per-path table
- Aggregate stats (median + p99)
- Failure-mode distribution
- Hypothesis verdict (H1 vs H2 vs both)
- Recommendations for which path is appropriate for which bead-shape

TIMING
This study runs AFTER the executeloop refactor (C0-C13) lands so the ddx machinery is its post-refactor shape. Running pre-refactor measures behavior we're about to change. RELIABILITY-PRINCIPLES + bead-quality-audit + retrofit + refactor must all complete first. This bead is filed now and EXECUTION DEFERRED.

NOT IN SCOPE
- Fixing whatever the study reveals (separate bug beads filed from the study's findings)
- Running against pre-refactor ddx machinery (data we won't act on)
- Comparing different sub-agent harnesses (different concern)

EVIDENCE
- ddx-f339c399 documents the 2026-05-04 ddx try ddx-29058e2a --harness=codex no_changes outcome and is partial Path B-vs-C data favoring the bead-quality hypothesis.

description:
PROBLEM
On 2026-06-29 DDx recorded four unrelated provider subprocess failures only as transport: exit status 1, then immediately claimed another bead after each failure. That erased whether the child was killed by SIGKILL/SIGTERM and allowed a clustered infrastructure failure to consume multiple beads and model contexts without a recovery interval.

ROOT CAUSE WITH FILE:LINE
cli/internal/agent/executor.go:301-330 records only an integer ExitCode and discards exec.ExitError.ProcessState/syscall.WaitStatus signal evidence. cli/internal/agent/runner.go:351-390 copies only that exit code and stderr into Result. cli/internal/agent/execute_bead_loop.go:6036-6098 then collapses transport-like text into the generic transport outcome. The watch loop maintains no rolling timestamps for transport outcomes, so three failures inside ten minutes do not delay the next claim.

PROPOSED FIX
Carry portable termination metadata from OSExecutor through Result and ExecuteBeadReport, including a signal name/number when ProcessState proves a signal termination. Preserve ordinary nonzero-exit behavior. In watch mode, track transport-class failure timestamps for the current worker; after three within ten minutes, emit a transport_cluster_cooldown observation and apply a context-cancellable delay of at least five minutes before another claim. Reset/expire the rolling window after successful work or elapsed window time.

NON-SCOPE
Do not infer OOM without kernel evidence, change queue ordering, mutate the failed bead to blocked/proposed, add host-load sampling, or change durable_audit commit flow. The cooldown is worker/infra pacing and must not become a per-bead retry-after.

PARENT
ddx-29491a0e. This child owns provider termination taxonomy and clustered transport pacing only.

DEPS
ddx-aa6cc320 must land first because this child changes internal/agent code and its required package gate currently launches live providers.

description:
PROBLEM
Parent bead ddx-6a2ce3bd is too broad for one execution pass. This child owns part 1 of 3 of that parent scope.

ROOT CAUSE
PROBLEM
DDx-owned temporary homes, provider shims, and helper scratch are created directly under raw os.TempDir(), so /tmp remains the choke point even when DDx has a configured execution/runtime temp root with available space. The 2026-07-08 incident had /tmp at 100% inode use while the configured execution worktree root under /Users/erik/Projects/.ddx-exec-wt still had capacity.

ROOT CAUSE WITH FILE:LINE
cli/internal/agent/provider_spawn.go:91 creates provider shims with os.MkdirTemp("", "ddx-provider-shim-").
cli/internal/agent/runner_test.go:29 and runner_test.go:56 create ddx-home-* with os.MkdirTemp("", "ddx-home-"); equivalent command tests create the same prefix in cli/cmd/work_resource_exhausted_test.go:80, cli/cmd/try_test.go:823, and cli/cmd/doctor_test.go:85.
cli/internal/testutils/fixture_repo.go:116 creates ddx-fixture-bin-* with os.MkdirTemp("", ...).
These producers bypass config.ExecutionScratchRoot / config.ExecutionWorktreeRoot and strand inode-heavy scratch under /tmp.

PROPOSED FIX
Add a shared helper for DDx-owned scratch temp dirs that prefers config.ExecutionScratchRoot(projectRoot) or the configured execution/runtime root when a project root is available, and falls back to os.TempDir() only when no configured root exists. Migrate provider shims and DDx-owned temp homes/fixture bins to the helper where production/runtime context is available. Keep tests hermetic by setting the helper root explicitly in tests.

IN-SCOPE FILES
- cli/internal/agent/provider_spawn.go
- cli/internal/config/execution_worktree_root.go or a new scratch-temp helper package
- relevant tests in cli/internal/agent and cli/cmd

NON-SCOPE
Do not move claim-liveness in this bead; ddx-3986b89a covers claim heartbeat root selection. Do not change git worktree placement. Do not store long-lived user config in execution scratch. Do not require a project root for all tests; fallback behavior must remain.

PROPOSED FIX
Implement only this child acceptance slice:
- TestDDXScratchTempDirUsesConfiguredExecutionRoot proves a DDx scratch temp helper creates ddx-home/provider-shim style directories under the configured execution/runtime root when configured.
- TestDDXScratchTempDirFallsBackToOSTempDirWithoutConfiguredRoot proves fallback behavior remains when no project/config root is available.

NON-SCOPE
Do not implement parent acceptance criteria assigned to sibling child beads. Preserve every parent non-scope constraint unless this child explicitly narrows it.

description:
PROBLEM
The cleanup-fixture split is not independently landable. Attempt 20260713T153145-d424151a correctly isolated TestWorkCleanup_RunsAfterSetupFailureBeforeNextClaim, added its outside-root sentinel regression, and passed the focused gate. The required full internal/agent gate still entered host-dependent fixture work and had to be interrupted after five minutes; the SIGQUIT snapshot was in TestWorkInterrupt_InFlightAttemptUnclaimsBead. Leaving the remaining production ExecutionCleanupManager fixtures for a dependent part 2 means part 1 cannot satisfy its own package acceptance before part 2 is allowed to run.

ROOT CAUSE WITH FILE:LINE
- cli/internal/agent/execute_bead_loop_cleanup_test.go:269-288 constructs a production NewExecutionCleanupManager without explicit TempRoot or ScratchRoots. The valid unlanded attempt patch shows this fixture needs roots below its own t.TempDir and an outside-root sentinel.
- cli/internal/agent/execution_cleanup_test.go:102-114 centralizes project-root setup but does not enforce hermetic effective cleanup roots across the many NewExecutionCleanupManager call sites in internal/agent tests.
- cli/internal/agent/execution_cleanup.go:830-843 derives the configured cache parent and os.TempDir whenever ScratchRoots is unset, so any missed test fixture can enumerate accumulated host state.
- cli/internal/agent/execute_bead_loop_test.go:3014-3027 creates stores through the normal config loader. In the failed full-suite snapshot, cli/internal/agent/execute_bead_loop_disruption_test.go:250-279 was blocked under that helper while the test process remained host-dependent. This path must be audited along with cleanup runners so the package gate has no hidden global-root dependency.

PROPOSED FIX
Make this the atomic fixture-hermeticity repair. Recreate the valid attempt-20260713T153145-d424151a work-loop change: configure fixture-local TempRoot and ScratchRoots and add TestWorkCleanup_RunsAfterSetupFailureBeforeNextClaim_DoesNotTouchSharedScratchRoot. Add or extend a shared cleanup-test helper that requires every internal/agent fixture invoking a production ExecutionCleanupManager.Cleanup to use roots beneath its own t.TempDir, and audit all such call sites. Add a regression for newExecuteLoopTestStore/runInterruptedWorkAttempt if it can inherit process-global DDx/config roots. The completed change must make the focused fixtures and the full internal/agent package gate independently green in one commit.

IN-SCOPE FILES
- cli/internal/agent/execute_bead_loop_cleanup_test.go
- cli/internal/agent/execution_cleanup_test.go and the nearest cleanup fixture helpers/call sites
- cli/internal/agent/execution_cleanup_process_test.go and execution_resources_test.go where production cleanup is invoked
- cli/internal/agent/execute_bead_loop_test.go and execute_bead_loop_disruption_test.go only as needed to make the observed store/config fixture hermetic

NON-SCOPE
Do not change production cleanup behavior, retention policy, or deletion semantics. Do not add a package-wide TestMain sandbox, skip tests, weaken timeouts, or treat a killed/incomplete full-suite run as success. Do not rely on an uncommitted worktree or /tmp artifact; the valid part-1 behavior is fully stated above.

PARENT AND DEPS

PROBLEM
Parent bead ddx-43b6b5fe is too broad for one execution pass. This child owns part 4 of 4 of that parent scope.

ROOT CAUSE
PROBLEM
The two principles of epic ddx-602ae31a (ddx home resolution + skills/personas install topology) must behave identically across both modes (in-tree and convention). Today there is no single test suite that drives the same scenarios through both modes; coverage is per-mode-ad-hoc and divergence between modes is invisible until operators hit it in production.

ROOT CAUSE
The two parent beads (ddx-06cbaa90 and ddx-937de9fc) each carry per-feature tests. Neither owns the cross-mode equivalence guarantee.

PROPOSED FIX

1. Add cli/internal/agent/test_mode_matrix_test.go (or equivalent suite under a new package) that parameterizes every behaviour-equivalence scenario across both modes:

  for mode in [Convention, InTree]:
    setup_fixture(mode)
    for scenario in [
      "bead-lifecycle":           create/show/update/close
      "bead-execution":           ddx try a bead, observe attempt evidence and state mutation
      "plugin-skill-resolution":  ddx-side plugin lookup honors precedence; agent-tier symlinks resolve to plugin content
      "persona-binding":          role → persona resolves correctly per binding config
      "worker-drain":             ddx work --watch picks beads and lands them
      "meta-prompt-sync":         CLAUDE.md (or equivalent) gets the right content
      "auto-commit-routing":      bead create/update auto-commit lands in the right git repo (project's vs XDG's)
      "attachments":              per-attempt event files written to the right anchor
      "index-lock-recovery":      gitlock recovery fires correctly in both modes
    ]:
      run scenario in current mode
      assert behaviour identical to the other mode modulo storage path

2. Fixture setup must be deterministic and isolated:
   - Convention mode fixture: tempdir as project root, no .ddx/; XDG_DATA_HOME pointed at a per-test tempdir; git remote set to a deterministic URL.
   - In-tree mode fixture: tempdir as project root WITH .ddx/ pre-created; XDG_DATA_HOME pointed elsewhere (must not be consulted).
   - Two clones of the same project share an XDG dir — explicitly tested as a separate sub-scenario.

3. Document the test-mode invariant in cli/internal/agent/test_mode_matrix_test.go's package doc: "Any behavior that diverges between Convention and InTree modes (other than the on-disk anchor) is a regression."

acceptance:
1. TestOfflineJournal_OrderedDurableResume verifies crash-safe monotonic sequence persistence across journal close/reopen.
2. TestOfflineJournal_OrderedDurableResume verifies acknowledged-through resume skips acknowledged mutations while preserving later unacknowledged mutations in original order.
3. TestOfflineJournal_OrderedDurableResume verifies compaction does not drop an unacknowledged mutation and preserves idempotency key, payload hash, precondition, and outcome fields.
4. cd cli && go test ./internal/agent/... -run "TestOfflineJournal_OrderedDurableResume" passes.
5. lefthook run pre-commit passes.
description:
<context-digest>
<principles>Spec-first development · Executable specifications · Audit trail required · Work is a DAG · Drift is debt · Inspect and adapt</principles>
<concerns>go-std | security-owasp | testing</concerns>
<practices>Go domain interface with contract tests against real implementations · project-scoped durable files · no call-recording mocks · go test + lefthook</practices>
<adrs>ADR-022 rev 6 requires one reconnecting coordination client, durable ordered offline journal, idempotency keys, and a cross-process offline project lock.</adrs>
<governing>FEAT-006 Worker Contract: connected mutations use the server; disconnected manual workers apply the same operations locally and reconcile before new online writes.</governing>
</context-digest>

PROBLEM
Disconnected/manual worker mutations have no durable ordered journal, so a process crash can lose ordering, idempotency keys, preconditions, outcomes, or acknowledgement state needed for later reconciliation before online writes.

ROOT CAUSE WITH FILE:LINE
cli/internal/agent/workerprobe/probe.go:129-224 buffers only workerprobe events in memory. The parent bead identifies that no durable idempotency-keyed coordination record exists, and cli/cmd/try.go:256-259 plus cli/cmd/execute_loop_shared.go:280-282 bypass any journal by constructing local landing coordination directly.

PROPOSED FIX
Add a project-scoped offline journal under cli/internal/agent with monotonic sequence numbers, idempotency key, payload hash, precondition, outcome, durable acknowledgement-through state, resume ordering, and safe compaction that never drops unacknowledged mutations.

NON-SCOPE
Do not add server routes, wire Cobra commands, centralize bead picking, or change process ownership. Do not implement the HTTP coordination client. Do not wire Cobra command flows to the journal in this bead beyond package-level production APIs and tests.

PARENT
- ddx-635ae251.

DEPS
- No deps.

description:
PROBLEM
The worker self-healing fixes need an end-to-end proof that one project can fail while other supervised projects continue reconciling.

ROOT CAUSE WITH FILE:LINE
SupervisorRegistry.ReconcileAll already iterates projects with per-project error isolation, but the combined failure modes from this plan are not covered by one multi-project regression. Prior incidents crossed DDx, Cayce, Snorri, and Pqueue-shaped projects.

PROPOSED FIX
Add a multi-project integration test fixture with four project roots. Seed one stale blocked terminal, one unresolved preserved-review bead using Bead.Extra markers, one resource-exhausted terminal, and one empty queue. Prove reconcile restarts eligible desired workers, does not reclaim unresolved preserved-review work, surfaces resource attention with backoff, and continues other projects independently.

NON-SCOPE
Do not require real external providers or network. Use fakes/stubs for worker launches where possible.
title: Prove multi-project worker self-healing end to end

  The execute-bead subsystem files use execute_bead_* naming that conflates the orchestrator, the attempt, the review, and the loop under one prefix, making package boundaries and import graphs ambiguous. The refactor proposal was stored at /tmp/ and is unreadable post-session.

ROOT CAUSE
  cli/internal/agent/execute_bead_loop.go (drain loop), cli/internal/agent/execute_bead.go (attempt), cli/internal/agent/execute_bead_orchestrator.go (land coordinator), cli/internal/agent/execute_bead_land.go (landing), cli/internal/agent/execute_bead_review.go (review), cli/internal/agent/execute_bead_review_triage.go (review triage), cli/internal/agent/execute_bead_status.go (disposition), and cli/internal/agent/executions_mirror.go (mirror) all share a flat package with unrelated concerns. The ddx try CLI command named in FEAT-010 does not exist (cli/cmd/try.go absent).

PROPOSED FIX
  Rename per the following table (no behavior change):
    cli/internal/agent/execute_bead.go             -> cli/internal/agent/try/attempt.go (already exists; merge or verify)
    cli/internal/agent/execute_bead_orchestrator.go -> cli/internal/agent/try/land.go
    cli/internal/agent/execute_bead_land.go         -> cli/internal/agent/try/coordinator.go
    cli/internal/agent/execute_bead_review.go       -> cli/internal/agent/try/review.go
    cli/internal/agent/execute_bead_review_triage.go -> cli/internal/agent/try/review_triage.go
    cli/internal/agent/execute_bead_status.go       -> cli/internal/agent/try/disposition.go
    cli/internal/agent/execute_bead_loop.go         -> cli/internal/agent/work/drain.go
    cli/internal/agent/executions_mirror.go         -> cli/internal/agent/try/mirror.go

  Rename identifiers: ExecuteBeadWorker -> work.Worker, ExecuteBeadWorker.Run -> work.Worker.Drain, ExecuteBead -> try.Attempt (FEAT-006 + FEAT-010).

  Add cli/cmd/try.go with cobra command "ddx try <bead-id>" invoking try.Attempt directly (FEAT-010 surface).

  Update FEAT-006 and FEAT-010 spec docs to reflect new package paths. Keep ExecuteBead* shims as typedefs; deletion is C14.

NON-SCOPE
  - Behavior changes to the drain loop or attempt logic.
  - Deletion of ExecuteBead* typedefs (C14).
  - ddx-dc157075 file-path reference migration if that bead has not yet landed.

INTERSECTIONS
- P2: file and identifier names should reflect the subsystem boundary and keep responsibilities separated.
- P5: ddx try as a first-class CLI surface makes the worker/attempt state easier for operators to see.
- P7: the refactor aligns names and prompt surface with the bead-as-prompt contract.

description:
PROBLEM
When /tmp inode exhaustion occurs, DDx currently reports ENOSPC or resource_exhausted without naming the directories consuming inodes. Operators had to manually run df/find/du to discover that ddx-home-* and ddx-claim-heartbeats were responsible. This slows recovery and hides whether cleanup is effective.

ROOT CAUSE WITH FILE:LINE
cli/internal/agent/execution_resources.go:250-267 enforces resource thresholds on known roots but does not collect top inode-consuming children for the failing root.
cli/internal/agent/execution_resources.go:309-323 collapses writable probe failures into generic messages, and later resource_exhausted payloads lack a compact per-root top-consumer list.
cli/internal/agent/execution_cleanup.go:140-168 has structured summary fields, but no standard observation for top inode consumers after cleanup/preflight failure.

PROPOSED FIX
When resource preflight fails for ENOSPC, low inode count, or EMFILE-adjacent temp creation failures, attach a bounded top-inode-consumers diagnostic for the failing root. The diagnostic should include child path, file/dir entry count, byte size if cheap, age/mtime, and whether the child matches a DDx-owned cleanup prefix. Keep the scan bounded and avoid recursively walking untrusted huge trees without limits.

IN-SCOPE FILES
- cli/internal/agent/execution_resources.go
- cli/internal/agent/execution_resources_test.go
- cli/internal/agent/execution_cleanup.go only if shared diagnostic structs live there
- cli/internal/server or cmd rendering only if existing JSON/text reports need pass-through

NON-SCOPE
Do not delete anything in this bead. Do not change resource threshold values. Do not perform unbounded full-filesystem scans. Do not include sensitive file contents; paths and counts only.

description:
PROBLEM
Docker-clone attempts currently make DDx responsible for installing concrete Claude, Codex, and Gemini binaries, copying their private credentials and settings, selecting provider environment-variable prefixes, and seeding provider-specific Fizeau quota caches. This duplicates Fizeau runtime knowledge and becomes stale whenever Fizeau adds or changes a harness.

ROOT CAUSE WITH FILE:LINE
- cli/internal/agent/attempt_backend.go:263-280 prepares a DDx-owned synthetic home for the embedded runtime.
- cli/internal/agent/attempt_backend.go:290-347 constructs the container invocation and calls dockerToolMounts before dispatch.
- cli/internal/agent/attempt_backend.go:803-871 applies DDx-owned tool mounts and credential environment forwarding.
- cli/internal/agent/attempt_backend.go:902-914 hard-codes claude, codex, and gemini binary discovery.
- cli/internal/agent/attempt_backend.go:941-975 copies Codex and Claude credentials/settings plus Claude, Codex, and Gemini Fizeau quota snapshots.
- cli/internal/agent/attempt_backend.go:1002-1020 hard-codes Anthropic, Codex, Fizeau, Gemini, Google, OpenAI, and OpenRouter environment prefixes.
- Fizeau bead fizeau-725d478d owns the missing public portable-runtime materialization seam; fizeau-b9a2037c must publish that seam in the pinned module before DDx consumes it.

PROPOSED FIX
Pin the released Fizeau version containing PreparePortableRuntime or its final public equivalent. During Docker workspace preparation, ask Fizeau to materialize one complete route-neutral runtime bundle under the attempt runtime root. Store only the returned opaque generic mount/environment/cleanup plan. Apply returned mounts and environment names byte-for-byte without inspecting, filtering, naming, or selecting a harness/provider/model. Invoke bundle cleanup during normal cleanup and failed preparation. Delete dockerToolMounts, provider-specific home copies, provider environment prefixes, and all concrete harness/credential/quota strings from the Docker backend. Retain DDx-owned container identity, worktree mount, prompt path, DDX correlation variables, resource limits, project caches, network selection, candidate transport, and DDx container cleanup.

NON-SCOPE
Do not design or duplicate the portable-runtime contract in DDx, choose a concrete route from bundle contents, make Fizeau own DDx worktrees/container resource policy/verification/landing/tracker state, remove provider-process supervision or text classification before separately pinned v0.15 guarantees, bake credentials into images, or emit secrets in evidence.

PARENT
ddx-b8cacbeb.

DEPS
ddx-98e9fe56 establishes route-neutral Fizeau-only dispatch. fizeau#fizeau-725d478d supplies the opaque portable runtime contract. fizeau#fizeau-b9a2037c publishes it in the supported module and is the structured external blocker.
notes: Fizeau v0.15 pin and public conformance are centralized in ddx-00d406ce; this consumer must not repin Fizeau independently.

description:
<context-digest>
<principles>Spec-first development · Executable specifications · Audit trail required · Work is a DAG · Drift is debt · Inspect and adapt</principles>
<concerns>go-std | security-owasp | testing</concerns>
<practices>Go domain interface with contract tests against real implementations · project-scoped durable files · no call-recording mocks · go test + lefthook</practices>

<governing>FEAT-006 Worker Contract: connected mutations use the server; disconnected manual workers apply the same operations locally and reconcile before new online writes.</governing>
</context-digest>

PROBLEM
Execution code has no transport-neutral coordination domain contract for claims, lease/transition handling, or landing outcomes, so the later connected and offline implementations cannot share behavioral guarantees.

ROOT CAUSE WITH FILE:LINE
cli/cmd/try.go:256-259 and cli/cmd/execute_loop_shared.go:280-282 construct NewLocalLandCoordinator directly. cli/internal/agent/workerprobe/probe.go:129-224 owns only connection state and an in-memory event buffer, not typed coordination requests, outcomes, or idempotency semantics.

PROPOSED FIX
Add a coordination domain package under cli/internal/agent that defines typed claim/lease, tracker-transition, and landing request/outcome APIs plus a behavioral contract suite. Add the first real local implementation path sufficient for the contract tests to exercise claim contention, tracker transition, landing, and idempotent already-applied outcomes against a real bead store and git repository.

NON-SCOPE
Do not add server routes, wire Cobra commands, centralize bead picking, or change process ownership. Do not implement the HTTP coordination client in this bead. Do not implement the durable offline journal or cross-process offline lock here except for interfaces needed by the contract.

PARENT
- ddx-635ae251.

description:
PROBLEM
`ddx doctor` still reports DDx package-layer topology instead of checking whether required marketplace skills/plugins are available. Current code at `cli/cmd/doctor.go:292-298` prints `Checking Skill Install Topology` and calls `reportSkillInstallTopology`; `cli/cmd/doctor.go:432-462` reports `Global Install` and `Project Install` for `.ddx/plugins/ddx`. The new product requirement is for doctor to check configured plugin marketplace skill availability for `ddx`, `helix`, and `easel-skills`, and suggest installing missing ones.

ROOT CAUSE
Doctor is coupled to the old DDx package install model. It has no loader for marketplace requirements from the ddx-library package config and no deterministic availability checker for marketplace-installed skills.

PROPOSED FIX
- Replace the Skill Install Topology section in `cli/cmd/doctor.go:292-298` with a `Plugin Marketplace Skills` check.
- Load required marketplace plugin requirements from the active ddx library package config added by dependency bead `ddx-7abf3a7a`. Resolve package config from project/global/baked-in DDx package layers, but use those layers only to find config, not as the success signal for skill availability.
- Implement deterministic availability checks from the configured hints, for example scanning explicit skill directories and/or plugin metadata paths declared in config. The exact sources must be documented in the code and tests; do not shell out to `npx` during doctor.
- When config is unreadable or absent, use a small baked-in fallback containing `ddx`, `helix`, and `easel-skills`, and print that fallback requirements are being used so stale config is visible.
- Missing marketplace skills/plugins should be warning-level and exit 0; a broken legacy symlink may remain fatal only if the existing legacy-symlink guard still detects harmful project-local state.

NON-SCOPE
- Do not install marketplace plugins from doctor. Print install commands only.
- Do not hardcode the normal requirement list in doctor when package config is readable.
- Do not remove `ddx install` command registration in this bead; sibling bead `cli: remove top-level ddx install commands` owns that.

DEPS
Depends on ddx-7abf3a7a for typed package config.

description:
PROBLEM
An attempt that has done all its work can fail at the last step when a sibling advances the shared branch:
  land advancer: fast-forwarding refs/heads/main to merge commit d9c2f86...:
  git update-ref refs/heads/main: cannot lock ref 'refs/heads/main':
  is at 88ed449... but expected 7b95380...: exit status 128
  status: land_retry
The work survives on a refs/ddx/iterations/... ref and the bead stays claimable, but `ddx try` is single-shot so tryExitCodeForStatus (cli/cmd/try.go:590) maps land_retry to exit 2 and the caller sees a hard failure.

There is a second, more serious implication: this update-ref runs INSIDE withMainGitLock. If the lock were doing its job, refs/heads/main could not move underneath it.

ROOT CAUSE
cli/internal/agent/execute_bead_land.go:1564 hard-fails when UpdateRefTo(expected=lockedTip) loses the compare-and-swap. The same loop already handles the pre-merge equivalent correctly: at approximately line 1493, `lockedTip != prep.currentTip` sets `retry = true; continue`. The post-merge CAS loss is the same recoverable condition and should take the same path.

Separately, the ref moved while the main git lock was held. Either:
  (a) something mutates refs/heads/main outside withMainGitLock, or
  (b) lockmetrics.SharedTrackerLockPath resolves to a different lock directory for --attempt-backend local-clone attempts than for worktree attempts, splitting the lock domain so two attempts believe they hold "the" lock.
(b) is plausible because the default attempt backend recently changed to local-clone (01ea8b7de).

PROPOSED FIX
- cli/internal/agent/execute_bead_land.go:1564 — on CAS loss, set retry and continue the land loop, mirroring the pre-merge handling near line 1493, bounded by the existing retry cap.
- Determine whether (a) or (b) explains the ref moving under the lock, and fix that. If (b), make the lock path independent of attempt backend so all attempts on one project share one lock domain.

NON-SCOPE
- Do not make `ddx try` itself retry the whole attempt; only the land loop's CAS step is in scope.
- Do not change land semantics for the non-concurrent case.

description:
<context-digest>
<principles>Spec-first development · Executable specifications · Audit trail required · Work is a DAG · Drift is debt · Inspect and adapt</principles>
<concerns>go-std | security-owasp | testing</concerns>
<practices>Go domain interface with contract tests against real implementations · project-scoped durable files · no call-recording mocks · go test + lefthook</practices>
<adrs>ADR-022 rev 6 requires one reconnecting coordination client, durable ordered offline journal, idempotency keys, and a cross-process offline project lock.</adrs>
<governing>FEAT-006 Worker Contract: connected mutations use the server; disconnected manual workers apply the same operations locally and reconcile before new online writes.</governing>
</context-digest>

PROBLEM
workerprobe knows Connected versus NotConnected and buffers events, but execution code has no transport-neutral coordination abstraction or durable offline mutation journal. Each CLI invocation therefore constructs its own local land coordinator.

ROOT CAUSE WITH FILE:LINE
cli/internal/agent/workerprobe/probe.go:129-224 owns only connection state and an in-memory event buffer. cli/cmd/try.go:256-259 and cli/cmd/execute_loop_shared.go:280-282 construct NewLocalLandCoordinator directly. No durable idempotency-keyed coordination record exists.

PROPOSED FIX
- Add a coordination domain package under cli/internal/agent with typed claim/lease, tracker-transition, and landing requests/outcomes.
- Add a durable project-scoped ordered offline journal with monotonic sequence, idempotency key, payload hash, precondition, outcome, and acknowledged-through compaction.
- Add a real local implementation that holds a cross-process project coordination lock and uses existing bead-store/landing implementations.
- Define one behavioral contract suite that runs against the local implementation and the later HTTP implementation.

NON-SCOPE
Do not add server routes, wire Cobra commands, centralize bead picking, or change process ownership.

PARENT
- ddx-635ae251.

DEPS
- No deps.

- cli/internal/bead/factory.go:56 adapts *lifecycle.WatcherHub through lifecycleSubscriber; callers should only see bead.LifecycleSubscriber.

description:
PROBLEM
Concurrent stale breakers can classify the same canonical main-git lock from independent stale snapshots and both mutate it, because observation and mutation of the canonical lock are not serialized across processes. The crash-safe guard primitive now exists but is not held around the observe+mutate transition, and guard contention does not yet consume the retry budget or surface a bounded timeout.

ROOT CAUSE WITH FILE:LINE
cli/internal/agent/tracker_lock.go:238-278 (withTrackerLockPolicy) classifies the existing lock object and, via breakStaleTrackerLock, removes or renames it with no cross-process transition guard. cli/internal/agent/tracker_lock.go:309-328 (breakStaleTrackerLock) reads pid/acquired_at and os.RemoveAll(lockDir) without serializing observation and mutation across processes. The LockRetryPolicy budget (MaxRetries/MaxElapsed) at cli/internal/agent/tracker_lock.go:251-254 governs canonical acquisition but not guard contention.

GOVERNING ARTIFACT
Phase 0 WB-5 single-winner cross-process stale-break protocol: docs/helix/06-iterate/phase0-stop-the-self-harm-plan-2026-07-13.md:124-132.

PROPOSED FIX
Acquire the crash-safe guard (from the guard-primitive child) immediately before the classify+break transition and release it immediately after, so only one process at a time observes-and-mutates the canonical lock. The guard MUST NOT be held across the ordinary os.Mkdir happy-path acquisition, pid/acquired_at metadata publication, the fn callback, the retry sleep, git/harness operations, or private tombstone removal — only across the observe+break critical section. Guard contention consumes the same LockRetryPolicy MaxRetries/MaxElapsed budget already threaded through the loop; on deadline, return TrackerLockTimeoutError (via lockTimeoutError) without invoking fn and without mutating the canonical lock. Reuse trackerLockContendedAttemptHook-style determinism for tests where needed.

NON-SCOPE
This child does NOT implement the guard type, its Unix/Windows advisory-lock backends, or the sidecar path helper (owned by the guard-primitive child and consumed here). It does NOT touch synthesizeCommitExcludePathspecs, preDispatchCheckpointIgnoredPath, or checkoutSyncDeferralIgnoredPath (owned by the ignore-wiring child). Do not change tracker record format, trackerLockStaleAge, LockRetryPolicy defaults, lockmetrics caps, harness/Fizeau behavior, bead-store locks, git index locks, or the execution-cleanup lock in cli/internal/agent/execution_cleanup_loop.go:116-156. Do not extract a shared lock package; Phase 1 WB-8 owns unification. Do not implement token-bearing lease release.

PARENT
ddx-1c8d9319

DEPS
Sibling guard-primitive child (crash-safe main-git transition guard primitive with sidecar path helper) — provides the guard type and path helper consumed here.
