description:
PROBLEM
Parent bead ddx-24949caf is too broad for one execution pass. This child owns part 3 of 3 of that parent scope.

ROOT CAUSE
PROBLEM: Restarting the DDx user service during active supervised work can hang until systemd times out, leaving systemd to SIGKILL server child processes. Live evidence from 2026-07-07 03:05:19 EDT: `ddx server stop` did not return until systemd marked `ddx-server.service` failed with `Result: timeout` and killed leftover git subprocesses, interrupting the Axon worker attempt that was in post-execution handling.

ROOT CAUSE WITH FILE:LINE: `cli/internal/server/server.go:379-385` cancels the supervisor and then waits on `supervisorDone` with no timeout. Worker cleanup is only reached afterward at `cli/internal/server/server.go:388-395`. The worker shutdown path itself has a bounded wait (`cli/internal/server/workers.go:1696-1703`), but it is unreachable while the supervisor goroutine is stuck in a reconcile/git operation. The installed systemd unit generated from `cli/cmd/server_service.go:26-42` has no explicit stop timeout or ExecStop mitigation, so the default systemd timeout eventually kills the whole cgroup.

PROPOSED FIX: Make server shutdown bounded and ordered so worker cleanup always runs promptly even when supervisor reconciliation is slow or stuck. A good implementation is to cancel the supervisor, wait only a short bounded grace for `supervisorDone`, continue to `supervisorRegistry.Shutdown()` / `workers.Shutdown()` on timeout, and surface/log the supervisor timeout without preventing worker cleanup.

NON-SCOPE: Do not rewrite worker execution semantics, change bead claim/lease policy, or alter unrelated service install behavior.

Parent: none. Dependencies: none.

PROPOSED FIX
Implement only this child acceptance slice:
- `cd cli && go test ./internal/server/... ./cmd/...` exits 0.
- `lefthook run pre-commit` exits 0.

description:
ExecuteBeadWorker.Run() is a 700-line function with 24 returns: 4 legitimate terminal exits, 1 legacy idle-loop exit, 1 routing-preflight-kills-worker exit, and 18 store-error escalations from the same handleOutcomeStoreError pattern repeated across outcome paths. The implicit state machine in the loop is real and coherent (Pick -> Gate -> Claim -> Execute -> Classify -> Reviewing -> Terminal) but written as conditional soup instead of explicit state.

## Three-package split aligned to FEAT-010

  cli/internal/agent/run/   - Layer 1: invocation atom (existing dispatch + runner)
  cli/internal/agent/try/   - Layer 2: bead attempt (worktree, prompt, single Execute, Land, conflict-recovery, post-merge review, triage)
  cli/internal/agent/work/  - Layer 3: queue drain (pick, claim, heartbeat, drain-loop control, stop conditions)

try.Attempt(beadID) returns sealed Outcome { Disposition (enum), Cooldown, ParkReason, RecordEvents }. Loop becomes approximately 30 lines: pick -> guard -> claim -> attemptWithHeartbeat -> applyOutcome. Single commitOutcome helper deletes the 18 store-error returns.

## Ordering: refactor-LAST per user decision

In-flight Group A beads (c6e3db02 rate-limit, b24e9630 no_changes, cfedee8e ladder wire, a8718bec cost-cap reviewer) land first against current code. dc157075 tactical worker-stay-alive lands first as operational bridge. The stdout/watch-mode beads (ddx-7d9e1e82, ddx-f9acb86d, ddx-7dcbd40b, ddx-8b7ed960, ddx-dc300be9) define the public work-loop contract this refactor must preserve. THIS refactor lands last and absorbs all intervening behavior into the new architecture. Per-child ACs explicitly call out which in-flight bead's behavior each child must preserve.

## Naming and public semantics

Package = try (not try_bead - Go idiom). Function = try.Attempt(beadID). Loop = work.Worker.Drain. CLI surface is ddx run / ddx try / ddx work. ddx work has three modes: once (one ready bead then exit), drain (default: run ready work until no execution-ready beads remain, then exit), and watch (stay alive indefinitely, sleep for idle interval when no execution-ready beads exist, and poll for newly arriving work). The removed polling flag is not preserved as a public compatibility alias; the durable vocabulary is mode plus idle_interval.

## Children

  C0  Pre-refactor JSONL fixture baseline for event-shape regression detection
  C1  try.Outcome sealed sum type + Disposition enum + ParkReason vocabulary enumeration
  C2  try.Attempt function shell (wraps existing executor; no behavior change)
  C3  Move review verdict handling into try.Attempt (180 lines from loop body)
  C4  Move conflict recovery into try.Attempt
  C5  Move no_changes adjudication, decomposition, push-failed, push-conflict (absorbs ddx-b24e9630, ddx-c6e3db02 behavior)
  C6  Single commitOutcome helper; deletes 18 store-error exit paths + handleOutcomeStoreError
  C7  Uniform Guard contract; delete attempted/hookFailed maps; pick() derives from drain.result
  C8  Routing preflight moves to Drain startup (runs once, not per iteration)
  C9  First-class StopCondition enum + cost-cap relocation + downstream-consumer audit for execution_failed:max-cost grep before relocation. Includes queue snapshot plumbing and human-review blocker pressure from ddx-7dcbd40b.
  C10 ddx work once/drain/watch modes + transient idle substate. Watch mode owns idle interval sleeps, per-idle queue status, and next-ready transition messaging from ddx-f9acb86d and ddx-8b7ed960.
  C11 Heartbeat extracted to withHeartbeat helper
  C12 Single phase-event emission (replaces 4 sites)
  C13 File and identifier rename per package split + ADD ddx try CLI command + handle dc157075 file-path migration if it landed first
  C14 Delete ExecuteBead* shims; verify all callers ported off (grep audit)

description:
PROBLEM
DDx has no canonical durable run-record schema for .ddx/runs/<run-id>/record.json. The server still treats run records as a local GraphQL projection detail, so workers cannot publish a stable record before dispatch.

ROOT CAUSE WITH FILE:LINE
cli/internal/server/state_runs.go:15-55 defines a server-private legacy runRecord tied to .ddx/exec/runs, while docs/helix/06-iterate/phase3-server-rebuild-plan-2026-07-13.md:104-149 requires a versioned .ddx/runs/<run-id>/record.json substrate with typed lifecycle state, DDx correlation, optional opaque Fizeau public-result fields, evidence pointers, and no provider process internals. There is no schema-owning package in cli/internal/agent.

PROPOSED FIX
Create a small package under cli/internal/agent for the v1 run-record data model. Include version, run ID, bead ID, attempt ID, lifecycle phase values, timestamps, typed outcome fields, optional opaque Fizeau public-result fields such as public session/result references, and evidence links. Keep the package neutral about concrete harness routing policy. Add JSON round-trip tests and negative tests proving provider raw output, provider PID, provider process-tree metadata, and provider-session canonical-state fields are not represented in the v1 schema.

NON-SCOPE
Do not query provider sessions for canonical state, build the UI migration, implement legacy migration, choose a Fizeau route, add CLI runs list/show verbs, repoint GraphQL read paths, migrate .ddx/exec/runs, .ddx/exec-runs, or .ddx/executions, implement recovery transitions, or add the atomic publish helper beyond what tests need to serialize records.

GOVERNING ARTIFACT
docs/helix/06-iterate/phase3-server-rebuild-plan-2026-07-13.md:104-149, WB-2 run substrate.

PARENT
ddx-61c41896. Upstream parent field from original bead: ddx-5bf0f8d0.

DEPS
Phase 1 typed Fizeau result contract and Phase 0 safe execution exit.

description:
PROBLEM
`ddx doc prose` is broken for every user who has Vale 3.x installed. Every real Vale invocation dies:
  E100 [vocab] Runtime error
  'config/vocabularies/Project' directory does not exist
  Execution stopped with code 1.
The failure is invisible in CI because CI never installs vale, so the runner falls back to the embedded checker (ValeDiagnosticMissing, cli/cmd/doc_prose.go:108-113). Only real users hit it.

ROOT CAUSE
cli/internal/docprose/valeconfig.go:59 writes the project vocabulary to <StylesPath>/Vocab/<name>/. Vale 3.x moved vocabularies to <StylesPath>/config/vocabularies/<name>/. Because the packaged default vocabulary is non-empty (library/checks/prose-quality/check.yaml, accept: [DDx, bead, execution, Helix, Fizeau]), vocabName is always "Project" and the generated INI always emits `Vocab = Project` (valeconfig.go:56-72 and :94) — so every invocation references a directory that is never created at the path Vale looks in.

Verified by hand against vale 3.13.0 (the pinned SupportedValeVersion, cli/internal/docprose/vale_runner.go:13): styles/Vocab/Project reproduces the E100 above (exit 2); styles/config/vocabularies/Project runs clean (exit 0).

PROPOSED FIX
- cli/internal/docprose/valeconfig.go:59 — write to filepath.Join(stylesDir, "config", "vocabularies", vocabName) instead of filepath.Join(stylesDir, "Vocab", vocabName).
- Update the matching expectations at cli/internal/docprose/valeconfig_test.go:90 and :103.

NON-SCOPE
- Do not address the inert DDx Vale style pack (sister bead: all rules carry `scope: summary` and match nothing in Markdown). Fixing this bead alone yields a clean Vale run that reports no findings; that is expected until the sister bead lands.
- Do not change the embedded checker path or the runner-selection logic.

description:
PROBLEM
DDx has no reusable writer for the initial .ddx/runs/<run-id>/record.json dispatching record, so execute-bead cannot publish a canonical DDx-owned attempt record before Fizeau dispatch.

ROOT CAUSE WITH FILE:LINE
cli/internal/agent/types.go:93-96 exposes OnExecuteStart immediately before FizeauService.Execute, but there is no lower-level run-record schema/writer API that can persist the initial lifecycle phase before that callback. cli/internal/agent/execute_bead.go:1188-1225 already has run ID, bead ID, attempt ID, worker ID, bundle path, prompt path, base revision, session ID, and correlation metadata, but no component converts those values into .ddx/runs/<run-id>/record.json with atomic write and fsync/rename semantics.

PROPOSED FIX
Add a focused run-record schema and writer for the initial dispatching record under .ddx/runs/<run-id>/record.json. The writer must accept stable DDx correlation fields, write valid JSON atomically, fsync/rename into place, and deliberately leave Fizeau harness/provider/model/route/result fields empty until public route/result data exists.

NON-SCOPE
Do not query provider sessions for canonical state, build the UI migration, implement legacy migration, choose a Fizeau route in this child, or wire the writer into execute-bead dispatch beyond unit-level caller tests.

GOVERNING ARTIFACT
docs/helix/06-iterate/phase3-server-rebuild-plan-2026-07-13.md:104-149, WB-2 run substrate.

PARENT
ddx-5bf0f8d0; split from bead context that references ddx-61c41896.

DEPS
Phase 1 typed Fizeau result contract and Phase 0 safe execution exit.

description:

The stale-record cleanup path must still terminate genuinely stale server-managed worker processes. The live-PID preservation regression fix must not weaken cleanup of dead PIDs or safely reclaimable stale leases.

ROOT CAUSE WITH FILE:LINE
cli/internal/server/workers.go:1447-1449 currently sends cleanupManagedWorkerProcessTree before cli/internal/server/workers.go:1451-1467 asks staleDiskEntryCanReleaseClaim whether the claim can be released. Moving classification earlier must preserve the existing reclaim behavior for stale claims that staleDiskEntryCanReleaseClaim allows. cli/internal/server/workers.go:1470-1482 is the stopped-record rewrite path that should remain reachable only after ownership and liveness evidence prove cleanup is safe.

PROPOSED FIX
After introducing pre-cleanup classification, keep the cleanup branch for reclaimable stale claims: terminate the process tree, release the stale bead claim, emit bead.stopped, and mark the disk record stopped. Make the decision explicit so preserved live fresh workers and genuinely reclaimable stale workers have separate test-covered branches.

NON-SCOPE
Do not change desired worker count, generic process cleanup, provider parent-death behavior, or manual/server coordination owned by ddx-635ae251. Do not weaken cleanup of dead PIDs or genuinely stale leases. Do not add supervisor reconciliation duplicate-prevention behavior in this bead.

Split from root regression bead "server: preserve live managed PIDs during stale-record cleanup".

description:
EPIC

Eliminate the .ddx/ footprint from arbitrary git repos using DDx, while keeping today's in-tree behavior available for projects that want it (DDx itself, HELIX, etc.). Make init effectively touchless: zero ceremony for the common case.

DESIGN PRINCIPLE

Single rule: presence of <project>/.ddx/ determines the DDx root.
- If <project>/.ddx/ exists → in-tree mode. Root = <project>/.ddx/. Operator commits or gitignores per their own .gitignore. DDx never manipulates .gitignore.
- If <project>/.ddx/ does NOT exist → convention mode. Root = ${XDG_DATA_HOME}/ddx/projects/<host>/<owner>/<repo>/ (defaults to ~/.local/share/ddx/projects/<host>/<owner>/<repo>/). The XDG directory is itself a git repo containing all DDx state for that project; the project's own git repo stays pristine.

PROJECT ID is the human-readable remote URL host/owner/repo triple, parsed from `git remote get-url origin`. SSH URLs (`git@github.com:easel/ddx.git`) and HTTPS URLs both resolve to the same path. Projects without a remote fall back to `local/<basename>-<abs-path-short-hash>/`. The slashes are filesystem-real, so the XDG path is browsable: `~/.local/share/ddx/projects/github.com/easel/ddx/`.

OVERRIDE PRECEDENCE at command time:
1. In-tree (<project>/.ddx/config.yaml) — top priority
2. Global (${XDG_DATA_HOME}/ddx/global/config.yaml) — installed by `ddx init --global`
3. Convention defaults — baked into the binary

Each layer is a delta on the one below. A project with no overrides commits zero new files and writes zero files into its worktree.

ENGINEERING IMPERATIVE

EVERY path in the codebase that today reads or writes under .ddx/ must route through a single DDxRoot(ctx) resolver. No filepath.Join(projectRoot, ".ddx", ...) calls outside that resolver. A regression linter asserts this invariant. The audit is the hard part of this epic.

KNOWN-HARD QUESTION (worth solving but not blocking):

When multiple worktrees of the same project (same remote URL) exist on one machine — e.g. `~/Projects/ddx` and `~/work/ddx-experiment` — they share the same XDG state. SHAs in events are unambiguous, but operator UX for "where do I cd to inspect this" is. Solution direction: each XDG project keeps a worktrees.json registry. One entry is marked master (operator pin or first-seen). Cross-references in audit logs and bead show output cite the master path.

CHILD BEADS

- E1: config: DDxRoot resolver + audit every .ddx/ path writer
- E2: config: convention mode bootstrap (XDG git repo + worktree registry)
- E3: config: ddx init --global installs user-tier skills/personas
- E4: config: ddx init creates .ddx/ in project, switches to in-tree mode
- E5: config: optional .ddx/config.yaml overlay for per-project overrides

NON-SCOPE
- Migration of existing in-tree repos (today's DDx repo, HELIX) is a separate concern. They stay in-tree mode by virtue of having .ddx/ already.
- Server-backed state (federation) is orthogonal. XDG state can be a git repo with a remote; pushing that remote IS the team-share mechanism.
- Manifest-only mode is rejected — the convention/in-tree split makes a separate manifest file unnecessary.
title: config: XDG-rooted DDx state — convention mode + in-tree mode + touchless init

description:
PROBLEM
Stale breaking for the process-shared main-git lock has no crash-safe single-winner transition guard. Concurrent stale breakers can classify the same canonical lock path from stale snapshots, and a permanent guard sidecar would become runtime dirt unless all DDx git/checkpoint/checkout-sync surfaces ignore it explicitly.

ROOT CAUSE WITH FILE:LINE
cli/internal/agent/tracker_lock.go:215-278 retries os.Mkdir on the canonical lock and classifies existing directories or malformed regular files before mutating the pathname. cli/internal/agent/tracker_lock.go:309-328 reads lock metadata and removes or renames the canonical object without serializing observation and mutation across processes. cli/internal/agent/gitops_real.go:165-205 synthesizes git-add pathspec exclusions, cli/internal/agent/predispatch_dirty.go:477-488 checks pre-dispatch dirt, and cli/internal/agent/execute_bead_land.go:923-931 handles checkout-sync deferral; each must explicitly ignore the stable sidecar independently of project .gitignore state.

GOVERNING ARTIFACT
Phase 0 WB-5 requires a single-winner cross-process stale-break protocol at docs/helix/06-iterate/phase0-stop-the-self-harm-plan-2026-07-13.md:124-132.

PROPOSED FIX
Add a package-local crash-safe transition guard for the process-shared main-git lock. Use a never-deleted sibling advisory-lock file with a deterministic name ending in .lock, plus keyed same-process coordination. The OS lock must release automatically on handle close or process death. Non-contention open/lock errors fail safe. Ordinary acquisition/release must never delete or recreate the sidecar inode/path. Guard contention must consume the existing LockRetryPolicy budget and return TrackerLockTimeoutError on deadline. Add one package-local path constant/helper for the sidecar, and use it from synthesize-commit exclusions, pre-dispatch dirt, and checkout-sync deferral so these surfaces cannot drift. Provide Unix and Windows guard implementations; because the current dependency graph does not cross-compile for Windows, include a self-contained GOOS=windows GOARCH=amd64 go test -c file-list command naming the final guard source/test files.

NON-SCOPE
Do not change tracker mutation semantics, tracker record format, trackerLockStaleAge, LockRetryPolicy defaults, lockmetrics caps, harness/Fizeau behavior, bead-store locks, git index locks, or the separate execution-cleanup lock in cli/internal/agent/execution_cleanup_loop.go:116-156. Do not extract a shared lock package; ddx-dffb7454 and ddx-3f156500 own separate sites and Phase 1 WB-8 owns unification. Do not implement token-bearing lease release or stale directory/file disposal semantics except as needed to exercise guard acquisition/release and ignored-path behavior.

PARENT
ddx-8b22914e

DEPS
None. ddx-dffb7454 is a related collection-lock implementation, not a prerequisite or shared-package dependency.

description:
PROBLEM
The server conflates observation, worker ownership, session-derived run views, and managed coordination. It cannot currently present one durable run truth or a safe managed-worker contract.

ROOT CAUSE WITH FILE:LINE
The governing plan defines observer demotion, an atomic .ddx/runs substrate, and managed-worker reconstruction at docs/helix/06-iterate/phase3-server-rebuild-plan-2026-07-13.md:92-159. Current run reads scan and synthesize session stores, managed and reported workers are merged, and restart behavior is not journal-and-record based.

PROPOSED FIX
First gate every managed-worker spawn while preserving observer repair. Then publish one atomic run record per DDx attempt, migrate all readers, and rebuild managed workers over the existing ADR-022 coordination chain. Provider process cleanup remains Fizeau's responsibility; DDx may stop only DDx-owned worker contexts/processes.

NON-SCOPE
Do not make the server a provider or harness supervisor. Do not infer run truth from provider session directories after the run store exists. Do not preserve fabricated management UI while the backend is disabled.

PARENT
None; root recovery epic.

DEPS
Phase 2 truth exit for public rebuild; Phase 0 exit for safe execution; Phase 1 exit and compatible Fizeau result contract for run lifecycle wiring.

description:
PROBLEM
A Verification mapping row that cites only a test file path — with no specific mapped test, check, or artifact target — reads as evidence to the cardinality join and silently satisfies a requirement that has no pinned proof. Without this exclusion, FEAT-009/FEAT-002/FEAT-012-style documents can pass the coverage gate by pointing at whole files.

ROOT CAUSE WITH FILE:LINE
The spechonesty analyzer package does not exist in this checkout — the expected path cli/tools/lint/spechonesty/analyzer.go:1 is absent (cli/tools/lint/ currently contains only evidencelint, routinglint, runtimelint). The sibling cardinality pass counts any mapping row as coverage, with no granularity predicate distinguishing a bare file path from a row naming a concrete target. The governing contract is docs/helix/06-iterate/phase2-doc-truth-plan-2026-07-13.md:67, which requires coverage by a Verification mapping row rather than an unspecific pointer.

PROPOSED FIX
Add a citation-granularity predicate to the coverage-cardinality pass: a mapping row whose evidence field resolves to a test-file path without an exact mapped test, check, or artifact target does not count as requirement coverage. Such rows are excluded before the cardinality join, so an otherwise-Complete requirement covered only by file-only citations is reported as uncovered by the sibling cardinality diagnostics. Rows naming a concrete target are unaffected. Follow the package and test conventions in cli/tools/lint/evidencelint/analyzer.go and cli/tools/lint/evidencelint/analyzer_test.go, including golang.org/x/tools/go/analysis and analysistest-style fixtures where applicable. The analyzer is read-only.

NON-SCOPE
Do not implement the zero-evidence (empty row set) diagnostic — that is the sibling zero-evidence child. Do not implement the uncovered/duplicate cardinality diagnostics themselves — that is the sibling cardinality child; this child only supplies the exclusion predicate feeding it. Do not handle waivers — that is the waiver child. Do not parse requirement inventories or mapping tables — that is the mapping-parser child. Do not implement status parsing — that is the scaffold child. Do not auto-restamp documents, infer proof from prose, fetch network state, or mark aspirational metrics complete. Duplicate-id and stale-observation detection are a sibling child. Prose quality and AC numbering style are out of scope. Do not resolve whether named Test* symbols, static checks, or artifacts actually exist on disk — evidence-target resolution is a sibling child; this child only inspects whether the row names a target at all. Do not enforce the executable verification command allowlist — command allowlist enforcement is a sibling child.

DEPS: parent ddx-29449fa5 (and its parent ddx-471d66b6); the spechonesty scaffold/status-parser child; the Verification mapping-parser child that provides the inventory + rows model; the sibling coverage-cardinality child. GOVERNING ARTIFACT: docs/helix/06-iterate/phase2-doc-truth-plan-2026-07-13.md WB-1 steps 3-4.

description:
<context-digest>
<principles>Spec-first development · Executable specifications · Audit trail required · Work is a DAG · Drift is debt · Inspect and adapt</principles>
<concerns>go-std | security-owasp | testing</concerns>
<practices>Cobra CommandFactory · project-scoped localhost HTTP APIs · real server/git/bead-store integration tests · go test + golangci-lint + lefthook</practices>
<adrs>ADR-022 rev 6: all workers are autonomous and server-preferred; connected coordination mutations serialize through the server, disconnected manual workers journal and reconcile, managed workers terminate with the server.</adrs>
<governing>FEAT-002 Worker Boundaries and FEAT-006 Worker Contract require one coordination protocol for manual and managed workers.</governing>
</context-digest>

PROBLEM
Manual ddx try/work commands and server-managed workers currently construct separate process-local land coordinators. The existing workerprobe reconnects and backfills observability only. When both paths run against one project, each process can believe it is the single writer, causing tracker and landing conflicts.

ROOT CAUSE WITH FILE:LINE
cli/cmd/try.go:232-259 and cli/cmd/execute_loop_shared.go:254-282 wire workerprobe only as an event tee and unconditionally create NewLocalLandCoordinator. cli/internal/agent/workerprobe/probe.go:1-12 explicitly limits server communication to best-effort event mirroring. cli/internal/server/land_coordinator.go:91-110 provides process-local serialization only.

PROPOSED FIX
Implement ADR-022 rev 6 in four bounded children: shared coordination client and offline journal; project-scoped server mutation/reconcile endpoints; uniform try/work/managed wiring; and real integration coverage.

NON-SCOPE
Do not centralize the picker, replace the bead store or git history, change Fizeau routing, or keep server-managed processes alive after server death.

PARENT
Root epic.

DEPS
No deps.

description:
PROBLEM
BuildDDxBinary and BuildDDxFizeauTestSeamBinary create process-lifetime binary directories shared through sync.Once but publish the binary path without any durable owner marker. After ddx-b2702b9f moves both directories beneath configured execution scratch, cleanup cannot tell an abandoned directory from one still owned by a live test process because the producer emits no ownership evidence.

ROOT CAUSE WITH FILE:LINE
cli/internal/testutils/fixture_repo.go:87-95 stores both built binary paths in process-wide sync.Once state.
cli/internal/testutils/fixture_repo.go:119-167 creates the two binary directories and caches/returns the binary path without writing a process-lifetime owner marker.

PROPOSED FIX
Using the internal/scratchowner contract, have BuildDDxBinary and BuildDDxFizeauTestSeamBinary write a live-owner marker immediately after creating each directory and before the binary path is cached or returned. If marker creation fails, remove the newly created directory and fail the build helper instead of publishing an unowned path. Preserve the existing sync.Once process-wide binary cache; do not switch to t.TempDir.

IN-SCOPE FILES
- cli/internal/testutils/fixture_repo.go and fixture_repo_test.go

NON-SCOPE
Do not change execution_cleanup.go recognition or reclamation logic; child bead ddx (cleanup wiring) owns that.
Do not replace the process-wide sync.Once binary cache with t.TempDir.
Do not change Fizeau routing, test-seam behavior, harness selection, model selection, or provider policy.
Do not change execution scratch placement; ddx-b2702b9f owns that migration.

PARENT
ddx-f914dddd

DEPS
Sibling bead ddx (internal/scratchowner marker contract) must land first so the marker type exists.
ddx-b2702b9f must land first so both producers use the configured scratch root.

description:
PROBLEM
The candidate-cycle abstraction has deterministic Checks and Repair seams, but production wires only Reviewer. The real repository gate runs after LLM review and a failure immediately preserves the candidate; the existing RepairContext is ignored. DDx therefore neither checks before review nor asks Fizeau to repair a fixable gate failure in the same attempt workspace.

ROOT CAUSE WITH FILE:LINE
- cli/internal/agent/execute_bead.go:376-389 constructs applyWorkerCandidateCycle with Reviewer and NoReview while Checks and Repair are nil.
- cli/cmd/execute_loop_shared.go:475-491 and cli/cmd/try.go:452-467 run checks after candidate review.
- cli/internal/agent/execute_bead_loop.go:390-467 preserves a failed repository gate without a repair operation.
- cli/internal/agent/execute_bead_post_review.go:398-417 creates RepairContext, but execute_bead_loop.go:4207-4236 does not execute it.
- cli/internal/agent/repair_prompt.go:8-70 lacks the full original task, current diff, and deterministic failure output required for an executable repair request.

PROPOSED FIX
Wire the production candidate cycle so deterministic repository checks run before review. On a fixable check or review failure, submit a fresh public Fizeau Execute operation in the same DDx attempt worktree using the original task, current diff, and failure evidence. Preserve the primary operation MinPower and immutable operator passthrough exactly; do not set a concrete route. Append the repair commit, rerun checks, then review. Keep the repair budget bounded and durable in attempt evidence.

NON-SCOPE
Do not invent or call a Continue or resume API, invoke a provider CLI, raise power inside the current attempt, change Fizeau internals, or implement new-attempt escalation policy.

PARENT AND DEPS
Parent: ddx-b8cacbeb. Depends on ddx-8bcf71e0 so repair inherits the route-neutral reviewer and immutable passthrough contract.

description:
PROBLEM
Parent bead ddx-53df5e2f requires post-migration verification by reading migrated beads back from Axon/Postgres and checking field fidelity. That verification should be independently testable from write-path and CLI routing work.

ROOT CAUSE WITH FILE:LINE
The importer enables verification through MigrateAxonOptions.Verify at cli/internal/bead/import_postgres.go:38 and calls verifyImportedAxonCorpus from cli/internal/bead/import_postgres.go:113 after writes. If the verifier is absent or shallow, ddx bead migrate --to-axon --verify can report success even when Axon data drifts from the JSONL source corpus.

PROPOSED FIX
Implement or complete verifyImportedAxonCorpus and supporting comparison helpers so --verify reads back the Axon target, compares migrated source beads field-for-field for the imported corpus, detects drift with an error naming the affected bead ID and field, and passes cleanly after a normal import. For large corpora, keep the implementation compatible with sample-based verification if the existing codebase already has a corpus-size threshold; otherwise compare the bounded imported set produced by --limit or full import.

NON-SCOPE
- Schema-versioning migration ladder; deferred until first v1-to-v2 breaking change.
- Real-wire integration test against actual Postgres; separate WIRE bead.
- Continuous sync between JSONL and Postgres.
- CLI flag parsing beyond consuming the Verify option; sibling child owns command UX.
- Core apply/idempotency mechanics except as needed to create verifier fixtures; sibling child owns apply path.
- Do not claim or edit parent bead ddx-53df5e2f tracker data manually; tracker mutations must go through ddx bead commands.

description:
PROBLEM
DDx has no reusable crash-safe publisher for the initial .ddx/runs/<run-id>/record.json dispatching record, so execute-bead cannot publish a canonical DDx-owned attempt record before Fizeau dispatch.

ROOT CAUSE WITH FILE:LINE
cli/internal/agent/types.go:93-96 exposes OnExecuteStart immediately before FizeauService.Execute, but there is no lower-level run-record schema/writer API that can persist the initial lifecycle phase before that callback. cli/internal/agent/execute_bead.go:1188-1225 already has the values needed to identify the run, but no component atomically creates .ddx/runs/<run-id>/record.json using temp-file, fsync, rename, and directory fsync semantics.

description:
PROBLEM
Runtime artifact validation must inspect current-revision evidence without modifying documents or fixture files. A linter that mutates fixtures or source documents while checking Verification rows would violate the spechonesty analyzer contract and make validation unsafe to run in pre-commit.

ROOT CAUSE WITH FILE:LINE
The spechonesty analyzer path is absent in this checkout at cli/tools/lint/spechonesty/analyzer.go:1, and the analyzer run has no runtime-artifact existence check over parsed Verification rows. Current-revision executable verification is reinforced at docs/helix/06-iterate/phase2-doc-truth-plan-2026-07-13.md:176.

PROPOSED FIX
Add explicit read-only coverage around the runtime artifact validation path in the spechonesty analyzer. The validation should consume parsed Verification rows and the runtime artifact resolver, emit diagnostics in memory, and leave all fixture and document files unchanged after the run.

NON-SCOPE
Do not change diagnostic content beyond what is required to exercise read-only validation. Do not reimplement target classification or path resolution — consume the resolver child. Do not handle waivers — that is the waiver child. Do not parse requirement inventories or mapping tables — that is the mapping-parser child. Do not auto-restamp documents, infer proof from prose, fetch network state, or mark aspirational metrics complete. Status parsing lives in the scaffold child. Duplicate-id and stale-observation detection are a sibling child. Prose quality and AC numbering style are out of scope. Do not enforce requirement coverage cardinality or duplicate mapping counts — the coverage-cardinality child owns that. Do not resolve Go Test* symbols or static check names — the evidence-target child owns those checks. Do not enforce command allowlisting — the verification-command allowlist child owns that.

DEPS: parent ddx-e743ce67; grandparent ddx-29449fa5; root dependency ddx-471d66b6; the spechonesty scaffold/status-parser child; the Verification mapping-parser child that provides the inventory + rows model; the runtime artifact target resolver child. description:
PROBLEM
`cli/internal/bead/watcher.go:23-100` defines and exports `StoreFactory`, `WatcherHub`, and `NewWatcherHub` from the public `bead` package, while `cli/internal/bead/watcher.go:109-224` keeps the polling `projectWatcher` internals in the same public package. TD-027 §21 requires the concrete lifecycle polling hub to sit behind an internal boundary, but callers can still import the public bead package and construct the hub directly.

ROOT CAUSE
The concrete watcher implementation lives in `cli/internal/bead/watcher.go:23-224` instead of `cli/internal/bead/internal/lifecycle/`, so the concrete type and constructor are part of the public `bead` package API. The public interface boundary already exists at `cli/internal/bead/backend.go:144-147`, but the implementation is not separated from it.

PROPOSED FIX
Move the concrete watcher implementation from `cli/internal/bead/watcher.go` to `cli/internal/bead/internal/lifecycle/watcher_hub.go` with package name `lifecycle`. Keep `LifecycleEvent` in the public `bead` package, update the internal lifecycle implementation to reference `bead.LifecycleEvent`, and keep `LifecycleSubscriber` as the public interface. Move or rewrite watcher tests under `cli/internal/bead/internal/lifecycle/` so behavior is proven against the relocated implementation.

Parent: ddx-74452926. Governing artifact: TD-027 §21. No additional parent dependency IDs were supplied.

NON-SCOPE
- Storage backend relocation.
- Caller-field narrowing.
- Boundary import test.
- Lint analyzer cleanup.

description:
PROBLEM
DDx-owned temporary homes, provider shims, and helper scratch are created directly under raw os.TempDir(), so /tmp remains the choke point even when DDx has a configured execution/runtime temp root with available space. The 2026-07-08 incident had /tmp at 100% inode use while the configured execution worktree root under /Users/erik/Projects/.ddx-exec-wt still had capacity.

ROOT CAUSE WITH FILE:LINE
cli/internal/agent/provider_spawn.go:91 creates provider shims with os.MkdirTemp("", "ddx-provider-shim-").
cli/internal/agent/runner_test.go:29 and runner_test.go:56 create ddx-home-* with os.MkdirTemp("", "ddx-home-"); equivalent command tests create the same prefix in cli/cmd/work_resource_exhausted_test.go:80, cli/cmd/try_test.go:823, and cli/cmd/doctor_test.go:85.
cli/internal/testutils/fixture_repo.go:116 creates ddx-fixture-bin-* with os.MkdirTemp("", ...).
These producers bypass config.ExecutionScratchRoot / config.ExecutionWorktreeRoot and strand inode-heavy scratch under /tmp.

PROPOSED FIX
Add a shared helper for DDx-owned scratch temp dirs that prefers config.ExecutionScratchRoot(projectRoot) or the configured execution/runtime root when a project root is available, and falls back to os.TempDir() only when no configured root exists. Migrate provider shims and DDx-owned temp homes/fixture bins to the helper where production/runtime context is available. Keep tests hermetic by setting the helper root explicitly in tests.

IN-SCOPE FILES
- cli/internal/agent/provider_spawn.go
- cli/internal/config/execution_worktree_root.go or a new scratch-temp helper package
- relevant tests in cli/internal/agent and cli/cmd

NON-SCOPE
Do not move claim-liveness in this bead; ddx-3986b89a covers claim heartbeat root selection. Do not change git worktree placement. Do not store long-lived user config in execution scratch. Do not require a project root for all tests; fallback behavior must remain.

description:
PROBLEM

description:
Part of EPIC ddx-42893255. Read ADR-029 first. Depends on hub endpoints (ddx-48c55db2) + identity binding (ddx-26ae40ed).

ROOT CAUSE: ddx work/try run in a separate process from the server and cannot see federation role, node_id (s.state.Node.ID set only in EnableSpokeMode, cli/internal/server/federation_spoke.go:50), or hub URL. So the worker cannot decide to acquire, nor reach the hub with correct identity/TLS.

PROPOSED: Add a worker-facing claim layer routed through the LOCAL server (self-signed cert -> newLocalServerClientTimeout skip-verify, cli/cmd/shared_helpers.go):
- GET /api/federation/self -> {federated:bool, node_id, role}. Worker queries once; non-federated => hard no-op (zero overhead single node).

description:
PROBLEM
When the pre-claim decomposition model returns invalid or empty output, the deterministic fallback can create malformed children that are not independently executable. On 2026-07-13 it split ddx-e6abf4a6 into two partial implementation beads plus a verification-only child, omitted sibling dependencies, duplicated and contradicted the parent context, and failed to place the required package and lefthook gates on every implementation child. An operator had to rewrite and rewire the queue manually.

ROOT CAUSE WITH FILE:LINE
cli/internal/agent/recovery_decompose.go:480-539 chooses child count from the raw number of numbered AC lines and chunks those lines without distinguishing implementation criteria from shared verification gates or dependency order. cli/internal/agent/recovery_decompose.go:587-603 embeds a truncated parent description beneath newly generated PROBLEM and ROOT CAUSE headings, preserving stale PARENT/DEPS text and creating contradictory child prompts. cli/internal/agent/recovery_decompose.go:606-619 adds go test and lefthook only when those strings are absent anywhere in the parent acceptance, so existing gates become their own chunk instead of being copied to each executable child. cli/internal/agent/recovery_decompose.go:456-477 validates only non-empty title, description, and acceptance and therefore accepts children that fail the repository bead-authoring floor.

PROPOSED FIX
Make deterministic fallback fail safe. Separate implementation ACs from shared build gates, copy required go test and lefthook gates to every implementation child, generate standalone child context without nested or contradictory parent headings, and validate every proposed child against an execution-readiness contract before writing any tracker rows. Never create a verification-only child. If the fallback cannot prove standalone scope, complete AC coverage, and safe sibling ordering, do not apply it: leave or park the parent with a durable operator_attention/decomposition event explaining why manual refinement is required. Keep writes atomic so a rejected fallback creates no partial children.

IN-SCOPE FILES
- cli/internal/agent/recovery_decompose.go
- cli/internal/agent/recovery_decompose_test.go
- The nearest shared bead-readiness validator if reuse avoids duplicating the authoring rubric

NON-SCOPE
Do not change model/provider routing, decomposition timeout budgets, worker lifecycle visibility, or generic bead lint policy. Do not infer semantic dependencies from AC ordering when the evidence is ambiguous; use the operator-attention lane instead. Do not repair previously created children in migration code.

PARENT AND DEPS
Parent: none; root queue-integrity regression. Depends on ddx-2afca9c9 because this internal/agent change must pass the restored package-runtime gate.
notes:
Live deterministic-decomposition failures observed on Niflheim, 2026-07-13:
- ddx-9c3e703b was split into two implementation slices plus verification-only ddx-f3d774d3. The implementation children omitted required full-package/lefthook gates and dependencies. The operator rewrote ddx-c4497391 and ddx-03568f89, wired their dependency, and cancelled ddx-f3d774d3.
- ddx-20e2148b split fixture code from regression tripwires but omitted the dependency and full-package gate from ddx-7326dd54. The operator restored the gate and made ddx-e03399c8 depend on it.
- ddx-69672921 contained only three verification commands as its acceptance slice. A managed worker spent 14m26s and 4,137,315 tokens proving its focused regression green before the unrelated full suite timed out. The bead produced no implementation and reopened, demonstrating the direct throughput cost of verification-only children.
These are concrete production examples for TestFallbackPreClaimDecompositionRejectsVerificationOnlyChildren, TestFallbackPreClaimDecompositionProducesExecutionReadyChildren, and atomic rejection of invalid fallback output.

description:
PROBLEM
Since the fizeau v0.15.0 bump (6ba97ef25, 2026-07-20), a zero Result.CostUSD is ambiguous: it can mean "the call genuinely cost nothing" or "cost provenance was unknown and the value was discarded". Nothing downstream can tell these apart, including cost-cap enforcement.

ROOT CAUSE / CURRENT STATE
fizeau v0.15.0 added a custom ServiceFinalData.UnmarshalJSON that refuses to decode cost_usd unless a sibling cost_source field is present (fizeau@v0.15.0/service_cost.go:34-38), deliberately so that "legacy source-less finals" are not promoted to authoritative billing evidence. CostUSD also became *float64 (service_events.go:499).

DDx consumes this at cli/internal/agent/service_run.go:344-346:
    if final.CostUSD != nil && *final.CostUSD > 0 { result.CostUSD = *final.CostUSD }
which is correct as far as it goes — but DDx never reads final.CostSource anywhere (grep CostSource finds only PredictedCostSource from routing candidates). So the provenance signal fizeau now provides is discarded.

This matters for cost-cap enforcement (cli/internal/agent/execute_bead_post_review.go:194, ReviewCostDeferredEventBody): a cap decision made on a zero cost cannot distinguish "free" from "unknown".

PROPOSED FIX
- Add a CostSource field to the agent Result (and to ExecuteBeadResult where cost is carried durably), populated from final.CostSource in cli/internal/agent/service_run.go around :344.
- Have cost-cap enforcement treat CostSourceUnknown distinctly from a genuine zero — at minimum, record it in the evidence rather than silently treating it as free.
- Surface CostSource in the durable attempt-metrics row so historical rows are interpretable.

NON-SCOPE
- Do not change the fizeau contract or attempt to reconstruct cost when provenance is absent.
- Do not alter the four test fixtures that now carry "cost_source":"reported" (already fixed).

description:
PROBLEM: Two issues mask the intended design system (`.stitch/DESIGN.md`: warm-paper brutalist). (1) `cli/internal/server/frontend/design-tokens.json` is the STALE generic Stitch export (`tertiary:#8e35a3` purple, `surface:#f9fafb`, Inter for all roles) — its warm palette only reaches the app because `cli/internal/server/frontend/tailwind.config.js:8-37` hardcodes `semanticColors` that override the JSON. So `bun run design:export` regenerates GENERIC values; a reader cannot tell which file is authoritative. (2) The typeface (`Inter`, tailwind.config.js:39-46) is SPECIFIED but never LOADED (no @font-face/@fontsource/Google Fonts anywhere) -> renders the OS system-sans fallback.

ROOT CAUSE: the design:export pipeline emits the generic default token DATA (not DESIGN.md's warm palette); and no font asset is imported. Per codex: `semanticColors` is the load-bearing alias layer (KEEP it) — only the generated token DATA is stale. Operator decision: load Inter (do NOT introduce a new display font — that would be a spec change).

PROPOSED FIX: Regenerate `design-tokens.json` from `.stitch/DESIGN.md` (warm palette: #3B5B7A lever-steel, #F4EFE6 cream, etc.) so the export pipeline is the source of truth and carries the correct values; KEEP the `semanticColors` alias layer in tailwind.config.js (do not delete it; ensure it reads the regenerated tokens rather than shadowing stale ones). Add Inter via `@fontsource-variable/inter` (`bun add`), import in `cli/internal/server/frontend/src/app.css`, so all non-mono roles render Inter instead of system fallback.

NON-SCOPE: introducing a distinctive display font (operator chose Inter-only); off-palette utility migration (separate bead); deleting the semanticColors layer.

description:
PROBLEM
Parent bead ddx-8a78ee90 is too broad for one execution pass. This child owns part 2 of 3 of that parent scope.

ROOT CAUSE
PROBLEM
Execute-bead agents are instructed to run `lefthook run pre-commit` after staging and then run `git commit`. The repository-installed Git pre-commit hook invokes Lefthook again on the same staged tree. During attempt `20260713T121749-836fcbe4`, a small containment patch ran the full staged `./cmd` plus `./internal/agent` race gate twice explicitly after one test correction, then `git commit` launched a third full pass on the identical final staged tree. The second explicit pass alone spent more than 18 minutes in `go test` output processing. This duplicate gate contract serializes the queue without adding evidence.

ROOT CAUSE WITH FILE:LINE
- `cli/internal/agent/execute_bead.go:2104-2113` and `cli/internal/agent/execute_bead.go:2137-2148` require rich and embedded agents to rerun `lefthook run pre-commit` after staging and then commit exactly once, without recognizing that the implementation commit invokes the installed hook.
- `lefthook.yml:205-216` maps staged Go files to package-wide race tests, so each duplicate invocation can repeat multi-minute `./cmd` and `./internal/agent` gates.
- `.git/hooks/pre-commit:11-18` invokes Lefthook for ordinary `git commit`, making a separately requested manual invocation redundant when the staged tree is unchanged.

PROPOSED FIX
Make the ordinary implementation commit hook the single authoritative staged pre-commit gate. Update both execute-bead prompt variants and integrity evidence so agents stage the exact commit set, run `git commit` normally, and treat the hook output/exit status from that commit as satisfying the bead’s `lefthook run pre-commit` acceptance criterion. If a workflow explicitly runs the hook before commit, reuse that success only when a content/config fingerprint proves the staged tree and hook inputs are identical; otherwise rerun. A failed hook must abort the commit and remain a failed gate.

NON-SCOPE
Using `--no-verify`, setting `LEFTHOOK=0`, weakening or removing repository hooks, reusing evidence after any staged-tree or hook-config change, caching across attempts, bypassing human commits, or changing which tests the hook selects.

PARENT
None; root worker-throughput regression observed while draining the Niflheim queue.

DEPS
Related to `ddx-2afca9c9` (test-output/runtime headroom) and `ddx-03568f89` (gate evidence); no implementation dependency.

PROPOSED FIX
Implement only this child acceptance slice:
- `TestExecuteBeadImplementationCommit_HookFailureAbortsCommit` proves a nonzero hook blocks the commit, records failed gate evidence, and never retries with `--no-verify` or `LEFTHOOK=0`.
- `TestExecuteBeadPreCommitEvidence_InvalidatedByStagedMutation` proves any staged content or relevant hook-config change invalidates prior green evidence and requires a new hook run.

NON-SCOPE
Do not implement parent acceptance criteria assigned to sibling child beads. Preserve every parent non-scope constraint unless this child explicitly narrows it.

acceptance:
1. TestWorkLoop_PreClaimDecompositionPublishesProviderChildMetadata blocks a hermetic decomposition hook and proves the sidecar includes provider-child metadata associated with the candidate bead ID while phase=resolving.
2. TestWorkLoop_PreClaimDecompositionPublishesProviderChildMetadata proves provider processes that predate the hook baseline or belong to another worker are excluded from the candidate metadata.
3. TestWorkLoop_PreClaimDecompositionPublishesResolvingLiveness proves the combined sidecar report contains candidate bead ID, phase=resolving, refreshed last_activity_at, and provider-child metadata before any claim or lease exists.
4. cd cli && go test ./internal/agent/... -run 'TestWorkLoop_PreClaimDecompositionPublishesProviderChildMetadata|TestWorkLoop_PreClaimDecompositionPublishesResolvingLiveness' -count=1 passes.
5. cd cli && go test ./internal/agent/... passes.
6. lefthook run pre-commit passes.
description:
PROBLEM
Operators need to see which provider child belongs to preclaim decomposition while still distinguishing it from claimed implementation work. The sidecar currently lacks provider-child observations for preclaim decomposition, so process-level activity is invisible or can only be inferred externally.

ROOT CAUSE WITH FILE:LINE
cli/internal/agent/execute_bead_loop.go:1604-1617 defers sidecar emission until claim, and cli/internal/agent/execute_bead_loop.go:3108-3120 runs PostAttemptDecompositionHook before claim without attaching provider-child observations to candidate resolving liveness.

PROPOSED FIX
Record provider-child metadata for the preclaim decomposition hook baseline and publish it in candidate-scoped resolving status. The status must identify child provider activity for the candidate while proving that no bead claim, lease, or implementation attempt was created.

NON-SCOPE
Do not claim the parent before decomposition, change decomposition prompts or AC-map validation, change queue ordering, or make preclaim model work count as an implementation attempt. Do not kill provider processes that predate the hook baseline or belong to another worker. Do not implement provider reaping or timeout enforcement in this child.

PARENT
Split from root reliability regression bead: work: surface, bound, and reap preclaim decomposition lifecycle. Original parent bead: work: publish preclaim decomposition resolving liveness.

DEPS
ddx-aa6cc320 must land first so the internal/agent verification gate does not launch five real Codex providers.

description:
PROBLEM
The embedded-dispatch runner tests isolate provider configuration by changing HOME to a raw ddx-home-* directory. On Niflheim, an abandoned ddx-home-3567057526 contained a 468 MB private Go module cache with read-only module directories, and later gates recursively walked it. The current fixture pattern can leave behind the same kind of scratch tree and silently suppress cleanup failures.

ROOT CAUSE WITH FILE:LINE
cli/internal/agent/runner_test.go:29-34 and cli/internal/agent/runner_test.go:56-61 call os.MkdirTemp with an empty root, change HOME, and discard os.RemoveAll errors. Changing HOME also changes the default GOPATH and GOMODCACHE for any Go subprocess or embedded tool that does not receive explicit values.

PROPOSED FIX
Replace the raw os.MkdirTemp fixtures with a shared test helper backed by t.TempDir so cleanup failures fail the test. Before changing HOME, preserve an explicit stable Go module-cache/GOPATH policy for child work so the isolated provider-config HOME cannot become a second module cache. Keep the LM Studio and OpenRouter embedded-dispatch tests using the helper and leave the no-real-provider/no-exec-path assertions intact.

NON-SCOPE
Do not change production runner routing, make live provider calls, delete existing host scratch, or change production cleanup ownership/budgets. ddx-f914dddd and ddx-de1ff4b4 own those cleanup changes.

PARENT
ddx-6a2ce3bd.

description:
PROBLEM
`ddx worker status` reports the persisted desired state, but when `desired_count=1` and no live worker exists after the last server-managed worker exited from fd exhaustion, the operator still cannot see why the desired worker is missing.

ROOT CAUSE WITH FILE:LINE
cli/cmd/worker.go:121-158 loads `.ddx/workers/desired.json` and prints only project, desired_count, restart state, default spec, and updated_at.
cli/cmd/worker_test.go:81-96 only covers the absent-desired-state case, so there is no regression coverage for a missing worker with a terminal fd-exhaustion reason.

PROPOSED FIX
Extend the worker status report with missing-worker count and an fd-exhaustion diagnosis when desired workers are absent, using the new supervisor helper rather than brittle string matching. Preserve the existing absent-state message and the current desired-state fields in both text and JSON output.

NON-SCOPE
Do not change `ddx worker enable`, desired-state persistence, or `ddx work status`. Do not weaken byte/inode resource guards. Do not alter the stale operator-attention fixes tracked by ddx-b17cad6d and ddx-4d92f2cf. Do not introduce a second fd classifier.

title: Surface missing desired-worker fd exhaustion in `ddx worker status`

acceptance:
1. `TestDefaultBranchPreflight_MatchingUpstreamPasses` proves a current branch whose upstream branch name equals origin/HEAD's target reports pass.
2. `TestDefaultBranchPreflight_MismatchedUpstreamFailsWithBothRefs` proves branch.master.merge=refs/heads/main with origin/HEAD -> refs/remotes/origin/master reports a hard failure naming both refs.
3. `TestDefaultBranchPreflight_DetachedHEADFailsWithMessage` proves detached HEAD reports a hard failure with a remediation-oriented message.
4. `TestDefaultBranchPreflight_BehindUpstreamWarns` proves a local branch behind its configured upstream reports a warning without fetching.
5. `cd cli && go test ./internal/agent/... ./cmd/... -run "TestDefaultBranchPreflight_.*" -count=1` passes.
6. `lefthook run pre-commit` passes.
description: PROBLEM: ddx drains can fork the bead queue when the current checkout tracks a branch whose upstream is not the remote default branch. A checkout with branch.master.merge=refs/heads/main while origin/HEAD resolves to refs/remotes/origin/master can look healthy while committing tracker mutations to the wrong branch. ROOT CAUSE: cli/cmd/shared_helpers.go:80 builds the CLI pre-claim hook from the current branch only, and cli/internal/agent/execute_bead_land.go:1093 compares that branch against refs/remotes/origin/<branch>; no shared diagnostic resolves the current branch upstream, origin/HEAD's target branch, or detached HEAD before the queue loop claims work. PROPOSED FIX: add a reusable, network-free git diagnostic helper that resolves HEAD attachment, current branch upstream ref, origin/HEAD's default branch target, and local-vs-upstream ancestry using already-observed refs. Return structured status for match, mismatch, detached HEAD, missing origin/HEAD, missing upstream, local behind upstream, local ahead, and divergence so CLI commands and doctor can render consistent messages. Preserve P9: do not fetch from the queue preflight. NON-SCOPE: do not change bead claim, landing, tracker sync, ddx sync, remote fetch behavior, server-managed worker supervision, or branch merge policy.

description:
PROBLEM
Parent bead ddx-4d92f2cf is too broad for one execution pass. This child owns part 3 of 3 of that parent scope.

ROOT CAUSE
PROBLEM
  Server-managed workers can remain absent even when .ddx/workers/desired.json has desired_count=1. On 2026-07-07, /home/erik/Projects/ddx had desired_count=1 and /home/erik/Projects/niflheim had desired_count=1, but ddx work status --all-projects --json showed only axon and helix workers. Both ddx and niflheim had older status=operator_attention worker records, while the current desired state still asked the supervisor to run one worker.

ROOT CAUSE
  cli/internal/server/workers_supervisor.go:364-374 records every restart-blocking terminal worker into blockedTerminals. cli/internal/server/workers_supervisor.go:417-419 then makes canStartMore return false whenever blockedTerminals is non-empty. There is no expiry, no check that the underlying dirty/root condition has been resolved, and no operator command/state transition that clears the block. Because snapshotWorkers reads historical terminal records from .ddx/workers, the block can survive server restarts and suppress a fresh desired worker indefinitely.

PROPOSED FIX
  - cli/internal/server/workers_supervisor.go:364-419: distinguish active unresolved operator-attention stops from stale historical records. A clean project root with a current desired state must be able to start again after the operator resolves the condition.
  - cli/internal/server/workers_supervisor.go:497-516: keep true restart-blocking semantics for genuinely unresolved dirty-root/operator-attention records, but add a deterministic release path keyed to resolved project state or an explicit desired-state update timestamp newer than the blocking worker.
  - cli/internal/server/workers_supervisor_test.go: add regression coverage for a historical operator_attention terminal followed by a newer desired state and clean project root.

NON-SCOPE
  - Do not weaken the dirty-root guard inside ddx work; a currently dirty implementation root must still stop.
  - Do not edit or delete existing .ddx/workers/*/status.json records as the fix. Worker history must remain durable.
  - Do not change routing/model/provider selection.

PARENT / DEPS
  Root operational bug. No deps.

PROPOSED FIX
Implement only this child acceptance slice:
- cd cli && go test ./internal/server/... passes.
- lefthook run pre-commit passes.

NON-SCOPE
Do not implement parent acceptance criteria assigned to sibling child beads. Preserve every parent non-scope constraint unless this child explicitly narrows it.

description:
PROBLEM
Server-managed drain workers are still started as in-process goroutines, so their WorkerRecord usually has PID zero and no PGID. The server cannot reliably target the ddx work process tree that later launches claude, codex, shell, or sleep descendants.

ROOT CAUSE WITH FILE:LINE
cli/internal/server/workers.go:123-127 records only PID and has no persisted PGID. cli/internal/server/workers.go:414-436 writes the initial WorkerRecord before any managed worker process boundary exists. cli/internal/server/workers.go:438 creates a cancelable context, and cli/internal/server/workers.go:461-462 starts drainProgress and runWorker goroutines instead of a server-owned OS process.

PROPOSED FIX
Add a server-managed subprocess launch path for StartExecuteLoop in cli/internal/server/workers.go:361-464. Persist ExecuteLoopWorkerSpec as today, then start the current ddx binary in its own process group for server-managed drain workers. Record nonzero PID and PGID on WorkerRecord and persisted status.json after the subprocess starts. Keep any in-process execution helper available only for tests that explicitly inject it.

NON-SCOPE
Do not implement the hidden ddx work --server-managed <worker-id> work-loop entry point beyond the minimal command invocation surface needed by this bead; that is covered by a sibling child bead. Do not kill external reported workers or interactive Claude/Codex sessions. Do not change bead claim semantics except releasing claims for the stopped/reaped managed worker. Do not implement UI controls.

GOVERNING ARTIFACT AND RELATIONSHIP
Parent bead: ddx-24a3da84. Original parent relationship cited by the too-large bead: ddx-9d1af129. Governing artifact reference: plan:server-managed-workers. No explicit dependency IDs were provided by the parent bead.

description:
PROBLEM
A single DDx attempt can monopolize the entire server-owned CPU allowance. On 2026-07-13, TestExecuteBead_ConcurrentWorkers_NoHEADRefRace launched five Codex providers whose aggregate use reached about 350 percent CPU, nearly saturating the installed server CPUQuota=400 percent. The aggregate service cap protected the host but provided no fairness between attempts, and a manual/offline worker outside ddx-server.service has no equivalent cap at all.

ROOT CAUSE WITH FILE:LINE
cli/cmd/server_service.go:98-102 exposes only an aggregate CPU quota and weight for the complete server-owned worker/provider/build tree. cli/internal/service/service.go:15-22 defines that policy explicitly as aggregate. cli/internal/agent/executor.go:177-188 starts each provider directly, while cli/internal/agent/executor_unix.go:10-29 configures only a process group and parent-death signal; no attempt-scoped CPU controller contains the provider and all descendants. Consequently one nested test/provider fanout can consume the whole managed-service budget, while the same manual worker path is unbounded.

PROPOSED FIX
- Add one attempt-scoped CPU-envelope abstraction at the provider execution boundary so the harness root and every descendant share a bounded controller. Membership must survive process-group/session changes, double-forking, and reparenting; cleanup and cancellation must act on controller membership rather than ancestry alone.
- Apply the same default and configuration to server-managed and manual/offline workers without requiring a live DDx server. Preserve the existing parent-death behavior so managed provider trees still die when their worker/server dies.
- Use a conservative default of 200 percent of one core per active attempt, allow an explicit 0 value to disable the per-attempt cap, and keep the existing aggregate server service cap as the outer ceiling.
- Emit structured attempt evidence containing requested/effective quota, controller kind, descendant membership, and fallback reason. When the platform cannot enforce a hard quota, continue with lowered scheduling priority and an operator-visible degraded-control event rather than silently claiming enforcement.

IN-SCOPE FILES
- cli/internal/agent/executor.go and adjacent platform-specific executor/resource-controller files
- cli/internal/config execution settings and validation
- cli/cmd/work.go and cli/cmd/try.go only for shared configuration plumbing
- cli/internal/integration for a real descendant-fanout proof

NON-SCOPE
Do not replace or remove the aggregate ddx-server.service CPUQuota/CPUWeight policy. Do not throttle arbitrary external cargo, Go, provider, or user processes that are not descendants of the current DDx attempt. Do not require the coordination server for manual/offline execution. Do not change desired worker count, queue ordering, provider routing, or the process-group/Pdeathsig ownership contract. ddx-aa6cc320 remains responsible for removing live providers from the default test fixture.
notes: Provider-descendant CPU containment belongs to the Fizeau harness/runtime boundary, not DDx attempt execution.

description:
PROBLEM
Even with the citation-granularity predicate consulted at the join, multiple duplicate or unrelated file-only mapping rows can accumulate and satisfy coverage cardinality if the exclusion is applied after or during counting rather than as a pre-join filter. A Complete requirement whose only rows are file-only citations must still be reported as uncovered no matter how many such rows exist.

ROOT CAUSE WITH FILE:LINE
The spechonesty analyzer package does not exist in this checkout: cli/tools/lint/spechonesty/analyzer.go:1 is absent, and cli/tools/lint/ currently contains only evidencelint, routinglint, and runtimelint. The sibling cardinality pass counts mapping rows as coverage, and without an explicit pre-join filtering stage the row multiset reaching the requirement-to-evidence join still contains file-only entries, so cardinality can be met by rows that carry no pinned proof. The governing contract is docs/helix/06-iterate/phase2-doc-truth-plan-2026-07-13.md:67, which requires coverage by a Verification mapping row rather than an unspecific pointer.

PROPOSED FIX
Move the citation-granularity exclusion into an explicit filtering stage that runs before the requirement-to-evidence cardinality join, so file-only rows never enter the joined row set. Duplicate or unrelated file-only rows are dropped in that stage and cannot contribute to cardinality or mask an uncovered Complete requirement. Rows naming concrete targets pass the filter unchanged. Follow cli/tools/lint/evidencelint/analyzer.go and cli/tools/lint/evidencelint/analyzer_test.go conventions, including golang.org/x/tools/go/analysis and analysistest-style fixtures where applicable. The analyzer is read-only.

NON-SCOPE
Do not re-design the citation-granularity predicate itself or the uncovered diagnostic emitted for a Complete requirement with no counting rows — those come from the sibling child. Do not implement the zero-evidence empty-row-set diagnostic. Do not design the uncovered or duplicate cardinality diagnostic family beyond applying the pre-join file-only exclusion to the sibling cardinality pass. Do not handle waivers. Do not parse requirement inventories or mapping tables beyond consuming the mapping-parser child model. Do not implement status parsing. Do not auto-restamp documents, infer proof from prose, fetch network state, or mark aspirational metrics complete. Do not implement duplicate-id or stale-observation detection. Prose quality and AC numbering style are out of scope. Do not resolve whether named Test* symbols, static checks, or artifacts actually exist on disk; this child only relies on whether the row names a target at all. Do not enforce the executable verification command allowlist.

description:
PROBLEM: the Inter typeface is SPECIFIED but never LOADED. `cli/internal/server/frontend/design-tokens.json:20-39` declares `fontFamily.h1/h2/body-md/body-sm/label` as `["Inter"]`, and `cli/internal/server/frontend/tailwind.config.js:39-46` maps those into the `semanticFonts` aliases (`headline-lg`, `headline-md`, `body-md`, `body-sm`, `label-caps`). But there is no `@font-face` rule, no `@fontsource*` import, and no Google Fonts `<link>` anywhere in `cli/internal/server/frontend/src/app.css`, `src/app.html`, or `static/`. Confirmed: `grep -rn "font-face|fontsource|fonts.googleapis" src static` returns nothing, and `ls node_modules | grep -i fontsource` is empty. Every non-mono text role therefore renders the OS system-sans fallback (Segoe UI / Helvetica / DejaVu Sans depending on platform), not Inter — the metrics and weights in `.stitch/DESIGN.md` (`headline-lg` 800 weight, `label-caps` 700 with 0.05em tracking) are silently unmet, and screenshots differ per developer machine.

ROOT CAUSE: no font asset is imported by the frontend build. The Tailwind config names a family it never ships.

PROPOSED FIX: `cd cli/internal/server/frontend && bun add @fontsource-variable/inter`, then add `@import '@fontsource-variable/inter';` to `cli/internal/server/frontend/src/app.css` near the top, above the existing `@import 'tailwindcss';` at line 2 so the face is registered before Tailwind's layers. Update the family stacks so the loaded variable family is what the browser actually resolves: the family name shipped by that package is `'Inter Variable'`, so the `fontFamily` entries that currently read `["Inter"]` must include it (e.g. `['Inter Variable', 'Inter', 'system-ui', 'sans-serif']`), keeping a system fallback. Font family data lives in `design-tokens.json`; the alias layer at `tailwind.config.js:39-46` stays as-is. Commit the resulting `bun.lock` change.

NON-SCOPE: introducing a distinctive display font — the operator explicitly chose Inter-only, and adding a second family would be a spec change; the mono role (`mono-code`, `tailwind.config.js:45`) keeps its existing `ui-monospace, SFMono-Regular, JetBrains Mono, monospace` stack and no mono webfont is shipped; changing any color token (that is the sibling token-canonicalization bead); re-baselining Playwright screenshot snapshots (separate child bead — this bead must not run `--update-snapshots`); the Hugo website's fonts (`.stitch/PLAN.md` phase 5); any Go backend change.

description:
PROBLEM
An author can supply a `spec:verification-waiver` in place of proof and thereby make an unverified Complete/Implemented document pass. A reasoned waiver is legitimate for work that is not yet claiming completion, but it must never suppress a Complete-status coverage failure.

ROOT CAUSE WITH FILE:LINE
The spechonesty analyzer at cli/tools/lint/spechonesty/analyzer.go has no waiver logic: it neither rejects waivers on Complete/Implemented documents nor downgrades unmet verification requirements to warnings for non-Complete statuses. The contract is docs/helix/06-iterate/phase2-doc-truth-plan-2026-07-13.md WB-1 step 5.

PROPOSED FIX
When a `spec:verification-waiver` is present, branch on status. For Complete/Implemented, ignore the waiver entirely: the coverage failure from the coverage child stands as a failure. For a non-Complete status (Proposed, In Progress, Deferred, Aspirational), a reasoned waiver downgrades the unmet verification requirement from a failure to a warning. A waiver can never suppress a Complete-status coverage failure. Analyzer remains read-only.

NON-SCOPE
Do not compute coverage or resolve evidence targets — that is the coverage child. Do not parse mapping tables — that is the mapping-parser child. Do not auto-restamp documents, infer proof from prose, fetch network state, or mark aspirational metrics complete. Status parsing lives in the scaffold child. Duplicate-id and stale-observation detection are a sibling child.

DEPS: the spechonesty scaffold/status-parser child and the verification-coverage child (provides the coverage failure that this child conditionally suppresses).

1. TestExpensiveReplayDetector_EquivalentFailedCommandAcrossWrappersCancels proves direct, timeout-wrapped, redirected/background, and setsid-wrapped forms of the same failed go test command share one semantic fingerprint and the second launch cancels before another suite runs.
2. TestExpensiveReplayDetector_WorktreeOrConfigMutationAllowsOneRevalidation proves a changed tracked-worktree or relevant environment/config fingerprint permits exactly one new validation and records why the prior output was invalid.
3. TestExpensiveReplayDetector_DistinctAndCheapCommandsRemainAllowed proves different test packages, changed flags, and cheap read-only shell commands do not trip the replay circuit.
4. TestExpensiveReplayDetector_ReapsDetachedReplay proves cancellation removes a setsid/reparented tool child from the attempt controller and emits operator_attention with bead ID, attempt ID, prior/current fingerprints, outcomes, and reason.
5. Existing TestLoopDetector_FiresAfterRepeatedIdenticalCommands and TestWedgeImmune_HardWorkRunsToCompletion remain green.
6. cd cli && go test ./internal/agent/... -run "^(TestExpensiveReplayDetector_(EquivalentFailedCommandAcrossWrappersCancels|WorktreeOrConfigMutationAllowsOneRevalidation|DistinctAndCheapCommandsRemainAllowed|ReapsDetachedReplay)|TestLoopDetector_FiresAfterRepeatedIdenticalCommands|TestWedgeImmune_HardWorkRunsToCompletion)$" -count=1 -timeout 120s passes.
7. cd cli && go test ./internal/agent/... -timeout 600s passes.
8. lefthook run pre-commit passes.
description:
PROBLEM
During attempt 20260713T145533-c006900a, the model ran cd cli && go test ./internal/agent/... -timeout 600s, received the same host-scratch traversal failure, reran it after operator termination, and finally launched the equivalent suite through setsid -f with redirected output. The detached run entered a new session and continued consuming CPU/I/O until the operator killed it. The prompt explicitly prohibited an unchanged long-command replay, but DDx did not intervene.

ROOT CAUSE WITH FILE:LINE
- cli/internal/agent/execute_bead.go:2088-2094 expresses the command-fingerprint rule only as model instructions.
- cli/internal/agent/agent_runner_service.go:39-76 keys loop detection on tool name, raw input JSON, error text, and result output. The same expensive command with a different termination message, redirection, timeout wrapper, or setsid wrapper therefore produces a different key.
- cli/internal/agent/agent_runner_service.go:268-271 and 399-415 require four identical call-result pairs in an eight-entry window, so two or three costly replays can consume tens of minutes without firing.
- cli/internal/agent/executor_unix.go:32-39 cannot reap a replay that changes session/process group; ddx-7df6b12a owns the attempt controller needed after cancellation.

PROPOSED FIX
Add an expensive-command replay detector over normalized service tool-call events. Canonicalize shell wrappers that do not change command semantics (cd into the same worktree, timeout, setsid, output redirection, foreground/background launch) while retaining command args, environment/config inputs, cwd, and a worktree/config fingerprint. After an expensive command fails, times out, or ends incomplete, cancel the attempt before a second equivalent replay unless the normalized args/environment/config or worktree fingerprint changed and the event records why the previous evidence is invalid. Persist a structured operator_attention event containing both fingerprints, outcomes, and the cancellation reason. Cancel through the ddx-7df6b12a attempt controller so detached/session-changing children are reaped.

IN-SCOPE FILES
- cli/internal/agent/agent_runner_service.go and adjacent replay-detector helpers/tests
- cli/internal/agent/service_run.go for correlation/evidence plumbing
- attempt-controller integration introduced by ddx-7df6b12a
- execute-bead event/operator-attention mapping for replay cancellation

NON-SCOPE
Do not block distinct commands, cheap read-only commands, one legitimate validation after a code/config fingerprint change, or manual operator commands outside an attempt. Do not infer success from a killed or incomplete command. Do not lower the generic four-pair loop detector for non-expensive tools.

PARENT AND DEPS
Root reliability incident. Depends on ddx-7df6b12a for controller-backed cancellation. Related to ddx-45ea2e36, which owns the independent hard attempt deadline.
notes: Shell-wrapper semantic replay policing belongs inside the selected harness; DDx reacts to typed attempt outcomes.

description:
PROBLEM
The same user-story id appearing in two feature documents (US-087/US-088 collision class) passes unnoticed, so feature requirements can collide across features without a lint failure.

ROOT CAUSE WITH FILE:LINE
After the spechonesty scaffold/status-parser and duplicate-document-id children land, cli/tools/lint/spechonesty/analyzer.go:1 is the analyzer entrypoint but has no duplicate US-id scan. The governing contract docs/helix/06-iterate/phase2-doc-truth-plan-2026-07-13.md:70 (WB-1 step 5-6) requires a failure for the same US-id appearing in two feature documents under docs/helix/01-frame/features/. docs/helix/06-iterate/phase2-doc-truth-plan-2026-07-13.md:69 says waivers cannot suppress duplicate-US-id failures.

PROPOSED FIX
Add deterministic read-only duplicate user-story-id detection to spechonesty, reusing the directory-walk helper established by the duplicate-document-id child. Scan docs/helix/01-frame/features/ (the same lint scope). Fail when the same US-id appears in two feature documents, reporting enough location detail to identify both conflicting feature files. Mark this failure class non-waivable so any waiver parser/status logic from sibling children cannot downgrade it.

NON-SCOPE
Do not auto-restamp documents, infer proof from prose, fetch network state, or mark aspirational metrics complete. Complete-coverage/waiver logic and status parsing live in sibling children. Duplicate document-id (TD-040) detection is a sibling child and out of scope here. Prose quality and AC numbering style are out of scope. Stale current-revision observation validation is out of scope.

GOVERNING ARTIFACT
Phase 2 doc truth plan WB-1 steps 5-6: docs/helix/06-iterate/phase2-doc-truth-plan-2026-07-13.md:69-70.

description:
PROBLEM
The normal internal/agent gate timed out after 10 minutes while TestLifecycleDispatchRejectsProjectRootMutation waited for captureLifecycleProjectStatus. One unbounded project-status subprocess can consume the complete package budget, fail unrelated beads, and force the queue to retry work whose focused acceptance tests are already green.

ROOT CAUSE WITH FILE:LINE
cli/internal/agent/lifecycle_dispatch.go:95-117 accepts no context. At line 105 it calls RepairKnownConfigCorruption with context.Background, and at line 110 it runs git status --porcelain --untracked-files=all with context.Background. The before, after, and restored snapshots at cli/internal/agent/lifecycle_dispatch.go:47, 144, and 157 therefore outlive caller cancellation and have no per-operation deadline. In attempt 20260713T104022-f6d5cb82, the package timeout stack showed TestLifecycleDispatchRejectsProjectRootMutation blocked in internalgit.Command(... status ...).CombinedOutput at lifecycle_dispatch.go:110.

PROPOSED FIX
Thread the lifecycle dispatch caller context through every project-status snapshot and repository-health repair. Derive a short per-snapshot deadline, capped by the caller deadline, and ensure cancellation terminates and waits for the Git subprocess. Return a typed lifecycle snapshot error that preserves deadline/cancellation diagnostics so the intake hook fails promptly instead of holding the package gate.

IN-SCOPE FILES
- cli/internal/agent/lifecycle_dispatch.go
- cli/internal/agent/preclaim_intake_hook_test.go or a focused lifecycle dispatch test file
- nearest internal Git test helper only if needed for a blocking git shim

NON-SCOPE
Do not weaken project-root mutation detection, skip pre/post/restored snapshots, change queue retry policy, increase the package timeout, or alter unrelated Git locking and tracker serialization. Do not rerun or close ddx-69672921 in this bead.

PARENT
None; root lifecycle reliability regression.

DEPS
None.
