description:
PROBLEM
When several `ddx try` / `ddx work` attempts run concurrently against one project, an attempt can abort with `execution_failed` before doing any work, because its pre-execute-bead checkpoint tries to stage a file that a sibling process deleted microseconds earlier.

Observed (2026-07-21, internal/integration under -race load):
  pre-execute-bead checkpoint: staging checkpoint changes:
  fatal: pathspec '.ddx/executions/.ddx-resource-preflight-1822793358' did not match any files: exit status 128
The whole attempt was reported execution_failed even though nothing was wrong with the bead.

ROOT CAUSE
The checkpoint enumerates dirty paths and then passes that list to `git add` as explicit pathspecs. Between the enumeration and the `git add`, a sibling attempt's resource-preflight temp file under `.ddx/executions/` is removed, so the pathspec no longer matches and git exits 128. This is a time-of-check-to-time-of-use gap: the path list is a snapshot, but `git add` requires every pathspec to still resolve.

The staging call lives in the pre-dispatch checkpoint path in cli/internal/agent/ (search: "staging checkpoint changes"). Two things are wrong:
1. `.ddx/executions/` is per-machine working state (see CLAUDE.md, "Execution Evidence Convention") and is gitignored; it should never be enumerated as checkpoint-worthy dirt in the first place.
2. Even for legitimate paths, `git add` with explicit pathspecs must tolerate a path vanishing under it.

PROPOSED FIX
- Exclude `.ddx/executions/**` from the pre-dispatch checkpoint's dirty enumeration, the same way cli/internal/agent/predispatch_dirty.go:489 already excludes `.ddx/beads.lock.*.lock` as runtime coordination state.
- Pass `--ignore-missing` semantics or re-filter the pathspec list immediately before `git add`, so a concurrently-deleted path degrades to a skipped file rather than a failed attempt.
- Classify a residual `did not match any files` staging error as retryable rather than execution_failed.

NON-SCOPE
- Do not change what the checkpoint commits for legitimately dirty tracked files.
- Do not address the land-time compare-and-swap loss (sister bead) or the dirty-worktree guard's sibling-output sensitivity (sister bead).

description:
PROBLEM
Complete/Implemented documents can leave normative requirements unmapped, map the same requirement more than once, or carry no verification evidence at all while still passing lint. FEAT-009/FEAT-002/FEAT-012 are called out by the Phase 2 recovery plan as Complete documents with absent or incomplete verification coverage.

ROOT CAUSE WITH FILE:LINE
The requested spechonesty analyzer path is absent in this checkout at cli/tools/lint/spechonesty/analyzer.go:1, and the parent analyzer work has not yet added Complete-status verification-coverage logic. The governing contract is docs/helix/06-iterate/phase2-doc-truth-plan-2026-07-13.md:67, which requires every Complete/Implemented requirement or stable anchor to be covered exactly once by a Verification mapping row, and docs/helix/06-iterate/phase2-doc-truth-plan-2026-07-13.md:68, which requires uncovered and duplicate mappings to fail.

PROPOSED FIX
After the scaffold/status-parser child and Verification mapping-parser child provide the Complete/Implemented document set, requirement inventory, and mapping rows model, add the coverage-cardinality pass: for every Complete/Implemented document, require at least one verification row, require every inventory requirement/anchor to be covered by exactly one row, emit one diagnostic per uncovered requirement, and emit one diagnostic per duplicate mapping. Treat a test-file path without the exact mapped test/check/artifact target as non-coverage for this cardinality pass. Analyzer remains read-only.

NON-SCOPE
Do not handle waivers — that is the waiver child. Do not parse requirement inventories or mapping tables — that is the mapping-parser child. Do not auto-restamp documents, infer proof from prose, fetch network state, or mark aspirational metrics complete. Status parsing lives in the scaffold child. Duplicate-id and stale-observation detection are a sibling child. Prose quality and AC numbering style are out of scope. Do not resolve whether named Test* symbols, static checks, or artifacts exist — evidence-target resolution is a sibling child. Do not enforce the executable verification command allowlist — command allowlist enforcement is a sibling child.

DEPS: parent ddx-471d66b6; the spechonesty scaffold/status-parser child; the Verification mapping-parser child that provides the inventory + rows model. GOVERNING ARTIFACT: docs/helix/06-iterate/phase2-doc-truth-plan-2026-07-13.md WB-1 steps 3-4.

Remove each unimplemented query field from the schema, regenerate GraphQL bindings, and delete the corresponding resolver stubs. Update schema-contract tests to assert absence.

description:
PROBLEM
Complete/Implemented documents can cite a Verification mapping row whose named `Test*` symbol does not exist. TD-027 demonstrates the failure mode: some cited tests are real, while TestOperationCatalog_AxonStoreSwitchCoverage and TestWatcherHub_UsesProvidedFactory do not exist, and the real tests must not make absent test coverage pass.

ROOT CAUSE WITH FILE:LINE
The requested spechonesty analyzer path is absent in this checkout at cli/tools/lint/spechonesty/analyzer.go:1, and the parent analyzer work has not yet added evidence-target resolution for Verification rows. The governing contract is docs/helix/06-iterate/phase2-doc-truth-plan-2026-07-13.md:67, which requires each mapping row to name an exact evidence target, and docs/helix/06-iterate/phase2-doc-truth-plan-2026-07-13.md:68, which requires resolving every named test/check and rejecting missing targets. The TD-027 mixed-real/missing-test example is recorded at docs/helix/06-iterate/phase2-doc-truth-plan-2026-07-13.md:71.

PROPOSED FIX
After the Verification mapping-parser child exposes row targets, add a Go test-symbol resolver for mapped `Test*` evidence targets. A mapped `Test*` target must resolve to an actual Go test function symbol in the referenced package/file scope. Emit a diagnostic naming each missing test symbol. A test-file path without the specific `Test*` target it proves is not coverage. Analyzer remains read-only.

NON-SCOPE
Do not handle waivers — that is the waiver child. Do not parse requirement inventories or mapping tables — that is the mapping-parser child. Do not auto-restamp documents, infer proof from prose, fetch network state, or mark aspirational metrics complete. Status parsing lives in the scaffold child. Duplicate-id and stale-observation detection are a sibling child. Prose quality and AC numbering style are out of scope. Do not enforce requirement coverage cardinality or duplicate mapping counts — the coverage-cardinality child owns that. Do not resolve runtime artifact paths or executable command allowlisting — sibling children own those checks. Do not resolve named deterministic static checks — the static-check resolver child owns that.

description:
PROBLEM
During the 2026-07-13 Niflheim queue drain, the operator ran `ddx bead queue top` on four newly discovered P0 reliability beads. Each command succeeded and committed, but all four beads received `queue-rank: 0`; `ddx bead ready` continued to put the older retry bead `ddx-415c8b95` first. The command therefore does not fulfill “move to the front” once any bead in the priority bucket already has rank zero.

ROOT CAUSE WITH FILE:LINE
- `cli/internal/bead/ops/queue/queue.go:25-32` implements `Top` as a direct `QueueSetTop{}` mutation without reading the priority bucket.
- `cli/internal/bead/operation.go:8-17` hard-codes every `QueueSetTop` result to rank zero.
- `cli/internal/bead/ops/queue/queue.go:34-75` already has the correct bucket-aware `Move(..., position=0)` machinery, including sparse negative ranks and renormalization, but `Top` bypasses it.
- `cli/cmd/bead_queue_test.go:48-71` tests top only against unranked beads and misses existing-rank-zero and repeated-top cases.
This regresses the ordering semantics specified and previously closed by `ddx-d0c656b0`.

PROPOSED FIX
Make `Top` use the same bucket-aware positioning contract as `Move` so the target strictly sorts before the current first bead, including when one or many entries already have rank zero. Preserve priority and avoid rewriting unrelated priority buckets. Add command- and ops-level repeated-top coverage.

NON-SCOPE
Changing priority values, global cross-priority ordering, clearing operator ranks, changing ready eligibility, or manually editing tracker JSONL.

PARENT
None; root queue-ordering regression found while prioritizing Niflheim reliability work.

DEPS
None.

description:
PROBLEM
Execute-bead agents are instructed to run `lefthook run pre-commit` after staging and then run `git commit`. The repository-installed Git pre-commit hook invokes Lefthook again on the same staged tree. During attempt `20260713T121749-836fcbe4`, a small containment patch ran the full staged `./cmd` plus `./internal/agent` race gate twice explicitly after one test correction, then `git commit` launched a third full pass on the identical final staged tree. The second explicit pass alone spent more than 18 minutes in `go test` output processing. This duplicate gate contract serializes the queue without adding evidence.

ROOT CAUSE WITH FILE:LINE
- `cli/internal/agent/execute_bead.go:2104-2113` and `cli/internal/agent/execute_bead.go:2137-2148` require rich and embedded agents to rerun `lefthook run pre-commit` after staging and then commit exactly once, without recognizing that the implementation commit invokes the installed hook.
- `lefthook.yml:205-216` maps staged Go files to package-wide race tests, so each duplicate invocation can repeat multi-minute `./cmd` and `./internal/agent` gates.
- `.git/hooks/pre-commit:11-18` invokes Lefthook for ordinary `git commit`, making a separately requested manual invocation redundant when the staged tree is unchanged.

PROPOSED FIX
Make the ordinary implementation commit hook the single authoritative staged pre-commit gate. Update both execute-bead prompt variants and integrity evidence so agents stage the exact commit set, run `git commit` normally, and treat the hook output/exit status from that commit as satisfying the bead’s `lefthook run pre-commit` acceptance criterion. If a workflow explicitly runs the hook before commit, reuse that success only when a content/config fingerprint proves the staged tree and hook inputs are identical; otherwise rerun. A failed hook must abort the commit and remain a failed gate.

NON-SCOPE
Using `--no-verify`, setting `LEFTHOOK=0`, weakening or removing repository hooks, reusing evidence after any staged-tree or hook-config change, caching across attempts, bypassing human commits, or changing which tests the hook selects.

PARENT
None; root worker-throughput regression observed while draining the Niflheim queue.

DEPS
Related to `ddx-2afca9c9` (test-output/runtime headroom) and `ddx-03568f89` (gate evidence); no implementation dependency.

description:
PROBLEM
When several attempts share one project worktree, the pre-dispatch dirty-worktree guard sees a sibling attempt's in-flight output file, concludes the operator has uncommitted work, and releases a perfectly healthy claim:
  operator attention: project worktree ... has uncommitted implementation changes;
  released ddxfixture-c16c024e ... out-ddxfixture-b70d1d65.txt
Note the released bead (c16c024e) and the file that triggered it (b70d1d65) belong to DIFFERENT beads. The guard is attributing a sibling's work to the current attempt.

Observed 2026-07-21 in internal/integration concurrent-try load testing.

ROOT CAUSE
The guard in cli/internal/agent/predispatch_dirty.go treats any unignored dirt in the project worktree as operator work. It already special-cases runtime coordination state (`.ddx/beads.lock.*.lock`, predispatch_dirty.go:489) but has no notion of "this path belongs to another live attempt". Under concurrency the guard is not attempt-aware, so a sibling's output file is indistinguishable from an operator edit — and the conservative response (release the claim, raise operator attention) is exactly wrong.

PROPOSED FIX
- Make the guard attempt-aware: paths owned by another live attempt (identifiable from the running-attempt registry / claim leases, or by the `out-<beadID>` naming the fixtures use) must not count as operator dirt for a different bead.
- Where ownership cannot be established, prefer blocking only the attempt whose own worktree is dirty rather than releasing the claim.

NON-SCOPE
- Do not weaken the guard for genuine operator edits; an uncommitted change with no live-attempt owner must still raise operator attention.
- Do not address the checkpoint staging TOCTOU or the tracker lost-update (sister beads).

description:
PROBLEM
A server-managed ddx work process can be terminated mid-attempt even while its bead lease and worker heartbeat are fresh. The parent regression incident recorded worker worker-20260711T204017-68e9, PID 303304, emitting a fresh heartbeat for ddx-69591a68 at 2026-07-13T05:47:15Z, then receiving cancellation and exiting 130 at 2026-07-13T05:47:45Z. This regresses ddx-57faa17c because that fix preserved the bead claim but did not protect the live process.

ROOT CAUSE WITH FILE:LINE
cli/internal/server/workers.go:1447-1449 calls cleanupManagedWorkerProcessTree for every live PID named by a disk record before cli/internal/server/workers.go:1451-1467 asks staleDiskEntryCanReleaseClaim whether the fresh lease is safe to reclaim. cli/internal/server/workers.go:1586-1614 correctly refuses claim release for fresh or live same-machine leases, but that decision arrives after the process has already been killed. cli/internal/server/workers.go:1470-1482 can still rewrite the record stopped after that premature cleanup decision.

PROPOSED FIX
Refactor stopStaleDiskEntry so it classifies whether a stale disk record is reclaimable before sending any signal or rewriting its state. When the disk record names a live same-machine PID and staleDiskEntryCanReleaseClaim refuses release because the bead lease or heartbeat is fresh, preserve the process, preserve the in_progress claim, and leave the worker record out of the stopped path. Add a structured lifecycle/supervisor diagnostic for this preservation path containing worker ID, PID, bead ID, and preservation reason.

NON-SCOPE
Do not change desired worker count, generic process cleanup, provider parent-death behavior, or manual/server coordination owned by ddx-635ae251. Do not weaken cleanup of dead PIDs or genuinely stale leases. Do not implement supervisor duplicate-prevention behavior beyond the direct stopStaleDiskEntry preservation path.

PARENT
Split from root regression bead "server: preserve live managed PIDs during stale-record cleanup".

DEPS
None.

When overridden, allow the drain but print a clear warning naming the current branch, its upstream, and origin/HEAD. Preserve the existing warning for local branch behind its upstream at drain start. NON-SCOPE: do not change queue selection, retry cooldowns, claim leasing, tracker sync defaults, provider routing, review behavior, ddx sync, or server supervisor desired-state files.

description:
PROBLEM
During preclaim decomposition of ddx-29491a0e on 2026-07-13, `ddx work status --json` reported active_work.count=0 with no bead_id, phase, or last_activity_at while a queue-critical provider was already running. The first missing piece is a candidate-scoped liveness state that can be published before a bead claim or lease exists.

ROOT CAUSE WITH FILE:LINE
cli/internal/agent/execute_bead_loop.go:1604-1617 constructs the sidecar liveness reporter but explicitly defers emission until a bead is claimed, so preclaim candidates have no status surface.

PROPOSED FIX
Add candidate-scoped resolving liveness publication before PostAttemptDecompositionHook dispatch. The sidecar status must expose the candidate bead ID, phase=resolving, and an initialized last_activity_at while preserving the fact that no claim or lease has been created.

NON-SCOPE
Do not claim the parent before decomposition, change decomposition prompts or AC-map validation, change queue ordering, or make preclaim model work count as an implementation attempt. Do not kill provider processes that predate the hook baseline or belong to another worker. Do not implement heartbeat refreshes or provider-child metadata in this child beyond any minimal fields needed for the candidate resolving state.

PARENT
Split from root reliability regression bead: work: surface, bound, and reap preclaim decomposition lifecycle. Original parent bead: work: publish preclaim decomposition resolving liveness.

DEPS
ddx-aa6cc320 must land first so the internal/agent verification gate does not launch five real Codex providers.

2. TestOwnedScratchMarkerRoundTrip (or a sibling assertion within it) proves a missing or malformed marker yields an uncertain/unowned status rather than an ownership claim, consistent with ddx-05e3d16b and ddx-1eb1ba93.
3. cd cli && go test ./internal/scratchowner/... -run "TestOwnedScratchMarkerRoundTrip$" -count=1 passes.
4. cd cli && go test ./internal/scratchowner/... passes.
5. lefthook run pre-commit passes.
description:
PROBLEM
There is no lower-level contract that a producer of process-lifetime scratch directories can use to record durable ownership evidence, and that execution cleanup can read, without creating an import cycle between internal/testutils and internal/agent. Without this marker, a directory's name prefix plus age becomes the only signal available to cleanup, which cannot distinguish an abandoned directory from one still owned by a live long-running test process.

ROOT CAUSE WITH FILE:LINE
cli/internal/testutils/fixture_repo.go:119-167 creates and publishes binary directories with no durable owner marker, so there is nothing for cleanup to key ownership on.
cli/internal/agent/execution_cleanup.go:667-681 synthesizes ownership only when cleanup.json is absent, and cli/internal/agent/execution_cleanup.go:189-221 preserves a directory with live PID or lease evidence only when compatible metadata already exists — no shared marker type exists that both a testutils producer and the agent cleaner can construct and validate.
ddx-05e3d16b and ddx-1eb1ba93 establish host-global trust and metadata-marked reclamation rules but define no producer-writable process-lifetime ownership marker.

PROPOSED FIX
Add a small internal/scratchowner package that defines an owner-marker contract importable by both internal/testutils and internal/agent with no import cycle. The marker records: resource kind, owner PID, creation time, and a process-start identity when the platform exposes one. Provide atomic write (temp file + rename within the target directory) and a read/validate path that reports live, dead, or uncertain owner status consistent with the ownership rules in ddx-05e3d16b and ddx-1eb1ba93. A prefix or name match is never treated as ownership proof.

IN-SCOPE FILES
- a new cli/internal/scratchowner package and its tests

NON-SCOPE
Do not modify fixture_repo.go producers or execution_cleanup.go in this bead; child beads ddx (fixture producers) and ddx (cleanup wiring) consume this contract.
Do not change Fizeau routing, test-seam behavior, harness selection, model selection, or provider policy.
Do not redesign general host-global scratch trust; ddx-05e3d16b and ddx-1eb1ba93 own that policy.
Do not change execution scratch placement; ddx-b2702b9f owns that migration.

PARENT
ddx-f914dddd

DEPS
ddx-1eb1ba93 must land first so metadata-marked reclamation and host-global ownership rules are established; it already depends on ddx-05e3d16b.

description:
PROBLEM
A missing runtime artifact diagnostic can point at the wrong fix if it reports a cleaned, absolute, resolved, or inferred artifact path instead of the artifact path exactly as written in the Verification mapping row.

ROOT CAUSE WITH FILE:LINE
The spechonesty analyzer path is absent in this checkout at cli/tools/lint/spechonesty/analyzer.go:1, and the analyzer run has no runtime-artifact existence check over parsed Verification rows. The governing contract is docs/helix/06-iterate/phase2-doc-truth-plan-2026-07-13.md:67, requiring every Complete/Implemented mapping row to name an exact evidence target, and docs/helix/06-iterate/phase2-doc-truth-plan-2026-07-13.md:68, requiring rejection of mappings to nonexistent artifacts. Current-revision executable verification is reinforced at docs/helix/06-iterate/phase2-doc-truth-plan-2026-07-13.md:176.

PROPOSED FIX
When spechonesty runtime-artifact validation emits a missing-artifact diagnostic, populate the artifact path field or message fragment from the raw mapped artifact path stored on the parsed Verification row, while still allowing the resolver child to use a resolved filesystem path internally for existence checks. Do not reconstruct the display path from resolver output, prose, or cleaned paths.

NON-SCOPE
Do not add new categories of diagnostics beyond missing inspectable runtime artifact mappings. Do not reimplement target classification or path resolution — consume the resolver child. Do not handle waivers — that is the waiver child. Do not parse requirement inventories or mapping tables — that is the mapping-parser child. Do not auto-restamp documents, infer proof from prose, fetch network state, or mark aspirational metrics complete. Status parsing lives in the scaffold child. Duplicate-id and stale-observation detection are a sibling child. Prose quality and AC numbering style are out of scope. Do not enforce requirement coverage cardinality or duplicate mapping counts — the coverage-cardinality child owns that. Do not resolve Go Test* symbols or static check names — the evidence-target child owns those checks. Do not enforce command allowlisting — the verification-command allowlist child owns that. This child does not add new source-document or requirement-id metadata beyond consuming the row metadata made available by the mapping-parser and source-context diagnostic child.

DEPS: parent ddx-e743ce67; grandparent ddx-29449fa5; root dependency ddx-471d66b6; the spechonesty scaffold/status-parser child; the Verification mapping-parser child that provides the inventory + rows model; the runtime artifact target resolver child. GOVERNING ARTIFACT: docs/helix/06-iterate/phase2-doc-truth-plan-2026-07-13.md WB-1 steps 3-4.

description:
PROBLEM
A watch worker can prove its temp/evidence roots are healthy on every dispatch, yet beads previously blocked by local resource exhaustion remain outside candidate selection forever. This required manually reopening fifteen beads after the July 11 ENOSPC incident.

ROOT CAUSE WITH FILE:LINE
cli/internal/agent/execute_bead_loop.go:2352-2363 performs an idle-path auto-reopen only for retryable provider-connectivity proposals before nextCandidate. cli/internal/agent/execute_bead_loop.go:2492-2576 reports and sleeps on no ready work without rechecking blocked local resources. cli/internal/agent/execution_resources.go:208-300 already supplies the authoritative root health probe, but the idle lifecycle path never applies it to typed blocked beads.

PROPOSED FIX
- Before candidate selection in watch mode, list blocked beads carrying the typed local_resource_exhaustion marker from ddx-c4cbf253.
- Run the configured ExecutionResourceChecker once per idle pass. Reopen all matching beads through LifecycleTransitionOptions{ManualReopen:true} only when the probe is healthy.
- Append durable local_resource_blocker_recheck evidence containing before/after root checks and emit a loop event.
- Leave typed blockers blocked when the probe is unhealthy and leave every untyped/manual blocker untouched.

IN-SCOPE FILES
- cli/internal/agent/execute_bead_loop.go
- cli/internal/agent/execute_bead_loop_resource_exhausted_test.go or one focused companion test

NON-SCOPE
- Do not parse free-text blocker reasons.
- Do not reopen cross-repo, provider, test-suite, or operator-decision blockers.
- Do not change resource thresholds or cleanup policy.

PARENT
- ddx-5958e8a4.

- ddx-c4cbf253 persists the typed marker.

description:
PROBLEM
After preclaim decomposition starts, operators need `last_activity_at` to keep advancing while the provider is blocked or running. Without heartbeat refreshes, a long-running preclaim provider can look stale even if candidate resolving state exists.

ROOT CAUSE WITH FILE:LINE
cli/internal/agent/execute_bead_loop.go:3108-3120 invokes PostAttemptDecompositionHook before claim without setting a resolving phase or ticking liveness while the hook/provider is active.

PROPOSED FIX
Wrap preclaim decomposition dispatch with a resolving-phase heartbeat that refreshes candidate-scoped last_activity_at for the duration of the hook. The heartbeat must stop cleanly when the hook returns and must not create or require a bead lease.

NON-SCOPE
Do not claim the parent before decomposition, change decomposition prompts or AC-map validation, change queue ordering, or make preclaim model work count as an implementation attempt. Do not kill provider processes that predate the hook baseline or belong to another worker. Do not add provider-child metadata beyond any existing fields needed to identify the running candidate.

PARENT
Split from root reliability regression bead: work: surface, bound, and reap preclaim decomposition lifecycle. Original parent bead: work: publish preclaim decomposition resolving liveness.

DEPS
ddx-aa6cc320 must land first so the internal/agent verification gate does not launch five real Codex providers.

description:
PROBLEM
When an operator reviews a preserved dangling-success result and rejects it (bad implementation), the bead is set back to open for a fresh attempt. But on the next drain pass, a worker sees the still-existing preserved result ref, re-preserves it, and re-proposes the bead for operator landing — an endless propose/reject loop. Observed 3x on 2026-07-23 with ddx-074a82c2: its preserved result 3e787d9eb4 was operator-rejected (hard-coded example path as policy — see that bead's notes), reset to open at ~05:00, and re-proposed by workers at ~12:5x and ~17:2x without any fresh implementation attempt.

ROOT CAUSE
The dangling-success re-preserve path (emitter of dangling-success-preserved events in cli/internal/agent) treats any preserved result ref for an open bead as landable and re-proposes, with no record that an operator already rejected that specific result_rev.

PROPOSED FIX
Record operator rejection as a structured bead event (e.g. kind=preserved-result-rejected with the rejected result_rev). Before re-proposing a preserved result, the worker checks for a rejection event matching that result_rev; if rejected, skip the preserve/propose and treat the bead as ordinary ready work (fresh attempt). Provide the rejection via a CLI surface (e.g. ddx bead update <id> --reject-preserved <rev> or an event-append command) so operators do not hand-edit events.

NON-SCOPE
Automatic deletion of preserve refs (audit trail stays); changing dangling-success detection for non-rejected results.

description:
PROBLEM
DDx still chooses or biases concrete Fizeau routes in production even after removing the obvious run/try/work preflight. Local harness-name dispatch, lifecycle profile discovery, server defaults, project-model inheritance, and dead exported route-control APIs let DDx select harness/provider/model/profile policy it does not own. Removing preflight also left the advertised 60s route-resolution lease guard disconnected.

ROOT CAUSE WITH FILE:LINE
- cli/internal/agent/service_run.go:90-135, cli/internal/agent/dispatch.go:36-67, and cli/internal/agent/runner.go:84-114 route virtual/script names into DDx-local runners instead of forwarding an operator harness constraint to Fizeau.
- cli/internal/agent/preclaim_intake_hook.go:477-494,559-579 and cli/internal/agent/recovery_decompose.go:237-247 call ListPolicies/ListModels and select concrete lifecycle profiles.
- cli/internal/server/graphql_adapters.go:73-100, workers_supervisor.go:23-106, graphql/resolver_feat008.go:89-120, and the workers frontend seed default/smart profiles; server workers.go:363-372 and agent/run_dispatch_spec.go:103-127 leave opaque passthrough false, so config/resolved.go:73-80 can inject project agent.model into an unpinned request.
- cli/internal/agent/execute_bead_loop.go:6935-7533, service_run.go:461-636, cli/cmd/agent_execute_loop_escalation.go:104-379, internal/agent/escalation/ladder.go, and model_discovery_containment.go retain exclusion, resolver, catalog-ladder, historical-route-seeding, and discovery-control capabilities.
- cli/internal/agent/execute_bead_loop.go:88-91,215-228 plus work/try/server flag plumbing retain route-resolution-timeout after deleting its resolver call, making the documented lease-release guard a no-op.

PROPOSED FIX
Route every production agent and lifecycle invocation through Fizeau. Preserve explicit operator Harness, Provider, Model, Policy/Profile, MaxPower, and other public passthrough byte-for-byte, but never synthesize concrete route fields. Express DDx-owned difficulty or escalation only through abstract MinPower. Remove local script/virtual name dispatch from production, lifecycle catalog/profile selection, default/smart profile injection, project-model inheritance for opaque execution entry points, route exclusion/catalog/seed machinery, and dead exported control APIs. Retain the 60s wedge guard by timing only Fizeau's opaque route stage from Execute dispatch until its first routing_decision event; on expiry cancel the operation, release the lease, and append operator_attention, and permanently disarm the timer once routing_decision arrives.

NON-SCOPE
Do not remove read-only provider/model inventory or UI display of Fizeau-returned route evidence, change Fizeau internals, reject explicit operator passthrough, implement typed-result policy that requires a newer Fizeau release, or implement reviewer cardinality/stronger-review policy owned by dependent beads.

PARENT
ddx-b8cacbeb.

DEPS
None; Phase 1 WB-2a is start-immediately and this bead is the execution-boundary prerequisite for difficulty and review work.

description:
PROBLEM
Complete/Implemented documents can leave normative requirements unmapped or map the same requirement more than once and still pass lint. An unmapped requirement means a Complete stamp covers work with no stated proof; a duplicated mapping hides which row is the authoritative evidence and inflates apparent coverage.

ROOT CAUSE WITH FILE:LINE
The spechonesty analyzer package does not exist in this checkout — the expected path cli/tools/lint/spechonesty/analyzer.go:1 is absent (cli/tools/lint/ currently contains only evidencelint, routinglint, runtimelint). No pass performs coverage-cardinality arithmetic between a document's requirement inventory and its Verification mapping rows. The governing contract is docs/helix/06-iterate/phase2-doc-truth-plan-2026-07-13.md:67 (every Complete/Implemented requirement or stable anchor covered exactly once) and docs/helix/06-iterate/phase2-doc-truth-plan-2026-07-13.md:68 (uncovered and duplicate mappings must fail).

PROPOSED FIX
Consuming the Complete/Implemented document set from the scaffold/status-parser child and the requirement inventory plus mapping-rows model from the Verification mapping-parser child, add the coverage-cardinality pass: for each Complete/Implemented document, join inventory requirements/anchors against mapping rows by requirement identifier, emit one diagnostic per requirement covered zero times naming that requirement, and emit one diagnostic per requirement covered more than once naming that requirement as a duplicate mapping. A requirement covered exactly once yields no diagnostic. Follow the package and test conventions in cli/tools/lint/evidencelint/analyzer.go and cli/tools/lint/evidencelint/analyzer_test.go, including golang.org/x/tools/go/analysis and analysistest-style fixtures where applicable. The analyzer is read-only.

NON-SCOPE
Do not implement the zero-evidence (empty row set) diagnostic — that is the sibling zero-evidence child. Do not implement the file-only-citation exclusion rule — that is the sibling citation-granularity child. Do not handle waivers — that is the waiver child. Do not parse requirement inventories or mapping tables — that is the mapping-parser child; consume its model. Do not implement status parsing — that is the scaffold child. Do not auto-restamp documents, infer proof from prose, fetch network state, or mark aspirational metrics complete. Duplicate-id and stale-observation detection are a sibling child. Prose quality and AC numbering style are out of scope. Do not resolve whether named Test* symbols, static checks, or artifacts exist — evidence-target resolution is a sibling child. Do not enforce the executable verification command allowlist — command allowlist enforcement is a sibling child.

DEPS: parent ddx-29449fa5 (and its parent ddx-471d66b6); the spechonesty scaffold/status-parser child; the Verification mapping-parser child that provides the inventory + rows model. GOVERNING ARTIFACT: docs/helix/06-iterate/phase2-doc-truth-plan-2026-07-13.md WB-1 steps 3-4.

PROBLEM
Parent bead ddx-8a78ee90 is too broad for one execution pass. This child owns part 1 of 3 of that parent scope.

ROOT CAUSE
PROBLEM
Execute-bead agents are instructed to run `lefthook run pre-commit` after staging and then run `git commit`. The repository-installed Git pre-commit hook invokes Lefthook again on the same staged tree. During attempt `20260713T121749-836fcbe4`, a small containment patch ran the full staged `./cmd` plus `./internal/agent` race gate twice explicitly after one test correction, then `git commit` launched a third full pass on the identical final staged tree. The second explicit pass alone spent more than 18 minutes in `go test` output processing. This duplicate gate contract serializes the queue without adding evidence.

ROOT CAUSE WITH FILE:LINE
- `cli/internal/agent/execute_bead.go:2104-2113` and `cli/internal/agent/execute_bead.go:2137-2148` require rich and embedded agents to rerun `lefthook run pre-commit` after staging and then commit exactly once, without recognizing that the implementation commit invokes the installed hook.
- `lefthook.yml:205-216` maps staged Go files to package-wide race tests, so each duplicate invocation can repeat multi-minute `./cmd` and `./internal/agent` gates.
- `.git/hooks/pre-commit:11-18` invokes Lefthook for ordinary `git commit`, making a separately requested manual invocation redundant when the staged tree is unchanged.

PROPOSED FIX
Make the ordinary implementation commit hook the single authoritative staged pre-commit gate. Update both execute-bead prompt variants and integrity evidence so agents stage the exact commit set, run `git commit` normally, and treat the hook output/exit status from that commit as satisfying the bead’s `lefthook run pre-commit` acceptance criterion. If a workflow explicitly runs the hook before commit, reuse that success only when a content/config fingerprint proves the staged tree and hook inputs are identical; otherwise rerun. A failed hook must abort the commit and remain a failed gate.

NON-SCOPE
Using `--no-verify`, setting `LEFTHOOK=0`, weakening or removing repository hooks, reusing evidence after any staged-tree or hook-config change, caching across attempts, bypassing human commits, or changing which tests the hook selects.

PARENT
None; root worker-throughput regression observed while draining the Niflheim queue.

DEPS

PROPOSED FIX
Implement only this child acceptance slice:
- `TestExecuteBeadPrompt_UsesImplementationCommitAsSinglePreCommitGate` proves both rich and embedded prompts tell the agent to stage exact paths and rely on the normal commit hook once, without requesting a separate identical staged `lefthook` run.

description:
PROBLEM
Attempt 20260713T094206-53684645 for ddx-415c8b95 had a staged pre-commit gate terminated after it recursively walked 100 leaked host-global module caches. The provider then ran git commit --no-verify and DDx accepted, merged, closed, and pushed implementation commit 85bb0fae0. A code-changing attempt can therefore bypass its required staged hook and still be classified as successful.

ROOT CAUSE WITH FILE:LINE
cli/internal/agent/execute_bead.go:2108-2113 and cli/internal/agent/execute_bead.go:2143-2148 require tests and a staged lefthook run but do not explicitly forbid --no-verify, hook disabling, or bypassing a failed gate. cli/internal/agent/execute_bead.go:1507-1514 invokes ValidateAttemptIntegrity without populating GateRuns. cli/internal/agent/execute_bead_validation.go:160-186 checks gate evidence only when len(GateRuns) is nonzero, and TestValidateAttemptIntegrity_SingleCommitNoEvidenceSkips codifies missing evidence as success. The validation promised by closed bead ddx-725b65b4 is therefore not wired into the live execute-bead path.

PROPOSED FIX
- Add an explicit execute-bead instruction that implementation agents must never use git commit --no-verify, disable hooks, or commit after a required gate failed or was interrupted.
- Capture implementation-agent tool commands and foreground gate outputs/exit codes from the harness session into structured attempt-integrity input.
- When a code-changing bead acceptance requires lefthook run pre-commit, require at least one successful meaningful staged run after the final staged mutation and before the implementation commit. Missing, failed, interrupted, background-only, or no-staged-files evidence must reject and preserve the attempt.
- Treat an implementation-agent git commit --no-verify command as an integrity violation even if a prior gate appeared meaningful.
- Keep DDx-owned checkpoint, tracker-only, landing, and durable-audit commits outside this rule; their scoped --no-verify use is orchestrator-owned.

IN-SCOPE FILES
- cli/internal/agent/execute_bead.go
- cli/internal/agent/execute_bead_validation.go
- cli/internal/agent/execute_bead_validation_test.go
- execute-bead prompt guardrail/snapshot tests
- nearest harness-session evidence adapter needed to populate GateRuns and implementation commands

NON-SCOPE
Do not rewrite or remove existing execute-bead history, forbid DDx-owned tracker/audit commits, rerun repository hooks for synthesized commits, or weaken required gates. ddx-a3358532 owns synthesized-commit hook behavior.

PARENT
None; root attempt-integrity regression.

DEPS
Related to closed ddx-725b65b4 and open ddx-2295d9b1, but no dependency is required.

description:
PROBLEM
Verification mapping rows need citation-granularity logic for non-test evidence before coverage cardinality can correctly count rows that name concrete proof. Rows naming exact static checks or artifact targets must count as covering even when they are not Test* evidence.

ROOT CAUSE WITH FILE:LINE
The spechonesty analyzer package does not exist in this checkout: cli/tools/lint/spechonesty/analyzer.go:1 is absent, and cli/tools/lint/ currently contains only evidencelint, routinglint, and runtimelint. The expected Verification mapping row model and analyzer helpers therefore have no citation-granularity predicate for static check or artifact evidence. The governing contract is docs/helix/06-iterate/phase2-doc-truth-plan-2026-07-13.md:67, which requires coverage by a Verification mapping row rather than an unspecific pointer.

PROPOSED FIX
Add or extend the spechonesty citation-granularity predicate near the Verification mapping row model supplied by the mapping-parser child. For non-test evidence, the predicate must return true when the row names an exact static check or artifact target. It must not treat a bare file path as a targeted artifact unless the mapping row explicitly identifies an artifact target rather than only pointing at a file. Keep the implementation read-only and follow cli/tools/lint/evidencelint/analyzer.go and cli/tools/lint/evidencelint/analyzer_test.go conventions, including golang.org/x/tools/go/analysis and analysistest-style fixtures where applicable.

NON-SCOPE
Do not implement file-only test-path or exact Test* symbol behavior except as needed to preserve an existing predicate API; that is covered by a sibling child. Do not implement the zero-evidence empty-row-set diagnostic. Do not implement uncovered or duplicate cardinality diagnostics; this child only supplies static-check and artifact-target behavior for the exclusion predicate feeding that sibling pass. Do not handle waivers. Do not parse requirement inventories or mapping tables beyond using the mapping-parser child model. Do not implement status parsing. Do not auto-restamp documents, infer proof from prose, fetch network state, or mark aspirational metrics complete. Do not implement duplicate-id or stale-observation detection. Prose quality and AC numbering style are out of scope. Do not resolve whether named static checks or artifacts actually exist on disk; this child only inspects whether the row names a target at all. Do not enforce the executable verification command allowlist.

DEPS: parent ddx-29449fa5 and its parent ddx-471d66b6; the spechonesty scaffold/status-parser child; the Verification mapping-parser child that provides the inventory + rows model. GOVERNING ARTIFACT: docs/helix/06-iterate/phase2-doc-truth-plan-2026-07-13.md WB-1 steps 3-4.

description:
PROBLEM
A Complete or Implemented Helix document can cite a verification observation captured at a stale repository revision, so a checked-in assertion that a command once passed is treated as current proof.

ROOT CAUSE WITH FILE:LINE
After the spechonesty scaffold/status-parser child lands, cli/tools/lint/spechonesty/analyzer.go:1 is the analyzer entrypoint but has no observation-freshness check. The governing contract is docs/helix/06-iterate/phase2-doc-truth-plan-2026-07-13.md:68, which requires Complete/Implemented mappings to have current-revision, exit-zero observations and rejects checked-in assertions that a command passed as sufficient proof. docs/helix/06-iterate/phase2-doc-truth-plan-2026-07-13.md:33 and docs/helix/06-iterate/phase2-doc-truth-plan-2026-07-13.md:176 repeat that Complete/Implemented documents require passing observations produced for the current repository revision and no waiver path exists for those statuses.

PROPOSED FIX
Add deterministic read-only observation freshness validation to spechonesty. Inject the current repository revision and any fixture clock/test revision source so unit tests are hermetic and do not fetch network state. For each Complete/Implemented Verification mapping row, require an observation keyed to the injected current revision with exit code 0. Fail rows whose observation revision differs from the current revision, whose exit code is non-zero, or whose observation is only prose rather than structured evidence. Keep the scan scope aligned with WB-1: docs/helix/01-frame/features/ plus docs/helix/02-design/{adr,concepts,contracts,solution-designs,technical-designs}/.

NON-SCOPE
Do not auto-restamp documents, infer proof from prose, fetch network state, or mark aspirational metrics complete. Complete-coverage/waiver logic and status parsing live in sibling children. Prose quality and AC numbering style are out of scope. Duplicate document-id and duplicate US-id detection are out of scope for this child.

GOVERNING ARTIFACT
Phase 2 doc truth plan WB-1 step 4 and exit requirement: docs/helix/06-iterate/phase2-doc-truth-plan-2026-07-13.md:68 and docs/helix/06-iterate/phase2-doc-truth-plan-2026-07-13.md:176.

PARENT: ddx-af66f903. SOURCE/PARENT BEAD: ddx-2e992616. DEPS: the spechonesty scaffold/status-parser child that provides cli/tools/lint/spechonesty/ and status/verification-row parsing.

description:
PROBLEM
After an execution provider exits with task_failed and leaves implementation edits, DDx synthesizes an iteration commit. That commit runs the repository pre-commit hook even though the provider already ran or failed the same gate. On 2026-07-13, the failed ddx-0f29e87a attempt entered the internal/agent race suite a second time during synthesis and recreated real Codex provider processes, consuming CPU and preventing prompt failure finalization.

ROOT CAUSE WITH FILE:LINE
cli/internal/agent/execute_bead.go:1297-1383 invokes GitOps.SynthesizeCommit whenever the attempt worktree is dirty and HEAD did not move, including when exitCode is non-zero and the preliminary outcome is task_failed. cli/internal/agent/gitops_real.go:151-180 stages the implementation diff and executes plain git commit -m, so repository hooks run inside DDx orchestration. The durable DDx audit paths already use --no-verify at cli/internal/agent/durable_audit.go:125-128 and cli/internal/agent/execute_bead.go:1724-1731, demonstrating the intended separation between orchestration-owned commits and user-invoked validation.

PROPOSED FIX
Make RealGitOps.SynthesizeCommit create the DDx-owned synthesized attempt commit without invoking repository hooks. Preserve the substantive dirty diff and the per-attempt commit-message/audit contract. Keep validation in the provider run and DDx gate/review pipeline; do not silently reinterpret a failed attempt as success.

NON-SCOPE
Do not skip provider-requested gates, landing gates, or operator git hooks. Do not discard failed implementation edits or rewrite existing execute-bead history. Do not weaken test assertions or timeouts.

PARENT AND DEPS
Parent: ddx-5958e8a. Depends on ddx-aa6cc320 so the package gate cannot itself launch real provider fixtures while this fix is verified.

description:
PROBLEM
The default linked-worktree attempt backend creates an isolated checkout but stores its Git administrative directory under the primary repository at .git/worktrees/<attempt>. Sandboxed Codex agents that can write only their attempt workspace can edit code but cannot create index.lock, so completed changes fail to commit and DDx reports execution_failed / no evidence after expensive attempts.

ROOT CAUSE WITH FILE:LINE
cli/internal/agent/attempt_backend.go:87-104 resolves an empty attempt backend to AttemptBackendWorktree. WorktreeAttemptBackend.Prepare at lines 111-137 calls git worktree add; RealGitOps.WorktreeAdd at cli/internal/agent/gitops_real.go:27-34 creates linked-worktree metadata outside the sandbox-visible checkout. LocalCloneAttemptBackend.Prepare at attempt_backend.go:194-231 gives each attempt its own .git directory inside the workspace.

PROPOSED FIX
Make local-clone the binary default whenever no backend is explicitly configured. Preserve explicit worktree support for operators whose sandbox contract permits writes to the primary repository Git metadata. Update public config/docs to describe the sandbox requirement and add proofs for default selection and a commit from a clone-contained Git directory.

NON-SCOPE
Do not make DDx choose Fizeau harnesses or models, change Fizeau routing, bypass Git commits, widen Codex sandbox permissions, or rewrite execution audit history.

description:
PROBLEM
A DDx run record that is created before dispatch must advance to running when Fizeau public execution data first exists. Without this update, readers continue to infer active state from session directories, execution bundles, or provider-specific artifacts.

ROOT CAUSE WITH FILE:LINE
cli/internal/agent/service_run.go:230-233 calls FizeauService.Execute and then consumes public execution events, while cli/internal/server/state_runs.go:295-317 and cli/internal/server/state_runs.go:465-490 still synthesize run-layer state from sessions and bundles when no stored record exists. The Phase 3 WB-2 plan at docs/helix/06-iterate/phase3-server-rebuild-plan-2026-07-13.md:104-149 requires the DDx-owned record to transition from dispatching to running using public immediate execution fields, not provider-session canonical state.

PROPOSED FIX
When Fizeau public execution data first exists, atomically update the existing .ddx/runs/<run-id>/record.json from dispatching to running. Record only public route/result fields that are exposed through the typed Fizeau execution contract. Ensure the read side observes the stored running record without needing provider session synthesis for this path.

NON-SCOPE
Do not query provider sessions for canonical state, build the UI migration, implement legacy migration, choose a Fizeau route, implement terminal outcome updates, or implement kill-interruption atomicity tests beyond the normal writer contract used by this transition.

GOVERNING ARTIFACT
docs/helix/06-iterate/phase3-server-rebuild-plan-2026-07-13.md:104-149, WB-2 run substrate.

Original bead ddx-61c41896. Queue parent field ddx-5bf0f8d0.

Phase 1 typed Fizeau result contract and Phase 0 safe execution exit. Requires the run-record schema/writer and pre-dispatch publish children to be available before final wiring.

description:
PROBLEM
DDx pins Fizeau v0.14.50, whose subprocess discovery refresher discards its bounded context and whose Codex model discovery launches ptyquota with context.Background. A cancelled DDx request or stopped server can therefore return while codex --no-alt-screen continues consuming CPU and writing caller-owned temp/cache state. DDx-side containment wrappers reduce symptoms but do not repair the dependency lifecycle.

ROOT CAUSE WITH FILE:LINE
- cli/go.mod:7 pins github.com/easel/fizeau v0.14.50.
- In that release, Fizeau internal/serviceimpl/subprocess_discovery_cache.go:74-94 ignores the discoverycache.Refresher context before calling DefaultModelSnapshot.
- In that release, Fizeau internal/harnesses/codex/model_discovery.go:20-48 calls ptyquota.Run(context.Background(), ...).
- cli/cmd/lifecycle_model_discovery_test.go proves DDx's outer containment helper, but a local wrapper test cannot prove the Fizeau cache refresher or PTY receives cancellation.

PROPOSED FIX
Wait for upstream fizeau-d25b2862 to add a context-aware model-discovery contract, pass the refresh context through subprocessDiscoveryRefresher, and reap the Codex PTY on cancellation. After an upstream release contains that closing commit, bump cli/go.mod and cli/go.sum to that release. Add DDx integration coverage proving the service lifecycle cancellation reaches dependency discovery, returns only after the probe is reaped, and produces no late cache/home writes. Verify the existing embedded dispatch temp-root regressions with the released dependency.

IN-SCOPE FILES
- cli/go.mod
- cli/go.sum
- cli/cmd/lifecycle_model_discovery_test.go and the nearest DDx service-lifecycle integration fixture

NON-SCOPE
Do not patch Fizeau source in the DDx repository, add a local replace directive, certify the existing outer containment wrapper as the upstream fix, disable discovery, extend the two-second caller timeout, kill manual Codex sessions, or change route selection.

PARENT AND DEPS
Parent: ddx-f84ee9a7. Externally blocked by fizeau#fizeau-d25b2862. Related to ddx-092f0d34 and regression ddx-403e9a23.

description:
PROBLEM
DDx estimates missing cost from concrete model and harness identity, accepts its own local price input, and stores execution cost in a value-only field. That makes absent cost indistinguishable from explicit zero and presents DDx guesses as accounting facts. Cost must be only the value Fizeau reported, with explicit presence preserved from execution through indexing, metrics, CLI, and GraphQL.

ROOT CAUSE WITH FILE:LINE
cli/internal/agent/pricing.go:3-35 owns DDx model pricing and EstimateCost. cli/cmd/usage_support.go:54-72 and cli/internal/processmetrics/processmetrics.go:1274-1323 estimate missing cost from route identity. cli/internal/config/types.go:319-322 still accepts DDx local_per_1k_tokens pricing. cli/internal/agent/types.go:106-133 defines Result.CostUSD as value-only. cli/internal/agent/service_run.go:324-346 copies final cost only when greater than zero. cli/internal/agent/session_index.go:22-40 has CostPresent but lines 206-221 and 240-293 synthesize it from nonzero values. cli/internal/server/state_graphql.go:818-820 drops explicit zero.

PROPOSED FIX
Delete cli/internal/agent/pricing.go, EstimateCost, DDx local price configuration, and every model/provider/harness identity cost estimate. Add explicit cost presence at agent.Result and translate the public Fizeau terminal contract exactly: nil is unknown, non-nil 0.0 is known zero, and non-nil positive is known positive. Preserve that distinction through session writes/reindex, usage and process metrics, and GraphQL. Historical records without presence remain unknown. Aggregates sum only present values and expose unknown participation instead of fabricating a complete total.

NON-SCOPE
Do not classify billing mode, add a replacement DDx price table or remote pricing lookup, reinterpret missing as zero/free, change Fizeau pricing, or use reported cost for routing, retry, escalation, review grading, admission, or close policy. Fizeau predicted candidate cost remains audit evidence and is not DDx pricing.

PARENT
ddx-1b3272a6.

DEPS
ddx-00d406ce supplies released Fizeau terminal cost presence and its public conformance proof.

description:
PROBLEM
DDx currently guesses that reviewer errors are transport failures from error strings, raises reviewer power/profile on retry, and ultimately fails or parks otherwise valid implementation work. The design requires Fizeau to classify its own terminal transport outcome; DDx may retry one review operation at identical power and passthrough, then downgrade to deterministic-only close with operator-visible evidence.

ROOT CAUSE WITH FILE:LINE
- cli/internal/agent/execute_bead_loop.go:7949-7991 ClassifyReviewError uses text and defaults unknown errors to transport.
- cli/internal/agent/execute_bead_review.go:869-931 increases MinPower and selects top profiles after prior errors.
- cli/internal/agent/execute_bead_review.go:1251-1292 and execute_bead_review_group.go:153-175 return dispatch errors as review failures.
- cli/internal/agent/candidate_cycle.go:315-325 converts any reviewer error to review_malfunction and prevents landing.
- Current pinned Fizeau v0.14.50 in cli/go.mod exposes no typed Cause/Stage field, so this change must wait for ddx-66a8883f and its compatible upstream release/conformance proof.

PROPOSED FIX
Consume the single typed Fizeau terminal review-transport cause from the DDx attempt-policy adapter. Retry exactly once at identical MinPower and byte-identical operator passthrough. If the typed transport failure repeats, emit an operator-visible review-downgraded event and allow deterministic-checks-only close. Do not raise power, select a profile, or fail the implementation because review transport is unavailable. Non-transport review errors remain distinct and follow their typed policy.

NON-SCOPE
Do not classify provider text, implement Fizeau provider retry, add continuation, invoke provider CLIs, or weaken semantic BLOCK/REQUEST_CHANGES findings.

PARENT AND DEPS

description:
PROBLEM
TD-027 §21 requires the agent and server layers to compile against bead interface contracts before storage concretes are relocated. These packages still have many *bead.Store test fixtures, helper wrappers, and production escape hatches that make the later internal-package move too broad and fragile.

ROOT CAUSE with file:line
- cli/internal/server/workers.go:1580 accepts *bead.Store in staleDiskEntryCanReleaseClaim.
- cli/internal/server/graphql/ddxroot_paths.go:12 returns *bead.Store from projectBeadStore.
- cli/internal/server/graphql/resolver_mutation_beads.go:14 returns *bead.Store from mutationResolver.beadStore.
- cli/internal/agent/execute_bead_integration_test.go:199 type-asserts a store back to *bead.Store.
- cli/internal/agent/execute_bead_loop.go:5896 documents deterministic ready-queue eligibility as bead.Store-specific instead of depending on an interface.

PROPOSED FIX
Update agent, agent/try, server, and server/graphql production code and test helpers to accept bead.Backend, bead.ReadOnlyBackend, or existing narrow sub-interfaces where the concrete is not required. Introduce local test-only fakes/adapters where a test currently embeds *bead.Store only to satisfy a small method set. Preserve concrete construction only at the package boundary where NewStore/NewStoreWithCollection is called.

- Do not change command/metrics caller clusters assigned to the sibling caller-narrowing child.
- Do not move storage concrete definitions or aliases.
- Do not relocate lifecycle WatcherHub.
- Do not change queue semantics, claim semantics, retry policy, worker lifecycle policy, or GraphQL behavior except for type narrowing.
- Do not implement per-concern L/C/X/Q/D/A/MIG behavior or AxonStore/AxonBackend behavior.
- Do not manually edit .ddx/beads.jsonl.
- Do not fix unrelated provider-launch/orphan integration flakes; if cd cli && go test ./... is blocked by pre-existing failures, report exact failing Test* names and leave this child’s changes otherwise verified.

description: PROBLEM: on 2026-07-06..2026-07-19 two ddx drains of telepathdata/cayce silently forked the repo: one checkout had branch.master.merge=refs/heads/main while the repo default was refs/heads/master, so each worker fleet pushed commits AND the beads.jsonl tracker to a different remote branch for 13 days. Because the tracker lives in git, forking the branch forks the queue itself — both sides showed healthy progress, duplicated ~100 non-chore commits of work under different bead IDs, and nobody was alerted. Recovered manually on 2026-07-20 (archive branch + delete + port-audit bead cayce-30ea87db). ROOT CAUSE: ddx work/try honor whatever upstream the checkout is configured with and have no preflight check that the branch being drained is (or descends from) the remote's default branch (origin/HEAD). PROPOSED FIX: before claiming the first bead, ddx work (and ddx try) resolve origin/HEAD and compare with the current branch's upstream: hard-fail with a clear message when the upstream ref names a different branch than origin/HEAD (override flag, e.g. --allow-non-default-branch, for deliberate feature-branch drains); also warn when the local branch is behind its upstream at drain start. Same check surfaced in ddx doctor.

description:
PROBLEM
The targeted Go pre-commit helper can report success without running any tests when it is invoked from the repository root with the same root-relative cli/... paths that Git and operator diagnostics naturally produce. During execute-bead attempt 20260713T171608-d879ec96, sh scripts/lefthook-go-test.sh cli/internal/agent/execute_bead.go returned 0 in 123ms and launched no go process, creating false validation evidence after the real package gate had timed out.

ROOT CAUSE WITH FILE:LINE
scripts/lefthook-go-test.sh:8-18 converts each input to a directory, strips a leading cli/, and silently continues when that derived directory does not exist relative to the current working directory. lefthook.yml:11-14 and lefthook.yml:205-216 normally run the helper with cli/ as the command root, but the helper neither establishes nor validates that working-directory contract. From the repository root, cli/internal/agent becomes internal/agent, the directory check fails, and the helper exits with its initial zero status.

PROPOSED FIX
Make the helper resolve the Go module root deterministically from its own repository location or explicitly normalize both repository-root cli/... paths and cli-root internal/... paths before selecting packages. Track every Go path supplied to the helper and fail nonzero with a diagnostic naming any path that cannot be mapped to an existing module package. Preserve targeted package selection, the race detector, the 30-minute per-package timeout, and compatibility with the normal Lefthook cli/ root.

IN-SCOPE FILES
- scripts/lefthook-go-test.sh
- lefthook.yml only if invocation wiring needs an explicit root argument
- a Go or shell-backed regression test under cli/internal/agent that runs the helper with a fake go executable and inspects its arguments

NON-SCOPE
Do not broaden the hook to the full repository, remove -race, raise or remove the timeout, silently ignore unmapped Go paths, or change which staged files Lefthook passes to the command.

PARENT
None; root hook-validation reliability defect discovered during the Niflheim queue drain.

DEPS
None. Related prior hook reliability work is ddx-42a86089; duplicate-hook work is ddx-8a78ee90.

description:
PROBLEM
Duplicate document ids (TD-040 class) pass unnoticed, so two conflicting Helix artifacts can both look authoritative with no lint failure.

ROOT CAUSE WITH FILE:LINE
After the spechonesty scaffold/status-parser child lands, cli/tools/lint/spechonesty/analyzer.go:1 is the analyzer entrypoint but has no duplicate document-id scan. The governing contract docs/helix/06-iterate/phase2-doc-truth-plan-2026-07-13.md:70 (WB-1 step 5-6) requires a failure for duplicate document ids across docs/helix/01-frame/features/ plus docs/helix/02-design/{adr,concepts,contracts,solution-designs,technical-designs}/. docs/helix/06-iterate/phase2-doc-truth-plan-2026-07-13.md:69 says waivers cannot suppress duplicate-id failures.

PROPOSED FIX
Add deterministic read-only duplicate document-id detection to spechonesty. Establish a reusable directory-walk helper in cli/tools/lint/spechonesty/ that scans exactly docs/helix/01-frame/features/ and the five local docs/helix/02-design/ subdirectories (adr, concepts, contracts, solution-designs, technical-designs) — no other paths, no network. Fail when two documents share the same document id, reporting enough location detail to identify both conflicting files. Mark this failure class non-waivable so any waiver parser/status logic from sibling children cannot downgrade it.

NON-SCOPE
Do not auto-restamp documents, infer proof from prose, fetch network state, or mark aspirational metrics complete. Complete-coverage/waiver logic and status parsing live in sibling children. Duplicate user-story-id (US-087/US-088) detection is a sibling child and out of scope here. Prose quality and AC numbering style are out of scope. Stale current-revision observation validation is out of scope.

GOVERNING ARTIFACT
Phase 2 doc truth plan WB-1 steps 5-6: docs/helix/06-iterate/phase2-doc-truth-plan-2026-07-13.md:69-70.

5. cd cli && go test ./internal/agent -run "TestExecutionCleanup_(PreservesLiveFixtureBinaryScratch|ReclaimsDeadFixtureBinaryScratch|PreservesUnownedFixtureBinaryScratch|DefaultPrefixesRequireFixtureOwnerMarker)$" -count=1 passes.

description:
PROBLEM
The cleanup allowlist recognizes ddx-fixture-bin-* but not ddx-fizeau-testseam-bin-*. Adding the missing prefix without ownership evidence would make directory age alone sufficient to delete a live process-owned binary directory. Cleanup must reclaim abandoned directories for both prefixes while preserving any directory still owned by a live process.

ROOT CAUSE WITH FILE:LINE
cli/internal/agent/execution_cleanup.go:26-46 includes ddx-fixture-bin-* in defaultExecutionCleanupScratchPrefixes but omits ddx-fizeau-testseam-bin-*.
cli/internal/agent/execution_cleanup.go:667-681 synthesizes ownership when cleanup.json is absent, while cli/internal/agent/execution_cleanup.go:728-755 removes an allowlisted directory after the age threshold when no liveness evidence preserves it.
cli/internal/agent/execution_cleanup.go:189-221 preserves a directory with live PID or lease evidence only when compatible metadata exists.

PROPOSED FIX
Teach execution cleanup to recognize both ddx-fixture-bin-* and ddx-fizeau-testseam-bin-* through the internal/scratchowner marker contract. Preserve an old directory while its recorded owner process identity is live; reclaim it only after the owner is dead or conclusively mismatched and the existing minimum-age requirement is satisfied. When process identity cannot be validated safely, preserve the directory and emit a structured uncertain-owner observation. Missing or malformed markers follow the ownership rules from ddx-05e3d16b and ddx-1eb1ba93; a prefix alone is never host-global ownership proof. Add ddx-fizeau-testseam-bin-* to defaultExecutionCleanupScratchPrefixes only with the owner-marker preservation path wired, and apply the same ownership and liveness policy to both fixture prefixes.

IN-SCOPE FILES
- cli/internal/agent/execution_cleanup.go and execution_cleanup_test.go

NON-SCOPE
Do not modify fixture_repo.go producers; sibling bead ddx owns marker emission.
Do not change Fizeau routing, test-seam behavior, harness selection, model selection, or provider policy.
Do not redesign general host-global scratch trust; ddx-05e3d16b and ddx-1eb1ba93 own that policy.
Do not reclaim a metadata-less or uncertain-owner host-global directory merely because its name matches a DDx prefix.
Do not change execution scratch placement; ddx-b2702b9f owns that migration.

PARENT
ddx-f914dddd

DEPS
Sibling bead ddx (internal/scratchowner marker contract) must land first so cleanup can read markers.
Sibling bead ddx (fixture producers write marker) must land first so live directories carry owner evidence in tests.
ddx-b2702b9f must land first so both producers use the configured scratch root.
ddx-1eb1ba93 must land first so metadata-marked stale reclamation and host-global ownership rules are established; it already depends on ddx-05e3d16b.

description:
PROBLEM
Running the required cd cli && go test ./internal/agent/... gate launches five real Codex provider processes from TestExecuteBead_ConcurrentWorkers_NoHEADRefRace. In the 2026-07-13 ddx-2502d3c6 attempt, the package test spawned PIDs 225004, 225054, 225173, 225576, and 226111 as __provider-launch ... codex exec; each ran for more than six minutes at about 10-12% CPU. The test package approached its 10-minute timeout, blocking the single queue worker and consuming server-cgroup CPU for a test whose stated concern is only parent-repo Git serialization.

ROOT CAUSE WITH FILE:LINE
cli/internal/agent/execute_bead_concurrent_predispatch_test.go:31-55 builds five production NewRunner(Config{}) instances and labels directive-file paths as model names under the obsolete script route. cli/internal/agent/execute_bead_concurrent_predispatch_test.go:73-89 then calls ExecuteBeadWithConfig concurrently with those production runners. The current service-backed runner resolves the request to Codex, so each directive path is passed to codex exec as -m instead of being consumed by a hermetic script fixture. The test comments at cli/internal/agent/execute_bead_concurrent_predispatch_test.go:35-37 explicitly say agent output is irrelevant. The package previously had to be repaired for the same 600-second budget under ddx-1a0d4d26, but this fixture has regressed into live provider execution.

PROPOSED FIX
- Replace the five production runners in this Git-lock regression with an explicit bounded hermetic AgentRunner fixture that returns the minimal no-changes result needed to reach and validate pre-dispatch serialization.
- Preserve the real temporary Git repository, five concurrent ExecuteBeadWithConfig calls, tracker commits, worktree creation, and HEAD CAS assertions.
- Add a provider-spawn tripwire: real/fake codex, claude, gemini, and provider-launch lookup must fail the test immediately if invoked.
- Audit adjacent direct NewRunner plus Harness=script fixtures reached by the normal internal/agent package gate and migrate any that can invoke live providers to the same hermetic boundary.
- Ensure subprocesses are canceled and reaped on test failure or timeout.

NON-SCOPE
Do not weaken production provider discovery, reduce the concurrency below five, delete the HEAD race assertions, or skip the test. Live provider integration remains build-tagged/explicit integration coverage, not part of the default package gate.

PARENT
None; root regression bead.

DEPS
None.

description:
PROBLEM
DDx consumers need proof that Fizeau v0.15 Execute cancellation does not return while wrapped child or grandchild processes are still alive. Without a focused conformance test, downstream cleanup and lifecycle consumers can incorrectly assume process-tree containment from implementation details instead of the released public Fizeau contract.

cli/go.mod:5-8 pins github.com/easel/fizeau v0.14.50 and cli/go.sum:88-89 locks that version. cli/internal/agent/service_run.go:196-216 builds the public Execute request, while cli/internal/agent/service_run.go:283-367 consumes final events without proving cancellation waits for wrapped process-tree exit. cli/internal/agent/serviceconfig.go:17-48 is the sole production Fizeau constructor seam and should remain a seam rather than a place for DDx-specific process containment policy. docs/helix/06-iterate/phase1-lower-the-altitude-plan-2026-07-13.md:126-146 requires released public-boundary conformance before WB-1 consumers proceed.

The test must launch a wrapped process that spawns a child or grandchild, cancel Execute, and assert Execute returns only after both PIDs are gone.

NON-SCOPE

acceptance:
1. TestCompleteVerificationRejectsNonAllowlistedCommands passes: a Complete fixture with a Verification row command outside the executable verification allowlist emits a non-allowlisted-command diagnostic, while a fixture using an allowlisted command passes command validation.
2. TestCompleteVerificationCommandAllowlistChecks_ReadOnly passes: running command allowlist validation over fixtures does not modify any fixture file.
3. cd cli && go test ./tools/lint/spechonesty/... passes.
4. lefthook run pre-commit passes.
description:
PROBLEM
Complete/Implemented documents can claim verification with a Verification mapping row whose command is arbitrary prose or a non-executable/non-allowlisted shell command. That lets a Complete stamp rely on command text that spechonesty cannot safely execute as current-revision evidence.

ROOT CAUSE WITH FILE:LINE
The requested spechonesty analyzer path is absent in this checkout at cli/tools/lint/spechonesty/analyzer.go:1, and the parent analyzer work has not yet added command allowlist enforcement for parsed Verification rows. The governing contract is docs/helix/06-iterate/phase2-doc-truth-plan-2026-07-13.md:67, which requires each Complete/Implemented mapping row to name an allowlisted executable verification command. Current-revision executable verification is reinforced at docs/helix/06-iterate/phase2-doc-truth-plan-2026-07-13.md:176.

PROPOSED FIX
After the spechonesty scaffold/status-parser child and Verification mapping-parser child exist, add validation for the command field on every Complete/Implemented Verification mapping row. A mapping row command must match the executable verification allowlist accepted by spechonesty. Emit a non-allowlisted-command diagnostic for each command outside that allowlist, naming the rejected command. Keep the analyzer read-only and do not execute network-dependent checks.

NON-SCOPE
Do not handle waivers — that is the waiver child. Do not parse requirement inventories or mapping tables — that is the mapping-parser child. Do not auto-restamp documents, infer proof from prose, fetch network state, or mark aspirational metrics complete. Status parsing lives in the scaffold child. Duplicate-id and stale-observation detection are a sibling child. Prose quality and AC numbering style are out of scope. Do not enforce requirement coverage cardinality or duplicate mapping counts — the coverage-cardinality child owns that. Do not resolve Go Test* symbols, deterministic static check names, or inspectable runtime artifact existence — the evidence-target and runtime-artifact children own those checks.

DEPS: parent ddx-29449fa5; parent/root dependency ddx-471d66b6; the spechonesty scaffold/status-parser child; the Verification mapping-parser child that provides the inventory + rows model. GOVERNING ARTIFACT: docs/helix/06-iterate/phase2-doc-truth-plan-2026-07-13.md WB-1 steps 3-4.

1. TestStopProjectWorkersWaitsForRunWorkerFinalization uses a test-controlled executor finalization barrier and proves worker teardown cannot return after cancellation but before runWorker finalization completes.
2. TestStopProjectWorkersWaitsForRunWorkerFinalization proves teardown returns after the barrier is released, the worker record has a non-zero FinishedAt, and immediate os.RemoveAll of the fixture root succeeds without later worker writes recreating it.
3. stopProjectWorkers delegates to WorkerManager.Shutdown or an equivalent joining helper; it no longer treats runningManagedWorkerCount equal to zero as proof that the goroutine has exited.
4. TestUnpinnedEntryPointsLeaveModelSelectionToFizeau and TestWorkerSupervisor_ActiveBlockedTerminalConsumesOneDesiredSlot retain their existing assertions and pass repeatedly without test temporary-directory cleanup errors.
5. cd cli && go test ./internal/server -run "Test(StopProjectWorkersWaitsForRunWorkerFinalization|UnpinnedEntryPointsLeaveModelSelectionToFizeau|WorkerSupervisor_ActiveBlockedTerminalConsumesOneDesiredSlot)$" -count=20 passes.
6. cd cli && go test ./internal/server/... passes.
7. lefthook run pre-commit passes.
description:
PROBLEM
The internal/server package intermittently fails after otherwise successful tests because Go cannot remove a test-owned temporary project directory. Observed failures include TestUnpinnedEntryPointsLeaveModelSelectionToFizeau/server-managed leaving files beneath .ddx and TestWorkerSupervisor_ActiveBlockedTerminalConsumesOneDesiredSlot/does_not_suppress_all_starts_when_desired_count_exceeds_one leaving files beneath .ddx/workers. These unrelated tests share the same worker teardown helper.

ROOT CAUSE WITH FILE:LINE
cli/internal/server/workers_supervisor_test.go:1252-1271 implements stopProjectWorkers by calling WorkerManager.Stop and then waiting only until runningManagedWorkerCount returns zero.
cli/internal/server/workers.go:1684-1697 makes Stop set the in-memory worker state to stopped and return before the runWorker goroutine has completed.
cli/internal/server/workers.go:1332-1339 makes List overlay that stopped in-memory state, so runningManagedWorkerCount reaches zero while finalization is still active.
cli/internal/server/workers.go:1220-1293 subsequently records FinishedAt and writes the final status.json. That late write races removal of the test-owned project directory.
cli/internal/server/workers_resolve_route_test.go:213-216 and cli/internal/server/workers_supervisor_test.go:545-547 register the faulty helper in the two observed failing fixtures.
cli/internal/server/workers.go:1705-1806 already provides WorkerManager.Shutdown, which cancels live workers and waits for in-process runWorker finalization.

PROPOSED FIX
Replace the Stop-plus-state-poll implementation of stopProjectWorkers with a teardown path that delegates to WorkerManager.Shutdown and does not return until runWorker has written its final record.
If a separate error-returning test helper is useful, keep it private to internal/server tests and have stopProjectWorkers delegate to it.
Add TestStopProjectWorkersWaitsForRunWorkerFinalization. Use an injected ExecuteBeadWorker whose executor observes cancellation and then blocks on a test-controlled release channel. Start teardown asynchronously through the error-returning helper, prove teardown has not returned while finalization remains blocked, release the executor, then prove teardown returns, FinishedAt is persisted, and immediate removal of the fixture root succeeds.

NON-SCOPE
Do not change the asynchronous contract of WorkerManager.Stop.
Do not change managed subprocess termination, server supervisor cancellation deadlines, worker reconciliation, Fizeau routing, bead execution semantics, or production temporary-directory placement.
Do not weaken or skip either existing failing test.

PARENT
None. This is a standalone package-gate reliability defect.

DEPS
None. WorkerManager.Shutdown already implements the required join.

acceptance:
1. Add TestSupervisor_HistoricalOperatorAttentionDoesNotBlockFreshDesiredStateAcrossRestart proving old .ddx/workers/*/status.json records do not permanently suppress desired workers after a server restart.
2. cd cli && go test ./internal/server/... -run "TestSupervisor_OperatorAttentionTerminalDoesNotRespawn|TestSupervisor_ResolvedOperatorAttentionAllowsRespawnAfterDesiredUpdate|TestSupervisor_HistoricalOperatorAttentionDoesNotBlockFreshDesiredStateAcrossRestart" passes.
description:
PROBLEM
Parent bead ddx-4d92f2cf is too broad for one execution pass. This child owns part 2 of 3 of that parent scope.

ROOT CAUSE
PROBLEM
  Server-managed workers can remain absent even when .ddx/workers/desired.json has desired_count=1. On 2026-07-07, /home/erik/Projects/ddx had desired_count=1 and /home/erik/Projects/niflheim had desired_count=1, but ddx work status --all-projects --json showed only axon and helix workers. Both ddx and niflheim had older status=operator_attention worker records, while the current desired state still asked the supervisor to run one worker.

ROOT CAUSE
  cli/internal/server/workers_supervisor.go:364-374 records every restart-blocking terminal worker into blockedTerminals. cli/internal/server/workers_supervisor.go:417-419 then makes canStartMore return false whenever blockedTerminals is non-empty. There is no expiry, no check that the underlying dirty/root condition has been resolved, and no operator command/state transition that clears the block. Because snapshotWorkers reads historical terminal records from .ddx/workers, the block can survive server restarts and suppress a fresh desired worker indefinitely.

PROPOSED FIX
  - cli/internal/server/workers_supervisor.go:364-419: distinguish active unresolved operator-attention stops from stale historical records. A clean project root with a current desired state must be able to start again after the operator resolves the condition.
  - cli/internal/server/workers_supervisor.go:497-516: keep true restart-blocking semantics for genuinely unresolved dirty-root/operator-attention records, but add a deterministic release path keyed to resolved project state or an explicit desired-state update timestamp newer than the blocking worker.
  - cli/internal/server/workers_supervisor_test.go: add regression coverage for a historical operator_attention terminal followed by a newer desired state and clean project root.

NON-SCOPE
  - Do not weaken the dirty-root guard inside ddx work; a currently dirty implementation root must still stop.
  - Do not edit or delete existing .ddx/workers/*/status.json records as the fix. Worker history must remain durable.
  - Do not change routing/model/provider selection.

PARENT / DEPS
  Root operational bug. No deps.

PROPOSED FIX
Implement only this child acceptance slice:
- Add TestSupervisor_HistoricalOperatorAttentionDoesNotBlockFreshDesiredStateAcrossRestart proving old .ddx/workers/*/status.json records do not permanently suppress desired workers after a server restart.
- cd cli && go test ./internal/server/... -run "TestSupervisor_OperatorAttentionTerminalDoesNotRespawn|TestSupervisor_ResolvedOperatorAttentionAllowsRespawnAfterDesiredUpdate|TestSupervisor_HistoricalOperatorAttentionDoesNotBlockFreshDesiredStateAcrossRestart" passes.

NON-SCOPE
Do not implement parent acceptance criteria assigned to sibling child beads. Preserve every parent non-scope constraint unless this child explicitly narrows it.
