acceptance:
1. TestWorkStatusAllProjectsRetainsLiveWorkerListing proves `--all-projects` still lists every live worker and preserves each worker's project_root.
2. `cd cli && go test ./cmd/... -run 'TestWorkStatusAllProjectsRetainsLiveWorkerListing|TestWorkStatusAllProjectsShowsExplicitGlobalView|TestWorkStatusNoLiveWorkersNamesProjectRoot'` passes.
3. `lefthook run pre-commit` passes.
description:
PROBLEM
`ddx work status --all-projects` must keep reporting live workers even after the missing-desired-worker diagnostic lands elsewhere, but there is no regression coverage proving the global listing stays intact.

ROOT CAUSE WITH FILE:LINE
cli/cmd/work_status.go:80-116 builds work status only from live worker scans and active work.
cli/cmd/work_status.go:215-221 prints a single all-projects empty-state line, so there is no guard against a future change accidentally hiding live rows or mixing in desired-state diagnostics.

PROPOSED FIX
Add regression coverage for the all-projects live-worker listing and keep the formatter limited to live workers so the missing-desired-worker explanation stays in `ddx worker status`.

NON-SCOPE
Do not add desired-state reporting to `ddx work status`. Do not change the worker-status payload. Do not change restart accounting. Do not weaken byte/inode resource guards. Do not alter the stale operator-attention fixes tracked by ddx-b17cad6d and ddx-4d92f2cf. Do not implement a new classifier.

Governing artifact: ddx-9c53e551.

description:
PROBLEM
Shared DDx fixture binaries and several command-test HOME directories still allocate directly beneath the process-global OS temporary directory. These allocations bypass the configured execution scratch root or test-owned cleanup and can concentrate large binaries, configuration trees, and inode use in one host-global location.

ROOT CAUSE WITH FILE:LINE
cli/internal/testutils/fixture_repo.go:122 creates ddx-fixture-bin-* with os.MkdirTemp and an empty root.
cli/internal/testutils/fixture_repo.go:150 creates ddx-fizeau-testseam-bin-* the same way.
cli/cmd/work_resource_exhausted_test.go:80 and cli/cmd/work_resource_exhausted_test.go:163 create test-scoped ddx-home-* directories with raw os.MkdirTemp.
cli/cmd/try_test.go:830 creates another test-scoped ddx-home-* directory with raw os.MkdirTemp.
cli/cmd/doctor_test.go:85, cli/cmd/doctor_test.go:129, and cli/cmd/doctor_test.go:179 create additional test-scoped ddx-home-* directories with raw os.MkdirTemp.
cli/internal/config/execution_worktree_root.go:70-78 already provides config.MkdirExecutionScratch, so this child does not need a new production scratch-root abstraction.

PROPOSED FIX
Extract a small fixture-binary scratch-directory helper in cli/internal/testutils/fixture_repo.go and have both BuildDDxBinary and BuildDDxFizeauTestSeamBinary call config.MkdirExecutionScratch with an empty project root and their existing directory patterns. Preserve the sync.Once behavior and process-lifetime sharing; t.TempDir is not appropriate for binaries shared across tests.

Add cli/internal/testutils/fixture_repo_test.go with a table-driven test covering both fixture-binary patterns under a configured DDX_EXEC_WT_DIR.

description:
PROBLEM
Parent bead ddx-4d92f2cf is too broad for one execution pass. This child owns part 1 of 3 of that parent scope.

ROOT CAUSE
PROBLEM
  Server-managed workers can remain absent even when .ddx/workers/desired.json has desired_count=1. On 2026-07-07, /home/erik/Projects/ddx had desired_count=1 and /home/erik/Projects/niflheim had desired_count=1, but ddx work status --all-projects --json showed only axon and helix workers. Both ddx and niflheim had older status=operator_attention worker records, while the current desired state still asked the supervisor to run one worker.

ROOT CAUSE
  cli/internal/server/workers_supervisor.go:364-374 records every restart-blocking terminal worker into blockedTerminals. cli/internal/server/workers_supervisor.go:417-419 then makes canStartMore return false whenever blockedTerminals is non-empty. There is no expiry, no check that the underlying dirty/root condition has been resolved, and no operator command/state transition that clears the block. Because snapshotWorkers reads historical terminal records from .ddx/workers, the block can survive server restarts and suppress a fresh desired worker indefinitely.

PROPOSED FIX
  - cli/internal/server/workers_supervisor.go:364-419: distinguish active unresolved operator-attention stops from stale historical records. A clean project root with a current desired state must be able to start again after the operator resolves the condition.
  - cli/internal/server/workers_supervisor.go:497-516: keep true restart-blocking semantics for genuinely unresolved dirty-root/operator-attention records, but add a deterministic release path keyed to resolved project state or an explicit desired-state update timestamp newer than the blocking worker.
  - cli/internal/server/workers_supervisor_test.go: add regression coverage for a historical operator_attention terminal followed by a newer desired state and clean project root.

NON-SCOPE
  - Do not weaken the dirty-root guard inside ddx work; a currently dirty implementation root must still stop.
  - Do not edit or delete existing .ddx/workers/*/status.json records as the fix. Worker history must remain durable.
  - Do not change routing/model/provider selection.

PARENT / DEPS
  Root operational bug. No deps.

PROPOSED FIX
Implement only this child acceptance slice:
- TestSupervisor_OperatorAttentionTerminalDoesNotRespawn still proves an unresolved operator_attention worker is not immediately respawned.
- Add TestSupervisor_ResolvedOperatorAttentionAllowsRespawnAfterDesiredUpdate proving that a desired state update newer than the blocking terminal and a clean project root allow a new worker to start.

NON-SCOPE
Do not implement parent acceptance criteria assigned to sibling child beads. Preserve every parent non-scope constraint unless this child explicitly narrows it.

2. Existing `TestExecutor_ProviderSpawnSetsPdeathsigAndSetpgid` and cmd-package `TestProviderLaunchExecsProviderInDedicatedProcessGroup` remain green against an explicit DDx CLI/fake binary, proving production parent-death and process-group behavior is preserved.
description:
PROBLEM
Parent bead ddx-b291b0f6 is too broad for one execution pass. This child owns part 2 of 3 of that parent scope.

ROOT CAUSE
PROBLEM
The mandatory `cd cli && go test -short -race -timeout 30m ./internal/agent` gate recursively launches the package test binary as DDx's hidden provider wrapper. During attempt `20260713T190502-df5adc46`, the parent `agent.test` spawned five concurrent `agent.test __provider-launch <real-provider>` helpers for more than three minutes, grew a 666 MB testlog, and left a real `codex --no-alt-screen` process reparented to the managed worker for 12 minutes at about 188 MiB RSS. This makes the package gate itself create the CPU/memory/orphan condition it is supposed to prevent.

ROOT CAUSE WITH FILE:LINE
- `cli/internal/agent/agent_runner_service.go:102-113` calls `os.Executable()` unconditionally and passes that path to `EnsureProviderShimOnPATH`.
- `cli/internal/agent/service_run.go:152-163` repeats the same unconditional installation for the resolved-service path.
- `cli/internal/agent/provider_spawn.go:83-118` writes each shim as `<ddxBinary> __provider-launch <realBinary>`. Under `go test`, `os.Executable()` is `agent.test`, not the DDx CLI and it has no Cobra `__provider-launch` dispatch. Re-executing it starts the test suite again; the recursive process can install shims and launch real providers that escape the original gate process group.
- `cli/cmd/provider_launch.go:25-68` is the actual hidden-command implementation, and exists only in the DDx CLI command graph.

PROPOSED FIX
Introduce one injectable resolver for the provider-wrapper executable and use it from both service call sites. In package-test builds, install a suite-wide test resolver/guard that refuses to use the current `agent.test` executable as a provider wrapper while leaving direct `EnsureProviderShimOnPATH` tests free to supply an explicit real/fake DDx CLI binary. Fail closed with actionable evidence if a test fixture attempts to install a provider shim from a Go test binary. Preserve production PATH shim, `Pdeathsig`, process-group, and real CLI hidden-command behavior.

NON-SCOPE
- Do not remove provider parent-death protection in production.
- Do not replace Fizeau routing or provider discovery.
- Do not weaken the full `internal/agent` race gate or merely increase its timeout.
- Do not kill unrelated provider processes from other repositories.
- Scanner injection remains owned by `ddx-02200b1e`; fixture-specific spawn tripwires remain owned by `ddx-26bf19c7`.

PARENT AND DEPS
...[truncated]

PROPOSED FIX
Implement only this child acceptance slice:
- `TestAgentPackageSuite_DoesNotExecTestBinaryAsProviderLauncher` exercises the suite guard and proves no descendant command line matches `agent.test __provider-launch` and no real codex, claude, gemini, opencode, or pi process is launched.
- Existing `TestExecutor_ProviderSpawnSetsPdeathsigAndSetpgid` and cmd-package `TestProviderLaunchExecsProviderInDedicatedProcessGroup` remain green against an explicit DDx CLI/fake binary, proving production parent-death and process-group behavior is preserved.

NON-SCOPE
Do not implement parent acceptance criteria assigned to sibling child beads. Preserve every parent non-scope constraint unless this child explicitly narrows it.

description:
PROBLEM
Complete/Implemented documents can claim verification with a Verification mapping row whose evidence target is an inspectable runtime artifact path that does not exist. That lets a Complete stamp rely on unverifiable artifact names instead of current-revision evidence, and the analyzer currently reports nothing.

ROOT CAUSE WITH FILE:LINE
The spechonesty analyzer path is absent in this checkout at cli/tools/lint/spechonesty/analyzer.go:1, and the analyzer run has no runtime-artifact existence check over parsed Verification rows. The governing contract is docs/helix/06-iterate/phase2-doc-truth-plan-2026-07-13.md:67, requiring every Complete/Implemented mapping row to name an exact evidence target, and docs/helix/06-iterate/phase2-doc-truth-plan-2026-07-13.md:68, requiring rejection of mappings to nonexistent artifacts. Current-revision executable verification is reinforced at docs/helix/06-iterate/phase2-doc-truth-plan-2026-07-13.md:176.

PROPOSED FIX
Wire the runtime artifact target resolver into the spechonesty analyzer run. For each Complete/Implemented document mapping row classified as an inspectable runtime artifact target, emit a missing-artifact diagnostic when the target does not resolve, naming the path exactly as written in the mapping row and identifying the requirement and source document. Rows that resolve pass artifact validation and emit nothing. Keep the analyzer read-only.

NON-SCOPE
Do not reimplement target classification or path resolution — consume the resolver child. Do not handle waivers — that is the waiver child. Do not parse requirement inventories or mapping tables — that is the mapping-parser child. Do not auto-restamp documents, infer proof from prose, fetch network state, or mark aspirational metrics complete. Status parsing lives in the scaffold child. Duplicate-id and stale-observation detection are a sibling child. Prose quality and AC numbering style are out of scope. Do not enforce requirement coverage cardinality or duplicate mapping counts — the coverage-cardinality child owns that. Do not resolve Go Test* symbols or static check names — the evidence-target child owns those checks. Do not enforce command allowlisting — the verification-command allowlist child owns that.

DEPS: parent ddx-e743ce67; grandparent ddx-29449fa5; root dependency ddx-471d66b6; the spechonesty scaffold/status-parser child; the Verification mapping-parser child that provides the inventory + rows model; the runtime artifact target resolver child. GOVERNING ARTIFACT: docs/helix/06-iterate/phase2-doc-truth-plan-2026-07-13.md WB-1 steps 3-4.

description:
PROBLEM
While the managed DDx worker decomposed ddx-29491a0e on 2026-07-13, the preclaim-decompose Codex provider remained live for more than two minutes, but `ddx work status --json` changed to active_work.count=0 and reported no bead_id, phase, or last_activity_at. Operators therefore see an apparently idle worker while queue-critical model work is running.

ROOT CAUSE WITH FILE:LINE
cli/internal/agent/execute_bead_loop.go:1604-1617 constructs the sidecar liveness reporter but explicitly defers emission until a bead is claimed. cli/internal/agent/execute_bead_loop.go:3108-3120 invokes PostAttemptDecompositionHook before claim without setting a resolving phase or ticking liveness.

PROPOSED FIX
Publish candidate-scoped resolving liveness before dispatching preclaim decomposition, heartbeat it while the provider runs, and include provider-child observations without creating a bead lease. The sidecar status must expose the candidate bead ID, phase=resolving, refreshed last_activity_at, and provider-child metadata before any claim or lease exists.

NON-SCOPE
Do not claim the parent before decomposition, change decomposition prompts or AC-map validation, change queue ordering, or make preclaim model work count as an implementation attempt. Do not kill provider processes that predate the hook baseline or belong to another worker.

PARENT
Split from root reliability regression bead: work: surface, bound, and reap preclaim decomposition lifecycle.

DEPS
ddx-aa6cc320 must land first so the internal/agent verification gate does not launch five real Codex providers.

2. TestImplementedVerificationMissingRuntimeArtifactEmitsDiagnostic passes: an Implemented fixture mapping a requirement to a nonexistent inspectable runtime artifact emits a missing-artifact diagnostic naming the path exactly as written in the mapping row.
3. TestMissingRuntimeArtifactDoesNotFireForNonRuntimeTargets passes: unresolved evidence targets outside the inspectable runtime artifact classification do not emit the runtime missing-artifact diagnostic.

5. lefthook run pre-commit passes.
description:
PROBLEM
Complete/Implemented documents can claim verification with a Verification mapping row whose evidence target is an inspectable runtime artifact path that does not exist. That lets a Complete stamp rely on unverifiable artifact names instead of current-revision evidence, and the analyzer currently reports nothing.

ROOT CAUSE WITH FILE:LINE
The spechonesty analyzer path is absent in this checkout at cli/tools/lint/spechonesty/analyzer.go:1, and the analyzer run has no runtime-artifact existence check over parsed Verification rows. The governing contract is docs/helix/06-iterate/phase2-doc-truth-plan-2026-07-13.md:67, requiring every Complete/Implemented mapping row to name an exact evidence target, and docs/helix/06-iterate/phase2-doc-truth-plan-2026-07-13.md:68, requiring rejection of mappings to nonexistent artifacts. Current-revision executable verification is reinforced at docs/helix/06-iterate/phase2-doc-truth-plan-2026-07-13.md:176.

PROPOSED FIX
Extend the spechonesty analyzer runtime-artifact validation so each Complete/Implemented Verification mapping row classified as an inspectable runtime artifact target emits a missing-artifact diagnostic when the resolver cannot resolve the target. The diagnostic must name the artifact path exactly as written in the mapping row and must be emitted only for unresolved inspectable runtime artifact targets. Keep the analyzer read-only.

NON-SCOPE
Do not reimplement target classification or path resolution — consume the resolver child. Do not handle waivers — that is the waiver child. Do not parse requirement inventories or mapping tables — that is the mapping-parser child. Do not auto-restamp documents, infer proof from prose, fetch network state, or mark aspirational metrics complete. Status parsing lives in the scaffold child. Duplicate-id and stale-observation detection are a sibling child. Prose quality and AC numbering style are out of scope. Do not enforce requirement coverage cardinality or duplicate mapping counts — the coverage-cardinality child owns that. Do not resolve Go Test* symbols or static check names — the evidence-target child owns those checks. Do not enforce command allowlisting — the verification-command allowlist child owns that.

DEPS: parent ddx-e743ce67; grandparent ddx-29449fa5; root dependency ddx-471d66b6; the spechonesty scaffold/status-parser child; the Verification mapping-parser child that provides the inventory + rows model; the runtime artifact target resolver child. GOVERNING ARTIFACT: docs/helix/06-iterate/phase2-doc-truth-plan-2026-07-13.md WB-1 steps 3-4.

description:
PROBLEM
Parent bead ddx-53df5e2f requires post-migration verification that reads migrated beads back from Axon/Postgres and detects field-level drift. Drift detection should be independently executable from clean round-trip fixture expansion, dry-run behavior, write-path apply mechanics, and CLI routing.

ROOT CAUSE WITH FILE:LINE
The importer exposes MigrateAxonOptions.Verify at cli/internal/bead/import_postgres.go:38 and calls verifyImportedAxonCorpus from cli/internal/bead/import_postgres.go:113 after writes. If verifyImportedAxonCorpus or its comparison helpers are absent or shallow, ddx bead migrate --to-axon --verify can report success even when stored Axon data differs from the JSONL source corpus.

PROPOSED FIX
Implement or complete verifyImportedAxonCorpus and supporting comparison helpers so verification reads back the imported Axon target corpus, compares migrated source beads field-for-field, and returns an error that names the affected bead ID and the drifted field when target data is changed post-import. Keep implementation compatible with existing sample-based verification if a corpus-size threshold already exists; otherwise compare the bounded imported set produced by --limit or the full import.

NON-SCOPE
- Schema-versioning migration ladder; deferred until first v1-to-v2 breaking change.
- Real-wire integration test against actual Postgres; separate WIRE bead.
- Continuous sync between JSONL and Postgres.
- CLI flag parsing beyond consuming the Verify option; sibling child owns command UX.
- Core apply/idempotency mechanics except as needed to create verifier fixtures; sibling child owns apply path.
- Dry-run counting/no-mutation semantics; sibling child owns dry-run behavior.
- Clean round-trip fixture breadth for attachment/extras preservation; sibling child owns that proof.
- Do not claim or edit parent bead ddx-53df5e2f tracker data manually; tracker mutations must go through ddx bead commands.

GOVERNING CONTEXT
Spec: TD-027. Decomposition parent: ddx-53df5e2f. Upstream parent/dependency context: ddx-3d96c6f9.

1. TestTrackerStaleLockGuardCrashReleasesWithoutReplacingSidecar spawns a child process that Acquires the guard, signals the parent after actual advisory-lock acquisition, is killed and waited on; a successor Acquire in the parent then succeeds, and os.SameFile on the sidecar before and after proves the inode/path was never replaced.
2. Guard exposes both Unix (syscall.Flock LOCK_EX) and Windows (LockFileEx) implementations that operate on a single stable sidecar inode/path derived from the new package-local path helper, with keyed same-process coordination (path-keyed map + mutex) serializing intra-process callers.
3. Ordinary Acquire/Release never delete, truncate, rename, or recreate the sidecar; a non-contention open/lock error fails safe by returning an error rather than proceeding as held (asserted in TestTrackerStaleLockGuardCrashReleasesWithoutReplacingSidecar or a sibling unit test in the same file).
4. Run, naming the final guard source/test files after implementation: cd cli && GOOS=windows GOARCH=amd64 go test -c <final guard source/test file list> succeeds.
5. cd cli && go test -race ./internal/agent/... -run "TestTrackerStaleLockGuardCrashReleasesWithoutReplacingSidecar" -count=20 passes.
6. cd cli && go test ./internal/agent/... -timeout 600s passes.
7. lefthook run pre-commit passes.
description:
PROBLEM
The process-shared main-git tracker lock has no crash-safe advisory guard primitive that lets a single stale-breaker win a cross-process transition. There is currently no OS advisory lock and no package-local sidecar path helper to build one on.

ROOT CAUSE WITH FILE:LINE
cli/internal/agent/tracker_lock.go:215-278 (withTrackerLockPolicy) retries os.Mkdir on the canonical lock and classifies existing objects with no cross-process advisory serialization. cli/internal/agent/tracker_lock_unix.go:9 and cli/internal/agent/tracker_lock_windows.go:10 only implement trackerProcessAlive; there is no advisory-lock acquire/release. cli/internal/agent/tracker_lock.go:99-101 (trackerLockPath) resolves the canonical lock via lockmetrics.SharedTrackerLockPath but exposes no sibling sidecar path.

GOVERNING ARTIFACT
Phase 0 WB-5 single-winner cross-process stale-break protocol: docs/helix/06-iterate/phase0-stop-the-self-harm-plan-2026-07-13.md:124-132.

PROPOSED FIX
Add one package-local path helper (e.g. trackerLockGuardPath(projectRoot)) that derives a deterministic never-deleted sibling advisory-lock file whose name ends in .lock, adjacent to the canonical trackerLockPath. Add a crash-safe guard type with Acquire/Release: Unix uses syscall.Flock(fd, LOCK_EX) on a never-deleted file, Windows uses LockFileEx on a never-deleted HANDLE; the OS lock releases automatically on handle close or process death. Add keyed same-process coordination (package-level map keyed by resolved sidecar path + sync.Mutex) so two goroutines in one process serialize before touching the shared fd. Ordinary acquisition and release MUST NOT delete, truncate, rename, or recreate the sidecar inode/path — only open/lock/unlock/close. Non-contention open/lock errors fail safe (return an error, do not proceed as if held). Provide both Unix and Windows implementations. Because the dependency graph does not cross-compile for Windows, include a self-contained cross-compile smoke command in AC 4 naming the final guard source/test files.

NON-SCOPE
This child does NOT change withTrackerLockPolicy's observe/mutate flow, breakStaleTrackerLock, or wire the guard into the stale-break transition (owned by the sibling integration child). It does NOT touch synthesizeCommitExcludePathspecs, preDispatchCheckpointIgnoredPath, or checkoutSyncDeferralIgnoredPath (owned by the ignore-wiring child). Do not change tracker mutation semantics, tracker record format, trackerLockStaleAge, LockRetryPolicy defaults, lockmetrics caps, harness/Fizeau behavior, bead-store locks, git index locks, or the execution-cleanup lock in cli/internal/agent/execution_cleanup_loop.go:116-156. Do not extract a shared lock package; ddx-dffb7454 and ddx-3f156500 own separate sites and Phase 1 WB-8 owns unification. Do not implement token-bearing lease release or stale directory/file disposal beyond what is needed to exercise guard acquire/release.

PARENT
ddx-1c8d9319

DEPS
None. ddx-dffb7454 is a related collection-lock implementation, not a prerequisite or shared-package dependency.

acceptance:
1. TestOfflineJournal_SafeCompaction verifies compaction never drops an unacknowledged mutation.
2. TestOfflineJournal_SafeCompaction verifies compacted and reopened journals preserve unacknowledged mutations in original order with idempotency key, payload hash, precondition, and outcome fields intact.
3. TestOfflineJournal_SafeCompaction verifies acknowledged-through state and next monotonic sequence number survive compaction and close/reopen.
4. cd cli && go test ./internal/agent/... -run "TestOfflineJournal_SafeCompaction" passes.
5. lefthook run pre-commit passes.
description:
<context-digest>
<principles>Spec-first development · Executable specifications · Audit trail required · Work is a DAG · Drift is debt · Inspect and adapt</principles>
<concerns>go-std | security-owasp | testing</concerns>
<practices>Go domain interface with contract tests against real implementations · project-scoped durable files · no call-recording mocks · go test + lefthook</practices>
<adrs>ADR-022 rev 6 requires one reconnecting coordination client, durable ordered offline journal, idempotency keys, and a cross-process offline project lock.</adrs>
<governing>FEAT-006 Worker Contract: connected mutations use the server; disconnected manual workers apply the same operations locally and reconcile before new online writes.</governing>
</context-digest>

PROBLEM
The offline coordination journal needs bounded durable storage, but compaction can corrupt reconciliation if it drops unacknowledged mutations or strips idempotency keys, payload hashes, preconditions, outcomes, sequence order, or acknowledgement state.

ROOT CAUSE WITH FILE:LINE
cli/internal/agent/workerprobe/probe.go:129-224 has no durable ordered mutation journal or compaction boundary. cli/cmd/try.go:256-259 and cli/cmd/execute_loop_shared.go:280-282 construct local landing coordination directly, so there is no tested journal compaction behavior to preserve unacknowledged offline mutations before later online reconciliation.

PROPOSED FIX
Add safe compaction to the offline journal under cli/internal/agent. Compaction may remove acknowledged records at or below the durable acknowledgement-through sequence but must preserve all unacknowledged records in original order, keep their idempotency key, payload hash, precondition, and outcome fields, and retain enough state to continue monotonic sequence numbering after reopen.

NON-SCOPE
Do not add server routes, wire Cobra commands, centralize bead picking, or change process ownership. Do not implement the HTTP coordination client. Do not wire Cobra command flows to the journal in this bead beyond package-level production APIs and tests.

PARENT
- ddx-635ae251.

DEPS
- No deps.

1. TestVerificationMappingParser passes: a fixture declaring requirement IDs yields those IDs in order; a fixture declaring none yields its section anchors as the inventory; a well-formed Verification table yields rows each exposing requirement ref, evidence target, and command; and rows missing a requirement ref, evidence target, or command each produce a parse-level finding.

description:
PROBLEM
Before coverage can be enforced, the analyzer must know, for any Complete/Implemented document, (a) the set of normative requirement IDs it declares (or, when it declares none, its stable section anchors) and (b) the rows of its Verification mapping table. Today none of this is parsed, so downstream coverage logic has nothing structured to check against.

ROOT CAUSE WITH FILE:LINE
The spechonesty analyzer at cli/tools/lint/spechonesty/analyzer.go (created by the scaffold/status-parser child) parses only status; it has no requirement-inventory or Verification-mapping parser. The contract is docs/helix/06-iterate/phase2-doc-truth-plan-2026-07-13.md WB-1 step 3.

PROPOSED FIX
Add a read-only pass that, for each parsed document, produces (1) an ordered list of normative requirement IDs, falling back to stable section anchors when the document declares no requirement IDs, and (2) a list of Verification mapping rows, each row exposing its requirement/anchor reference, its evidence target string (a `Test*` symbol, a named static check, or an inspectable runtime artifact path), and its executable verification command string. Emit a structured model only; do not resolve targets, do not judge coverage, do not mutate any file. Malformed rows (missing requirement ref, missing evidence target, or missing command) must be surfaced as parse-level findings so later stages can rely on well-formed rows.

NON-SCOPE
Do not resolve whether a named test/check/artifact exists — that is the coverage child. Do not enforce one-mapping-per-requirement or zero-evidence rejection. Do not handle waivers. Do not auto-restamp documents, infer proof from prose, fetch network state, or mark aspirational metrics complete. Status parsing lives in the scaffold child. Duplicate-id and stale-observation detection are a sibling child. Analyzer remains read-only.

DEPS: the spechonesty scaffold/status-parser child (provides the package and status parser). Sibling coverage and waiver children depend on this child's model.

description:
PROBLEM
A code-changing execute-bead attempt can bypass required staged hooks and still be accepted. Attempt 20260713T094206-53684645 for ddx-415c8b95 committed with git commit --no-verify after its pre-commit run was interrupted; DDx merged and closed it.

ROOT CAUSE WITH FILE:LINE
cli/internal/agent/execute_bead_validation.go:160-186 validates gate evidence only when GateRuns is non-empty, while cli/internal/agent/execute_bead.go:1507-1514 calls ValidateAttemptIntegrity without evidence. The validator therefore treats missing evidence as success and does not distinguish implementation-agent bypass commands from orchestrator-owned commits.

PROPOSED FIX
Make the attempt-integrity validator fail closed when a code-changing bead requires a staged lefthook run but meaningful successful evidence is absent. Reject implementation-agent commit commands that use --no-verify. Explicitly retain the scoped exception for DDx-owned checkpoint, tracker-only, landing, and durable-audit commits, which are outside implementation-agent evidence.

IN-SCOPE FILES
- cli/internal/agent/execute_bead_validation.go
- cli/internal/agent/execute_bead_validation_test.go

NON-SCOPE
Do not wire live harness evidence or change execute-bead prompts; ddx-03568f89 owns that integration. Do not rewrite existing execution history or forbid DDx-owned orchestration commits.

PARENT
ddx-9c3e703b.

DEPS
None.

description:
PROBLEM
When an execution agent cannot start its shell because the host temp root is exhausted, it can only return status: blocked plus prose. DDx then parks the bead indefinitely even after resource health recovers.

ROOT CAUSE WITH FILE:LINE
cli/internal/agent/try/no_changes.go:35-98 parses status, reason, suggested_action, and retry fields but has no machine-readable blocker kind. cli/internal/agent/try/no_changes.go:193-203 carries no typed blocker field in NoChangesOutcome. cli/internal/agent/execute_bead_loop.go:6605-6626 persists only ExternalBlockerReason. The execution prompt at cli/internal/agent/execute_bead.go:2046 documents blocked prose but no typed local-resource contract.

PROPOSED FIX
- Accept optional blocker_kind: local_resource_exhaustion only with status: blocked; reject unknown kinds and invalid status combinations.
- Carry the parsed kind through NoChangesOutcome and persist the typed marker defined by ddx-89ee92b8 in applyNoChangesBlockedExternal.
- Update the execution prompt so agents use the field only for host-local byte/inode/writability exhaustion, not test failures or missing dependencies.

IN-SCOPE FILES
- cli/internal/agent/try/no_changes.go
- cli/internal/agent/execute_bead_loop.go
- cli/internal/agent/execute_bead.go
- nearest focused *_test.go files

NON-SCOPE
- Do not parse ENOSPC from arbitrary reason prose.
- Do not perform the recovery probe or reopen beads.
- Do not classify provider, routing, or acceptance failures as local resources.

PARENT
- ddx-5958e8a4.

DEPS
- ddx-89ee92b8 supplies the typed marker schema.

Analyzer remains read-only.

Do not resolve runtime artifact paths or executable command allowlisting — sibling children own those checks.

acceptance:
1. TestCompleteVerificationCoverageCardinality_IgnoresFileOnlyCitations passes: a Complete fixture that cites only a test file path without a specific mapped target does not count that citation as requirement coverage, and the affected requirement is reported as uncovered.
2. TestCompleteVerificationCoverageCardinality_TargetedRowsCount passes: a Complete fixture whose mapping row names an exact Test* symbol, static check, or artifact target counts as coverage and yields no uncovered diagnostic for that requirement.
3. cd cli && go test ./tools/lint/spechonesty/... passes.
4. lefthook run pre-commit passes.
description:
PROBLEM
A Complete requirement can pass coverage cardinality by pointing at a whole test file in the Verification mapping instead of pinned proof. The coverage-cardinality pass must not treat a file-only citation as coverage, and an otherwise-Complete requirement covered only by such a citation must be reported as uncovered. At the same time, rows that name a concrete target must keep counting and must not regress into false-positive uncovered diagnostics.

ROOT CAUSE WITH FILE:LINE
The spechonesty analyzer package does not exist in this checkout: cli/tools/lint/spechonesty/analyzer.go:1 is absent, and cli/tools/lint/ currently contains only evidencelint, routinglint, and runtimelint. The sibling cardinality pass counts every mapping row as coverage because there is no integration point that consults the citation-granularity predicate when a row is joined to a requirement. The governing contract is docs/helix/06-iterate/phase2-doc-truth-plan-2026-07-13.md:67, which requires coverage by a Verification mapping row rather than an unspecific pointer.

PROPOSED FIX
Wire the citation-granularity predicate into the coverage-cardinality pass at the requirement-to-evidence join. A mapping row whose evidence field resolves to a test-file path without an exact mapped Test* symbol, static check, or artifact target does not count as coverage; a Complete requirement left with zero counting rows receives the sibling uncovered diagnostic. Rows naming concrete targets continue to count and produce no uncovered diagnostic for that requirement. Follow cli/tools/lint/evidencelint/analyzer.go and cli/tools/lint/evidencelint/analyzer_test.go conventions, including golang.org/x/tools/go/analysis and analysistest-style fixtures where applicable. The analyzer is read-only.

NON-SCOPE
Do not implement the ordering guarantee that the exclusion happens before the join or that duplicate/unrelated file-only rows cannot mask an uncovered requirement — that is the sibling child. Do not implement the zero-evidence empty-row-set diagnostic. Do not design the uncovered or duplicate cardinality diagnostic family beyond applying the file-only exclusion to the sibling cardinality pass. Do not handle waivers. Do not parse requirement inventories or mapping tables beyond consuming the mapping-parser child model. Do not implement status parsing. Do not auto-restamp documents, infer proof from prose, fetch network state, or mark aspirational metrics complete. Do not implement duplicate-id or stale-observation detection. Prose quality and AC numbering style are out of scope. Do not resolve whether named Test* symbols, static checks, or artifacts actually exist on disk; this child only relies on whether the row names a target at all. Do not enforce the executable verification command allowlist.

DEPS: parent ddx-6299445a and its ancestors ddx-29449fa5 and ddx-471d66b6; the spechonesty scaffold/status-parser child; the Verification mapping-parser child that provides the inventory + rows model; the sibling coverage-cardinality child; the child bead that adds the citation-granularity predicate. GOVERNING ARTIFACT: docs/helix/06-iterate/phase2-doc-truth-plan-2026-07-13.md WB-1 steps 3-4.

description:
PROBLEM
After the ddx-29491a0e preclaim decomposer returned on 2026-07-13, an interactive nested `codex --no-alt-screen` process (PID 607041, process group 607041) remained directly under the DDx worker until the operator terminated it. Preclaim providers can therefore leak CPU after successful fallback or other hook exits.

ROOT CAUSE WITH FILE:LINE
cli/internal/agent/execute_bead_loop.go:3108-3120 invokes PostAttemptDecompositionHook before claim without wrapping the hook in provider-descendant cleanup. Attempt-end descendant reaping in cli/internal/agent/execute_bead.go:1150-1163 is never reached because decomposition happens before an implementation attempt exists.

PROPOSED FIX
Establish a preclaim lifecycle process baseline immediately before invoking the decomposition hook and reap every provider descendant introduced by the hook on success, deterministic fallback, error, timeout, and cancellation. Preserve any provider process present in the pre-hook baseline and any process owned by another worker.

NON-SCOPE
Do not claim the parent before decomposition, change decomposition prompts or AC-map validation, change queue ordering, or make preclaim model work count as an implementation attempt. Do not kill provider processes that predate the hook baseline or belong to another worker.

PARENT
Split from root reliability regression bead: work: surface, bound, and reap preclaim decomposition lifecycle.

DEPS
ddx-aa6cc320 must land first so the internal/agent verification gate does not launch five real Codex providers.

1. Add or update a worker-manager shutdown regression so a live managed worker with descendant git/provider subprocesses is reaped through the existing worker shutdown path even when supervisor cancellation is slow.

description:
PROBLEM
Parent bead ddx-24949caf is too broad for one execution pass. This child owns part 2 of 3 of that parent scope.

ROOT CAUSE
PROBLEM: Restarting the DDx user service during active supervised work can hang until systemd times out, leaving systemd to SIGKILL server child processes. Live evidence from 2026-07-07 03:05:19 EDT: `ddx server stop` did not return until systemd marked `ddx-server.service` failed with `Result: timeout` and killed leftover git subprocesses, interrupting the Axon worker attempt that was in post-execution handling.

ROOT CAUSE WITH FILE:LINE: `cli/internal/server/server.go:379-385` cancels the supervisor and then waits on `supervisorDone` with no timeout. Worker cleanup is only reached afterward at `cli/internal/server/server.go:388-395`. The worker shutdown path itself has a bounded wait (`cli/internal/server/workers.go:1696-1703`), but it is unreachable while the supervisor goroutine is stuck in a reconcile/git operation. The installed systemd unit generated from `cli/cmd/server_service.go:26-42` has no explicit stop timeout or ExecStop mitigation, so the default systemd timeout eventually kills the whole cgroup.

PROPOSED FIX: Make server shutdown bounded and ordered so worker cleanup always runs promptly even when supervisor reconciliation is slow or stuck. A good implementation is to cancel the supervisor, wait only a short bounded grace for `supervisorDone`, continue to `supervisorRegistry.Shutdown()` / `workers.Shutdown()` on timeout, and surface/log the supervisor timeout without preventing worker cleanup.

NON-SCOPE: Do not rewrite worker execution semantics, change bead claim/lease policy, or alter unrelated service install behavior.

Parent: none. Dependencies: none.

PROPOSED FIX
Implement only this child acceptance slice:
- Add or update a worker-manager shutdown regression so a live managed worker with descendant git/provider subprocesses is reaped through the existing worker shutdown path even when supervisor cancellation is slow.
- `Server.Shutdown()` must not block indefinitely on `supervisorDone`; timeout behavior must return/log a useful error while continuing to close bead hub and stop land coordinators.

NON-SCOPE
Do not implement parent acceptance criteria assigned to sibling child beads. Preserve every parent non-scope constraint unless this child explicitly narrows it.

description:
PROBLEM
DDx still installs provider-binary PATH shims, exposes a hidden provider-launch wrapper, scans concrete harness process trees, and signals/reaps Fizeau-owned children. Fizeau v0.15 containment work is implemented upstream but not yet published or pinned, so DDx cannot yet delete the safety fallback. Without a dedicated consumer bead, publishing v0.15 would leave this forbidden boundary crossing in DDx indefinitely.

ROOT CAUSE WITH FILE:LINE
- cli/internal/agent/service_run.go:93-102,116-128,276-297 installs the provider shim and performs route-aware child cleanup around Fizeau Execute.
- cli/internal/agent/provider_spawn.go:13-56 and 100-179 defines the hidden wrapper contract and concrete provider binary shims.
- cli/cmd/provider_launch.go:12-70 plus provider_launch platform files exposes the direct provider exec boundary.
- cli/internal/agent/provider_children.go:21-40,92-240,242-478 discovers, classifies, signals, and reaps provider children using concrete route/harness facts.
- cli/internal/agent/orphan_harness_reaper.go:42-169 plus orphan_harness_reaper_linux.go:22-113 discovers and kills orphan harness processes.
- cli/internal/agent/execute_bead.go:1249-1258 and execute_bead_loop.go:1616-1618 retain attempt-end and liveness integration.
- cli/internal/agent/execution_cleanup_process.go:61-195 and cli/internal/server/workers_reap_unix.go:33-213 mix Fizeau-owned descendants into otherwise DDx-owned attempt/worker cleanup.
- Fizeau containment epic fizeau-c795e7d9 is closed, but release bead fizeau-b9a2037c must publish and prove cancellation/caller-death cleanup before DDx removes the fallback.

PROPOSED FIX
After pinning the compatible Fizeau release, add consumer conformance proving Execute cancellation and caller death terminate every wrapped harness/provider process tree. Delete the PATH shim, hidden provider-launch command/platform implementation, concrete provider binary list, provider-child/orphan-harness census and reapers, route-aware child liveness, attempt-end provider reap, and provider-descendant branches in generic cleanup. DDx retains only cancellation of the context supplied to Fizeau Execute and may supervise/reap DDx-owned worker, attempt, verification, and container processes. No concrete returned route fact may authorize a signal.

NON-SCOPE
Do not weaken DDx-owned worker/attempt/container cleanup, move bead/worktree/verification/landing ownership to Fizeau, parse terminal text, or implement the typed outcome adapter owned by ddx-66a8883f.

PARENT
ddx-b8cacbeb.

DEPS
fizeau#fizeau-b9a2037c publishes the process-tree containment contract and is the structured external blocker. fizeau#fizeau-c795e7d9 supplies the already-landed implementation.
notes: Fizeau v0.15 pin and public conformance are centralized in ddx-00d406ce; this consumer must not repin Fizeau independently.

description:
PROBLEM
Existing agent tests intentionally create corrupted Git configuration to prove execute-bead repair behavior, but those fixtures must never mutate the real repository running the tests. The two affected tests must keep their intended assertions while operating only inside dedicated fixture repositories.

ROOT CAUSE WITH FILE:LINE
cli/internal/agent/execute_bead_loop_stay_alive_test.go:1244-1286 deliberately sets `core.bare=true` in a script-harness fixture. cli/internal/agent/execute_bead_env_isolation_test.go:181-237 asserts a separate contamination case does not affect the primary checkout. The observed full-hook run of `go test -short -race ./internal/agent` nevertheless rewrote `/home/erik/Projects/ddx/.git/config` at 2026-07-17 09:41 with `core.bare=true` and test user values, which means these fixture paths can still reach shared config outside their intended sandbox.

PROPOSED FIX
Refactor TestExecuteBeadWorkerCannotMutatePrimaryGitConfig and TestWorkRepairsCoreBareAndContinuesSameCandidate setup to create and use dedicated temporary repositories/config scopes for all intentional Git corruption and repair assertions. Snapshot the invoking repository configuration before fixture execution where practical, assert the fixture repository still observes and repairs its own `core.bare=true` state, and make the tests fail during setup if they cannot prove they are targeting private fixture config.

NON-SCOPE
Do not weaken the existing core.bare/core.worktree repair behavior, remove execute-bead config isolation, alter user project Git configuration, or change DDx/Fizeau routing. This child only changes the existing core.bare repair/contamination fixtures and their focused assertions; stale index-lock recovery is ddx-3f156500 and main-git lock safety is ddx-1c8d9319. Parent bead: ddx-8b22914e. Deps: none; independent defect discovered while validating ddx-3f156500.

3. cd cli && go test ./internal/agent/... -run "Test(ExecuteBeadLoop_RepeatedBestEffortReadinessErrorsDoNotStopDrain|PreClaimWarnSameFingerprintEscalatesAfterThreshold)" -count=1 passes.

description:
PROBLEM
A DDx watch worker exits after five distinct beads when the best-effort readiness hook repeatedly returns system_unready, even though each failure is explicitly logged as continuing and the worker can still claim and execute beads. This converts an advisory Fizeau readiness outage into a queue-wide drain stop.

ROOT CAUSE WITH FILE:LINE
cli/internal/agent/execute_bead_loop.go:3010-3058 logs intakeErr as "check unavailable ... (continuing)" but passes it to appendPreClaimWarn. execute_bead_loop.go:1961-1984 makes the fifth matching warning set OperatorAttention and terminate Run. The observed watch run exited after ddx-029c1dde, ddx-744b0996, ddx-b0de0d36, and ddx-8c8675ba with preclaim_warn_repeated while all failures were non-blocking readiness-route JSON errors.

PROPOSED FIX
For fail-open best-effort readiness intake errors, retain durable warning/operator-attention observability but do not return Stop from watch/drain execution. Keep terminal behavior for claim-blocking readiness policy, project corruption, and other genuine safety stops. Add focused regression proof using a repeated intakeErr across more than DefaultPreClaimWarnRepeatThreshold beads that confirms the worker completes the available queue and records non-terminal attention.

NON-SCOPE
Do not change Fizeau routing, harness selection, failure-class vocabulary, readiness policy when configured blocking, or bead execution escalation.

description:
PROBLEM
Parent bead ddx-b291b0f6 is too broad for one execution pass. This child owns part 3 of 3 of that parent scope.

ROOT CAUSE
PROBLEM
The mandatory `cd cli && go test -short -race -timeout 30m ./internal/agent` gate recursively launches the package test binary as DDx's hidden provider wrapper. During attempt `20260713T190502-df5adc46`, the parent `agent.test` spawned five concurrent `agent.test __provider-launch <real-provider>` helpers for more than three minutes, grew a 666 MB testlog, and left a real `codex --no-alt-screen` process reparented to the managed worker for 12 minutes at about 188 MiB RSS. This makes the package gate itself create the CPU/memory/orphan condition it is supposed to prevent.

ROOT CAUSE WITH FILE:LINE
- `cli/internal/agent/agent_runner_service.go:102-113` calls `os.Executable()` unconditionally and passes that path to `EnsureProviderShimOnPATH`.
- `cli/internal/agent/service_run.go:152-163` repeats the same unconditional installation for the resolved-service path.
- `cli/internal/agent/provider_spawn.go:83-118` writes each shim as `<ddxBinary> __provider-launch <realBinary>`. Under `go test`, `os.Executable()` is `agent.test`, not the DDx CLI and it has no Cobra `__provider-launch` dispatch. Re-executing it starts the test suite again; the recursive process can install shims and launch real providers that escape the original gate process group.
- `cli/cmd/provider_launch.go:25-68` is the actual hidden-command implementation, and exists only in the DDx CLI command graph.

PROPOSED FIX
Introduce one injectable resolver for the provider-wrapper executable and use it from both service call sites. In package-test builds, install a suite-wide test resolver/guard that refuses to use the current `agent.test` executable as a provider wrapper while leaving direct `EnsureProviderShimOnPATH` tests free to supply an explicit real/fake DDx CLI binary. Fail closed with actionable evidence if a test fixture attempts to install a provider shim from a Go test binary. Preserve production PATH shim, `Pdeathsig`, process-group, and real CLI hidden-command behavior.

NON-SCOPE
- Do not remove provider parent-death protection in production.
- Do not replace Fizeau routing or provider discovery.
- Do not weaken the full `internal/agent` race gate or merely increase its timeout.
- Do not kill unrelated provider processes from other repositories.
- Scanner injection remains owned by `ddx-02200b1e`; fixture-specific spawn tripwires remain owned by `ddx-26bf19c7`.

PARENT AND DEPS
...[truncated]

PROPOSED FIX
Implement only this child acceptance slice:
- `cd cli && go test ./internal/agent -run "^(TestProviderShimExecutableResolver_RejectsGoTestBinary|TestRunAgentViaService_UsesProviderShimExecutableResolver|TestDispatchViaResolvedConfig_UsesProviderShimExecutableResolver|TestAgentPackageSuite_DoesNotExecTestBinaryAsProviderLauncher|TestExecutor_ProviderSpawnSetsPdeathsigAndSetpgid)$" -count=1 -timeout 120s` passes.
- `cd cli && go test -short -race -timeout 30m ./internal/agent` passes without any `agent.test __provider-launch` descendant, orphaned real provider, or recursive package-test process.
- `lefthook run pre-commit` passes.

NON-SCOPE
Do not implement parent acceptance criteria assigned to sibling child beads. Preserve every parent non-scope constraint unless this child explicitly narrows it.

description:
PROBLEM
When a bead attempt succeeds but landing is blocked (e.g. review malfunction), the worker preserves the result and marks the bead proposed for operator landing. The preserve ref (refs/ddx/iterations/<bead>/<ts>) and the result commit exist only in the clone that ran the attempt. An operator on any other machine sees the proposed bead and the result_rev in events but cannot fetch the commit: verified 2026-07-23 — 7 proposed beads (ddx-056e2ac1, ddx-66100211, ddx-89ee92b8, ddx-a111c9a8, ddx-a9e49b44, ddx-aadddb27, ddx-e1a4caa2) reference result revs absent from this clone, and 'git ls-remote origin refs/ddx/iterations/*' returns 0 refs.

ROOT CAUSE
The dangling-success preserve path records a local ref but never pushes it to origin. (Locate the preserve implementation via the dangling-success-preserved event emitter in cli/internal/agent; it writes preserve_ref=refs/ddx/iterations/... event bodies.)

PROPOSED FIX
After creating the local preserve ref, push it to origin (best-effort: log and continue on network failure, so offline attempts still preserve locally). Record push success/failure in the dangling-success-preserved event body so operators know whether the result is fetchable.

NON-SCOPE
Ref garbage collection policy; landing automation; changing the proposed/operator-attention lifecycle.

description:
PROBLEM
Once preclaim decomposition starts publishing resolving liveness, stale candidate state could make `ddx work status --json` report old bead IDs or phases after the hook exits. The existing loop.start structured event ordering must also remain stable so downstream execution telemetry does not regress.

ROOT CAUSE WITH FILE:LINE
cli/internal/agent/execute_bead_loop.go:1604-1617 defers liveness emission until claim, so there is currently no preclaim transient state lifecycle to clear. cli/internal/agent/execute_bead_loop.go:3108-3120 invokes PostAttemptDecompositionHook before claim, so adding liveness there can accidentally emit before the existing loop.start event unless the new lifecycle is sequenced explicitly.

PROPOSED FIX
Clear transient candidate resolving state on every preclaim decomposition exit, including success, deterministic fallback/error, timeout, and cancellation. Sequence the new preclaim liveness setup so the existing loop.start structured event remains the first structured event while still allowing resolving liveness before claim.

NON-SCOPE
Do not claim the parent before decomposition, change decomposition prompts or AC-map validation, change queue ordering, or make preclaim model work count as an implementation attempt. Do not kill provider processes that predate the hook baseline or belong to another worker.

PARENT
Split from root reliability regression bead: work: surface, bound, and reap preclaim decomposition lifecycle.

DEPS

2. TestExecutionCleanup_CancelStopsMeasurementAndRemoval cancels during measurement and during deletion and proves both phases return promptly without continuing background mutation.
3. TestWorkCleanup_DoesNotBlockClaimOnLargeScratchTree proves the worker reaches the next candidate after the cleanup budget expires and later passes resume safe reclamation.
4. Tests prove live, foreign non-test-owned, registered, fresh, and metadata-preserved scratch paths remain untouched across budget boundaries.

6. cd cli && go test ./internal/agent -run "Test(ExecutionCleanup_(BoundsLargeScratchTree|CancelStopsMeasurementAndRemoval)|WorkCleanup_DoesNotBlockClaimOnLargeScratchTree)$" -count=1 -timeout 60s passes.

description:
PROBLEM
A ddx work worker can spend minutes synchronously measuring and deleting one accumulated scratch tree before it claims useful work. During the 2026-07-13 niflheim incident, one cleanup pass performed hundreds of megabytes of physical reads; the same path timed out at both 120 seconds in isolation and 600 seconds in the full package gate. This creates unbounded CPU/I/O latency and makes queue progress inversely proportional to stale cache size.

ROOT CAUSE WITH FILE:LINE
cli/internal/agent/execute_bead_loop.go:1687 runs the execution cleanup pass on the claim path. cli/internal/agent/execution_cleanup.go:620-747 scans every matching scratch directory, calls measureTreeWithContext over an unbounded tree, and then calls os.RemoveAll, which walks the tree again and cannot observe context cancellation. cli/internal/agent/execution_cleanup.go:830-843 includes the shared cache parent and legacy process temp directory by default. A large stale directory therefore monopolizes the single queue worker with no per-pass item, inode, byte, or wall-clock budget.

PROPOSED FIX
- Put a deterministic wall-clock/work budget around scratch discovery, measurement, and reclamation on worker passes.
- Make cancellation effective during both measurement and deletion; do not enter an uninterruptible whole-tree RemoveAll after the budget expires.
- Persist or rediscover unfinished candidates safely so later passes continue reclamation without restarting an O(tree) measurement from zero.
- Return a non-fatal structured deferred-cleanup observation when the budget is exhausted, then allow candidate selection to proceed.
- Preserve liveness, ownership, registered-worktree, and minimum-age checks before any mutation.

IN-SCOPE FILES
- cli/internal/agent/execution_cleanup.go
- cli/internal/agent/execution_cleanup_loop.go
- cli/internal/agent/execute_bead_loop.go only as needed for the bounded pass contract
- focused cleanup tests

NON-SCOPE
Do not delete live worktrees, reduce the six-hour minimum age, disable cleanup, or treat cleanup deferral as bead failure.

PARENT
None; root production reliability regression.

DEPS
Depends on ddx-e6abf4a6 so the hermetic test boundary lands before production cleanup stress tests run.

description:
PROBLEM
Duplicate document ids (TD-040 class) and duplicate user-story ids across features (US-087/US-088 collision class) pass unnoticed, and a Complete document can cite a verification observation captured at a stale repository revision rather than the current one, so a checked-in assertion that a command once passed is treated as current proof.

ROOT CAUSE WITH FILE:LINE
The spechonesty analyzer at cli/tools/lint/spechonesty/analyzer.go (from the scaffold child) has no duplicate-id or observation-freshness logic. The contract is docs/helix/06-iterate/phase2-doc-truth-plan-2026-07-13.md WB-1 step 4 (current-revision observation) and step 6 (duplicate ids), scoped to features/ plus all five 02-design subdirectories.

PROPOSED FIX
Add two independent checks. (1) Duplicate-id detection: fail on duplicate document ids and on duplicate US-ids across features, scoping the scan to features/ plus the five 02-design subdirectories; these failures are never suppressible by a waiver. (2) Stale-observation detection: a Complete/Implemented Verification mapping row passes only when its recorded observation names the current repository revision with exit-zero; an observation keyed to a stale revision is a failure. Both checks are deterministic and read-only; the current revision and any fixture clock are injected so tests are hermetic (do not fetch network state).

NON-SCOPE
Do not auto-restamp documents, infer proof from prose, fetch network state, or mark aspirational metrics complete. Complete-coverage/waiver logic and status parsing live in sibling children. Prose quality and AC numbering style are out of scope.

The regression must reproduce the risky topology, prove the primary and linked worktree configs are byte-identical before and after the affected fixture path, and verify both checkouts still accept `git status --short`.

acceptance:
1. A parent/superseded bead with an unclosed blocking dependency is NOT auto-closed by the roll-up path; `cascadeAndWalkUp` skips it and the bead stays open. Covered by `TestRollUpClose_RefusesBeadWithOpenBlocksDep` in cli/internal/bead/store_test.go, reproducing the pqueue-842ac11f shape: bead A blocks-depends-on B (in_progress), a roll-up close is triggered, and the test asserts A is still open afterward.
2. The skip records an auditable note/event on the affected bead naming the open dep ID; asserted within `TestRollUpClose_RefusesBeadWithOpenBlocksDep`.
3. Roll-up still auto-closes eligible beads whose blocking deps are all closed (no regression to RC-2/RC-3 covered by existing TestClose_EpicAutoClose_* / TestClose_WalkUp_* / TestClose_SupersededCascade_Eligible); covered by new `TestRollUpClose_AllowsBeadWithClosedBlocksDep`.
4. `cd cli && go test ./internal/bead/... green`.
5. `lefthook run pre-commit` passes.
description:
PROBLEM: The 2026-07-06 pqueue incident: a server-managed worker performed a tracker-only roll-up close (no closing commit) on pqueue-842ac11f while it still carried an open 'blocks' dependency on pqueue-657e5f8d (in_progress). The programmatic auto-close paths do not validate dependency status, so a parent/superseded bead is auto-closed even when it has unmet blocking deps.

ROOT CAUSE: `Store.cascadeAndWalkUp` (cli/internal/bead/store.go:1661) runs auto-close paths that call `SetLifecycleStatus(..., StatusClosed, ...)` directly, bypassing dependency checks: (a) RC-2 cascade-close of superseded beads via `cascadeCloseSuperseeded` (store.go:1833), guarded only by `canCascadeCloseSuperseeded` (store.go:1867) which checks supersession/claim state but not deps; (b) RC-3 walk-up via `walkUpClosureCandidate` (store.go:1712) which auto-closes dead-intermediate (`execution-eligible==false`) and epic parents once children are terminal. Neither consults sibling dependency statuses. This is the exact path that produced the incident (tracker-only roll-up, no commit). Reconcile also closes programmatically at cli/internal/bead/reconcile.go:285 — out of scope here.

PROPOSED FIX: Depends on the sibling bead adding `ErrDependencyGateRejected` and `Store.UnclosedBlockingDeps(id)` (cli/internal/bead/errors.go, store.go). Before each auto-close `SetLifecycleStatus(x.ID, StatusClosed, ...)` in `cascadeCloseSuperseeded` (store.go:1833) and before the closed transition inside `walkUpClosureCandidate` (store.go:1712), call `s.UnclosedBlockingDeps(<candidateID>)`; if it returns a non-empty slice, SKIP that auto-close (leave the bead open), append an audit note/event naming the open dep IDs (mirroring `appendClosureRejectNote`, store.go:2079), and continue the walk without closing that node. The roll-up must not abort the whole operation — it selectively skips the ineligible bead. If the sibling primitive has not landed, add a minimal resolver inline at the roll-up call sites rather than duplicating the exported method.

NON-SCOPE: Do NOT change `Store.Close` / `Store.CloseWithEvidence` / `Store.UpdateWithLifecycleStatus` direct-close gating (sibling bead). Do NOT change claim paths (sibling bead). Do NOT change `Reconcile` (reconcile.go:285). Do NOT alter epic/dead-intermediate terminal-child counting beyond adding the dep-gate skip.

title: Enforce dependency-close gate in roll-up / cascade auto-close paths (cascadeAndWalkUp / walkUpClosureCandidate / cascadeCloseSuperseeded)
work-last-detail: session closed before Stop hook

acceptance:
1. `TestLifecycleDiscoveryContainment_PreservesConcurrentUnownedProvider` starts an unrelated provider after the pre-call snapshot while `ListModels` is active and proves it survives while the current call-owned probe is reaped.
2. `TestLifecycleDiscoveryContainment_BoundsBaselineAndCleanupScans` injects blocked baseline and cleanup enumeration and proves each returns within the configured containment budget with no `context.Background()` wait.
3. `TestLifecycleDiscoveryContainment_SurfacesCleanupFailure` proves scan, signal, and reap failures are returned or durably recorded instead of being silently treated as successful containment.
4. `TestLifecycleModelDiscovery_CancellationReapsPTYProbe` and `TestLifecycleModelDiscovery_ReturnDoesNotLeaveNoAltScreenChild` remain green for success, upstream error, timeout, and cancellation.
5. `cd cli && go test ./internal/agent ./cmd -run "^(TestLifecycleDiscoveryContainment_(PreservesConcurrentUnownedProvider|BoundsBaselineAndCleanupScans|SurfacesCleanupFailure)|TestLifecycleModelDiscovery_(CancellationReapsPTYProbe|ReturnDoesNotLeaveNoAltScreenChild))$" -count=1 -timeout 60s` passes.
6. `cd cli && go test ./cmd/... ./internal/agent/... -timeout 600s` passes.
7. `lefthook run pre-commit` passes.
description:
PROBLEM
Commit `020853315` added `ListModelsWithProbeContainment`, which fixes the immediate leaked-probe symptom but identifies ownership by taking a process-wide provider baseline and reaping every provider descendant that appears afterward. A concurrent legitimate provider started under the same worker after the baseline can therefore be killed as if it belonged to this discovery call. Both scans use `context.Background()`, each termination can wait independently, and cleanup scan/termination errors are discarded, so the containment path can itself wedge or report false success.

ROOT CAUSE WITH FILE:LINE
- `cli/internal/agent/model_discovery_containment.go:28-35` attributes all post-baseline provider descendants to one `ListModels` call without a call-owned process/session identity.
- `cli/internal/agent/model_discovery_containment.go:38-64` runs both baseline and cleanup through `context.Background()` and drops cleanup errors.
- `cli/internal/agent/provider_children_unix.go:18-58` enumerates the host through `ps` and flattens descendants without PPID, process-group, session, or launch-owner metadata needed to prove call ownership.

PROPOSED FIX
Use an exact call-owned provider/session handle from the Fizeau cancellation work in `ddx-a751a7b1` when available and remove the process-wide baseline sweep. If a local fallback is still required, retain ancestry/session/launch ownership, serialize ambiguous lifecycle discovery, bound baseline and cleanup enumeration with explicit deadlines, fail closed by preserving ambiguous processes, and surface cleanup failures in the returned error and execution evidence. Cleanup must never wait on `context.Background()` or kill a provider solely because it appeared after a PID snapshot.

NON-SCOPE
Do not disable model discovery, extend the caller timeout, kill manual provider sessions, kill active implementation harnesses or their fixtures, weaken attempt-end cleanup, or change route selection.

PARENT
`ddx-f84ee9a7` (Niflheim provider-test CPU incident).

DEPS
Related to `ddx-a751a7b1` for the preferred upstream call-owned cancellation handle and `ddx-44e89575` for provider ancestry ownership; no hard dependency so the bounded fail-closed fallback can land independently.

reason=> The Bash tool in this execution worker is non-functional due to host-level /tmp exhaustion: every invocation (including trivial commands like `true`, `echo hi`, `ls /tmp`, `df -h`) fails identically with: ENOSPC: no space left on device, mkdir '/tmp/claude-501/-Users-erik-Projects--ddx-exec-wt--execute-bead-wt-ddx-e1e229f5-20260713T155819-ab3d0d3d' This is the harness's own execution sandbox failing to create its scratch directory under /tmp on the host — not a condition inside this repo's worktree, and not something a code change in this bead's scope can fix. Confirmed with 4 consecutive retries over multiple minutes to rule out a one-off blip. This bead's acceptance criteria (AC5, AC6, AC7) all require running `go test` and `lefthook run pre-commit` via Bash. Without a working Bash tool, no test can be run, no git commit can be made, and no verification evidence can be produced. Read/Edit/Write tools remain functional, but making unverified code changes to concurrency-sensitive lifecycle/reaping logic (cli/internal/agent/model_discovery_containment.go, provider_children_unix.go) without being able to run the existing test suite or the new containment tests would violate the "do not commit red code" / "cross-reference each AC to concrete evidence" requirements in the execute-bead instructions. This is the third occurrence of this exact failure signature on this host across separate ddx execute-bead sessions (ddx-a751a7b1, ddx-34113f35, and now ddx-e1e229f5), all on different, unrelated beads. The host /tmp condition needs cleanup (or the harness's scratch-dir allocation needs to target a path with free space) before any worker on this host can execute a bead that requires Bash. This is an infrastructure/host blocker external to the DDx codebase itself, not something resolvable within this bead's scope.

description:
PROBLEM
There is no mechanical way to read a DDx document's status stamp, so downstream verification-coverage, duplicate-id, and stale-observation checks have nothing to build on. Status markers are heterogeneous: some docs use a body line `**Status:**` with free-text qualifiers, some use YAML frontmatter `status:`, and 40 of 56 design docs (including SD-013 and TD-027) have no status marker at all.

ROOT CAUSE WITH FILE:LINE
The package `cli/tools/lint/spechonesty/` does not exist. The intended pattern is the sibling analyzer at cli/tools/lint/evidencelint/analyzer.go with a CLI entrypoint at cli/tools/lint/evidencelint/cmd/evidencelint/main.go and testdata fixtures under cli/tools/lint/evidencelint/testdata/. The mechanical contract is defined in docs/helix/06-iterate/phase2-doc-truth-plan-2026-07-13.md under WB-1, steps 1-2.

PROPOSED FIX
Create `cli/tools/lint/spechonesty/` (analyzer.go, analyzer_test.go, cmd/spechonesty/main.go, testdata/ fixtures) modeled on evidencelint. Implement a status parser that (a) recognizes both encodings — a body `**Status:**` line and YAML frontmatter `status:` — and normalizes free-text qualifiers to a base status (e.g. `Complete`, `Implemented`, `Proposed`, `In Progress`, `Deferred`, `Aspirational`), and (b) treats a missing status on any SD/TD/ADR document as a lint failure requiring a stamp. This missing-status rule — not the Complete-check — is what catches SD-013 and TD-027. Parsing must be deterministic and read-only; the linter never mutates documents.

NON-SCOPE
Do not auto-restamp documents, infer proof from prose, fetch network state, or mark aspirational metrics complete. Do not implement verification-coverage, waiver, duplicate-id, or stale-observation logic here (later children). Prose quality and AC numbering style are out of scope.

PARENT: ddx-2e992616. DEPS: none — this child lands first as the package foundation; later children depend on it.

description:
<context-digest>
<principles>Spec-first development · Executable specifications · Audit trail required · Work is a DAG · Drift is debt · Inspect and adapt</principles>
<concerns>go-std | security-owasp | testing</concerns>
<practices>Go domain interface with contract tests against real implementations · project-scoped durable files · no call-recording mocks · go test + lefthook</practices>
<adrs>ADR-022 rev 6 requires one reconnecting coordination client, durable ordered offline journal, idempotency keys, and a cross-process offline project lock.</adrs>
<governing>FEAT-006 Worker Contract: connected mutations use the server; disconnected manual workers apply the same operations locally and reconcile before new online writes.</governing>
</context-digest>

PROBLEM
Disconnected/manual worker mutations have no durable append record API, so a process crash can lose sequence ordering, idempotency keys, payload hashes, preconditions, or outcomes required for later reconciliation before online writes.

ROOT CAUSE WITH FILE:LINE
cli/internal/agent/workerprobe/probe.go:129-224 buffers only workerprobe events in memory. cli/cmd/try.go:256-259 and cli/cmd/execute_loop_shared.go:280-282 construct local landing coordination directly, so no package-level production API records idempotency-keyed offline coordination mutations durably before local execution proceeds.

PROPOSED FIX
Add a project-scoped offline journal package under cli/internal/agent that can create/open a durable journal file, append mutation records with monotonic sequence numbers, idempotency key, payload hash, precondition, and outcome fields, and close/reopen without losing the next sequence number. Keep the API package-level and production-ready for later wiring.

NON-SCOPE
Do not add server routes, wire Cobra commands, centralize bead picking, or change process ownership. Do not implement the HTTP coordination client. Do not wire Cobra command flows to the journal in this bead beyond package-level production APIs and tests. Do not implement acknowledgement-through resume or compaction in this child.

PARENT
- ddx-635ae251.

DEPS
- No deps.

description:
PROBLEM
DDx consumers need proof that DDx can retain and pass Fizeau v0.15 portable runtime plans as opaque public values without reading, selecting, or reconstructing route details. Without a conformance test, downstream consumers may couple to concrete harness, provider, model, endpoint, or server-instance internals.

ROOT CAUSE WITH FILE:LINE
cli/go.mod:5-8 pins github.com/easel/fizeau v0.14.50 and cli/go.sum:88-89 locks that version. cli/internal/agent/service_run.go:196-216 builds public Execute requests and cli/internal/agent/service_run.go:283-367 consumes routing/final events without proving portable runtime planning can stay opaque to DDx. cli/internal/agent/serviceconfig.go:17-48 is the sole production Fizeau constructor seam and should not become a DDx route-selection or provider-discovery layer. docs/helix/06-iterate/phase1-lower-the-altitude-plan-2026-07-13.md:126-146 requires released public-boundary conformance before WB-1 consumers proceed.

PROPOSED FIX
After fizeau#fizeau-b9a2037c publishes immutable v0.15.0, ensure cli/go.mod and cli/go.sum use github.com/easel/fizeau v0.15.0 exactly if a sibling child has not already landed that pin. Add cli/internal/agent/fizeau_v015_portable_plan_contract_test.go using only exported Fizeau APIs. Prove DDx can retain/pass the public portable runtime plan as an opaque value without selecting or reconstructing harness, provider, model, endpoint, or server instance.

NON-SCOPE
Do not implement DDx retry, escalation, close, or review policy; adopt Docker portable runtime; delete DDx cleanup shims; add route catalogs or provider probes; select a concrete harness/model/provider; or use Fizeau cost, billing, or route evidence as an execution-policy input. Downstream beads own production consumers after this prerequisite closes. Do not add terminal-cost or cancellation conformance beyond what is necessary for compilation.

PARENT
ddx-b8cacbeb.

GOVERNING ARTIFACT
docs/helix/06-iterate/phase1-lower-the-altitude-plan-2026-07-13.md:126-146 and adr:ADR-024.

DEPS
External blocker fizeau#fizeau-b9a2037c must publish v0.15.0 with public typed terminal fields, absent/zero/positive cost presence, wrapped-process-tree containment, and opaque route-neutral portable runtime planning.

1. TestCompleteVerificationResolvesExistingRuntimeArtifact passes: a Complete fixture mapping a requirement to an existing inspectable runtime artifact passes artifact resolution and emits no missing-artifact diagnostic.
2. TestImplementedVerificationResolvesExistingRuntimeArtifact passes: an Implemented fixture mapping a requirement to an existing inspectable runtime artifact passes artifact resolution and emits no missing-artifact diagnostic.

description:
PROBLEM
Complete/Implemented documents can claim verification with a Verification mapping row whose evidence target is an inspectable runtime artifact path, but the analyzer currently has no positive-path runtime-artifact existence check. Without the pass case, later missing-artifact diagnostics can regress by warning on valid current-revision artifacts.

ROOT CAUSE WITH FILE:LINE
The spechonesty analyzer path is absent in this checkout at cli/tools/lint/spechonesty/analyzer.go:1, and the analyzer run has no runtime-artifact existence check over parsed Verification rows. The governing contract is docs/helix/06-iterate/phase2-doc-truth-plan-2026-07-13.md:67, requiring every Complete/Implemented mapping row to name an exact evidence target, and docs/helix/06-iterate/phase2-doc-truth-plan-2026-07-13.md:68, requiring rejection of mappings to nonexistent artifacts. Current-revision executable verification is reinforced at docs/helix/06-iterate/phase2-doc-truth-plan-2026-07-13.md:176.

PROPOSED FIX
Wire the runtime artifact target resolver into the spechonesty analyzer run for Complete/Implemented Verification mapping rows classified as inspectable runtime artifact targets. Add the no-diagnostic path first: when the resolver finds the mapped artifact in the current checkout, artifact validation must emit no diagnostic for that row. Keep the analyzer read-only.

NON-SCOPE
Do not implement the missing-artifact diagnostic body beyond whatever structure is required to avoid false positives for existing artifacts. Do not reimplement target classification or path resolution — consume the resolver child. Do not handle waivers — that is the waiver child. Do not parse requirement inventories or mapping tables — that is the mapping-parser child. Do not auto-restamp documents, infer proof from prose, fetch network state, or mark aspirational metrics complete. Status parsing lives in the scaffold child. Duplicate-id and stale-observation detection are a sibling child. Prose quality and AC numbering style are out of scope. Do not enforce requirement coverage cardinality or duplicate mapping counts — the coverage-cardinality child owns that. Do not resolve Go Test* symbols or static check names — the evidence-target child owns those checks. Do not enforce command allowlisting — the verification-command allowlist child owns that.

DEPS: parent ddx-e743ce67; grandparent ddx-29449fa5; root dependency ddx-471d66b6; the spechonesty scaffold/status-parser child; the Verification mapping-parser child that provides the inventory + rows model; the runtime artifact target resolver child. GOVERNING ARTIFACT: docs/helix/06-iterate/phase2-doc-truth-plan-2026-07-13.md WB-1 steps 3-4.

description:
PROBLEM
The normal internal/agent unit-test gate reads and deletes host-global DDx scratch trees. On 2026-07-13, TestWorkCleanup_RunsAfterSetupFailureBeforeNextClaim drove about 431 MB of physical reads, timed out after 120 seconds in isolation, and caused the required 600-second package gate to time out. This makes test duration depend on accumulated host cache state and adds substantial I/O/CPU pressure while ddx work is trying to drain the queue.

ROOT CAUSE WITH FILE:LINE
cli/internal/agent/execute_bead_loop_cleanup_test.go:269-288 creates a production NewExecutionCleanupManager for t.TempDir but does not override TempRoot or ScratchRoots. cli/internal/agent/execution_cleanup.go:830-843 therefore derives the shared cache parent and legacy process temp directory. Cleanup reaches cli/internal/agent/execution_cleanup.go:620-747, where it recursively measures and removes every old matching scratch directory. The timeout stack was in measureTreeWithContext from cleanupScratchRoots, not in the predispatch fixture under test.

PROPOSED FIX
- Give every execution-cleanup unit fixture an explicit hermetic TempRoot and ScratchRoots beneath its own t.TempDir before calling Cleanup.
- Add a shared test helper if needed so future fixtures cannot silently fall back to ~/.cache/ddx or the process temp root.
- Add a sentinel/tripwire proving the loop-cleanup test cannot enumerate, measure, or remove a scratch root outside its fixture root.
- Audit adjacent NewExecutionCleanupManager test call sites reached by ./internal/agent and apply the same boundary where they invoke Cleanup.

IN-SCOPE FILES
- cli/internal/agent/execute_bead_loop_cleanup_test.go
- cli/internal/agent/execution_cleanup_test.go and nearest cleanup test helpers as required

NON-SCOPE
Do not weaken production cleanup, change retention policy, or skip cleanup assertions. Production cleanup latency is tracked separately.

PARENT
None; root gate-reliability regression.

DEPS
None.
